source: The owner console's actual UI implementation — the largest single body
title: Type scale bypassed by literal px 244 times against 38 token references, 78 of them at 12.5px (a size the 16-token scale does not contain), and 6 sites ship below the documented 11px floor
why: DESIGN.md:366 states the 11px Floor Rule: 'No --t-* pixel token drops below 11px, and tokens.test.ts asserts both that floor and the exact count of type tokens (16), so a new size has to be looked at rather than added quietly.' The rule binds tokens; the console writes the number into the className and clears both the floor and the count without a test noticing. Across the 23 files: 244 literal font-size classes against 38 spelling a token. Largest is text-[12.5px] x78 across 17 files (owner-clients.tsx alone has 22: :332, :338, :386) — 12.5px is on no scale in the repo, and the console's body is 13.5px (console.css:469 sets --t-body: 13.5px under [data-shell-role=admin] with the comment '--t-body is the token every atomic writes through'). Then text-[13px] x45 (the coach body size shipped onto a 13.5px console), text-[11.5px] x36 (= --t-mono-crumb), text-[12px] x32 (= --t-mono-meta and --t-badge), text-[11px] x19 (= --t-label and --t-over). Six sites go under the floor at text-[10.5px], three in the shipped audit feed at admin-audit-log.tsx:730, :737, :749 — and all three are applied to MonoMeta, the atomic whose entire job is to spend --t-mono-meta (12px), overridden downward at the call site to a fourth mono size that is neither the token (12), the badge (10, pinned by overline-size.test.ts) nor the overline (9.5). DESIGN.md's floor carve-out covers only 'the 9.5px overline and 10px badge... on a mono face at wide tracking'; :737 is a truncating scope column of prose, not an overline.
fix: Guard it the way overline-size.test.ts guards the overline: a test over src/components/workspace/**/*.tsx rejecting text-[Npx] below 11 or equal to an existing --t-* value. Then resolve 12.5px — either admit it to the scale as a real console sub-body role with a reason (console.css:432, _primitives.tsx:244 and atomics/type.tsx:52 all already draw it) and let tokens.test.ts's count move deliberately, or fold the 78 sites onto --t-mono-crumb / --t-badge. Replace the three 10.5px MonoMeta overrides with the token the atomic already carries.

source: The owner console's actual UI implementation — the largest single body
tell: self-inconsistency (surface ignores the scale authored for it)
title: The console's own density/rhythm scale is authored, commented and test-pinned, and the console spends none of it, writing 227 off-grid px literals instead
why: tokens.css:288-294 declares --d-stack-gap 12 / --d-head-gap 20 / --d-section-gap 32 (plus --d-card-p 16, --d-page-x 24) because a template that separates crumb, title, stat strip and table by one repeated 16px 'reads as a single undifferentiated stack, which is the other half of why the console reads flat', and closes: 'Each step aliases a --s-* rung so the rhythm cannot drift off the 4px grid.' tokens.test.ts:204-212 pins those aliases and its comment names the exact failure: 'a raw pixel value here is how a rhythm quietly drifts off the grid one screen at a time.' Measured consumption across the 23 console screens: --d-head-gap 0 sites (its only appearance in src is the test that pins it), --d-page-x 0 sites repo-wide, --d-card-p 0 sites (2 consumers, both generic kit: data-state.tsx:181, callout.tsx:48), --d-section-gap 0 sites (3 consumers, all kit templates), --d-stack-gap exactly 1 — admin-audit-log.tsx:1628, inside the dead AdminAuditLog component (pattern 2). In their place the 23 files carry 707 spacing declarations: only 274 reach a --s-*/--d-* token, 206 are literals respelling an existing rung, and 227 land off the 4px grid across 18 distinct off-rung values (1,2,3,5,6,7,9,10,11,13,14,15,18,22,28,36,56,60px). Heaviest: px-[14px] x27, gap-2.5 x15, py-[10px] x13, px-[18px] x13, gap-[10px] x12, gap-[13px] x9, gap-[14px] x9. admin-overview.tsx:1420-1479 stacks the whole Overview body on gap-[13px], a number on no scale in the repo. The guard was aimed at tokens.css; the drift happened in markup, so it passes green.
fix: Add a vitest guard over src/components/workspace/**/*.tsx (same shape as token-references.test.ts) rejecting arbitrary spacing utilities whose px value is not an --s-* rung, and Tailwind's .5 rungs with them. Then sweep: 13/14px gaps to --s-3/--s-4, 10px to --s-2/--s-3, and the four page rhythms onto --d-stack-gap / --d-head-gap / --d-section-gap / --d-card-p, which is what those tokens were written for.

source: There is dead CSS and there are orphaned assets, inside a hard budget
tell: self-inconsistency — the guard measures line count, so dead code is charged to the budget as if it were design
title: About 190 lines of provably unreachable CSS sit inside the 3,100-line cap that was raised by 100 today because the two sheets "stood at 2,999" and a four-token fix "could not land at all without moving the number"
why: The budget test counts lines, never reachability, so it cannot distinguish a considered rule from an inert one — and every scope that has audited these sheets counted the same lines as evidence of a considered system. The arithmetic: globals.css is 1,947 lines and tokens.css 1,129, total 3,076 against a `toBeLessThan(3_100)` cap, leaving 23 lines of headroom. The dead total in those same two files is roughly 190 — 120 in globals.css (88 for the four ghost surfaces, 24 reduced-motion overrides of unread tokens, 3 for the --text-nav trio, 4 for --trace-edge/--trace-dot/--agent-red-line/--agent-blue-body at 262-274, 1 for the never-worn `.is-open` alternate at 170) and 70 in tokens.css (37 unread motion tokens, 11 dead type-role and icon rules, 20 palette-role declarations, plus --d-page-x at 285 and --d-head-gap at 293). That is more than eight times the remaining headroom, and nearly twice the 100 lines someone had to argue for in a comment on 2026-09-04 — a comment that is emphatic the 100 "buys the fork and its comments and nothing else; it is not headroom for a new surface." The same file, twenty lines earlier, records the repo already finding and deleting a 2,620-line unimported stylesheet on 2026-09-01, so the failure mode is not unknown here — it is documented, dated, and unguarded against.
fix: Land the deletions in the other patterns first; that returns roughly 190 lines to the two budgeted sheets and puts them near 2,886, back under the original 3,000 with real room. Then either revert APP_CSS_BUDGET to 3,000 (the raise stops being needed) or, better, make the guard measure the thing it cares about: add a reachability assertion alongside the line count — every class selector in the app stylesheets must appear as a class token in some .ts/.tsx, with an explicit allowlist for library-emitted classes (.react-flow, .react-flow__pane, .react-flow__edge-path) and template-constructed BEM modifiers.

source: Orphaned dead CSS — named in the audit brief as a tell-adjacent axis,
title: css-budget.test.ts caps these sheets by line count and its header records raising the cap for want of 1 line — 129 of the 3,076 capped lines are dead
why: The budget applies to top-level src/app/*.css only, which is exactly globals.css (1,947) + tokens.css (1,129) = 3,076 against `toBeLessThan(3_100)` — 23 lines of headroom. Dead weight inside that 3,076: tokens.css contributes 47 lines (2 icon variants at :995-996, 7 unused .t-* recipes at :1002-1014, .t-hero at :1109, 37 unread motion tokens across :299-397); globals.css contributes 82 lines (15 loading-*, 12 .admin-version, 19 .trace-blueprint, 12 @keyframes kit-toast-in, 24 dead motion re-declarations in the reduced-motion block). 129 lines, 4.2% of the cap, and 5.6x the headroom that remains. The header makes this consequential rather than cosmetic: the cap was raised twice, and the second raise (:10-15, 2026-09-04) says the sheets 'stood at 2,999 against the 3,000 cap, so a fix that forks four tokens per palette block and explains why could not land at all without moving the number', and that the 100 'is not headroom for a new surface'. Deleting the 129 dead lines lands the pair at 2,947 — under the 3,000 that had to be moved, with 52 lines to spare. A line-count budget that is being paid by dead rules is measuring the wrong thing, and the deferred list makes it worse: coach.css spends 8 more lines at :1677 and :1682 overriding classes tokens.css declares and nothing uses, and src/components/agent-flow.module.css's 71 fully dead lines are neither charged to the budget nor printed by the diagnostics test, so nothing in CI can see them.
fix: Remove the 129 dead lines (patterns above), then either lower APP_CSS_BUDGET back toward 3,000 with a note that the raise was repaid, or replace the line-count assertion with one that cannot be paid by dead rules — e.g. assert that every class selector declared in the two sheets has at least one reference in src/**/*.tsx or design/coach/*.dc.html, which is the property the budget is a proxy for. Add src/components/*.css and src/components/*.module.css to DEFERRED_STYLESHEETS so an unimported module sheet is at least printed, the way onboarding.css was only caught by hand.

source: src/lib was in no scope, yet it is a presentation layer: it holds the
tell: accessible name printed as visible copy
title: The audit log's action filter prints the screen-reader name as body text, doubling all 102 labels
why: audit/actions.ts gives every action two strings for two channels: `microcopy` is the visible words and `ariaLabel` is the accessible name that REPLACES them for assistive tech. src/components uses them exactly that way -- go-live-step.tsx:111 puts ariaLabel on aria-label and :115 renders microcopy; calendar-step.tsx:340/344, :403/407 and :522/526 repeat the pattern. src/lib/copy/audit-labels.ts:5 instead concatenates them: `${action.microcopy}: ${action.ariaLabel}`. admin-audit-log.tsx:138 makes that string the label of all 102 AUDIT_ACTION_FILTER_OPTIONS, and :969 makes it the active-filter chip. So the filter dropdown reads 'Booking logged: Booking recorded in the audit log', 'Publish logged: Brain publish recorded in the audit log', 'Attendance logged: Attendance action recorded in the audit log' -- the same fact stated twice with a colon, and the phrase 'in the audit log' repeated 102 times inside a control that is already the audit log's own filter. The accessible name exists precisely because it duplicates the visible one; printing both is the mechanical join no designer chose. audit-labels.test.ts:10-11 asserts the label contains BOTH fields, so the test pins the defect in place rather than catching it.
fix: Return `AUDIT_ACTIONS[key].microcopy` from auditActionLabel and let admin-audit-log.tsx pass `ariaLabel` through as the option's aria-label, matching go-live-step.tsx:111/115. Update audit-labels.test.ts:10-11 to assert the label equals microcopy and does NOT contain ariaLabel.

source: There is dead CSS and there are orphaned assets, inside a hard budget
tell: orphaned dead code — surfaces styled in full and never built
title: Four complete features exist only as CSS: a nine-class loading skeleton, an admin version switcher, a blueprint underlay, and a toast keyframe the comment beneath it explains can never fire
why: Each of these is a finished, internally coherent block — the loading skeleton has a 47%/53% two-pane grid, a --wide message variant, a composer, a trace pane and a receipt, plus a shimmer engine and responsive overrides at three breakpoints — and not one line of it can ever paint. Verified: `.loading-topbar`, `.loading-panels`, `.loading-heading`, `.loading-message`, `.loading-message--wide`, `.loading-composer`, `.loading-trace`, `.loading-receipt`, `.agent-loading` and `.skeleton` return zero string-literal matches across every .ts/.tsx in src/. The real loading route is src/app/meet-agent/loading.tsx, one line re-exporting @/components/kit/skeleton, which draws Tailwind arbitrary utilities and `data-slot` attributes and never writes a bare class. `.skeleton::after` (1467) reads `--agent-loading-sheen`, declared only on `.agent-loading` (1453) — a chain that resolves to nothing at both ends. `.admin-version` (467, 1747, 1752, including a 44px touch-target override) and `.trace-blueprint` (1029, 1038-1039, 1046, a full SVG path/circle treatment with a dashed last circle) have zero consumers. `@keyframes kit-toast-in` (1556) is the sharpest: the very next comment at 1569 explains that sonner owns the toast's transform and opacity, so "what is left unclaimed is `filter`" — the keyframe animates transform and opacity, which is exactly what the repo decided it must not do, and it was left in anyway. The tell is not that these are unused; it is that they are complete. A person building a feature leaves a stub; a generator leaves a finished stylesheet for a screen nobody wrote. Dead rules also actively mislead — an author reading globals.css:1476 reasonably concludes the agent surface has a loading skeleton and styles against it.
fix: Delete globals.css 1451-1484 (the .agent-loading token block, .skeleton, .skeleton::after and all nine .loading-* rules), the `.loading-panels` member of the group selector at 1492, the .loading-panels rule at 1500-1503, the two .loading-panels rules at 1843-1844, and `.agent-loading` from the group selector at 238. Delete .admin-version at 467-470 and 1747-1755. Delete .trace-blueprint at 1029-1049. Delete @keyframes kit-toast-in with its comment at 1555-1567. Then delete --toast-distance and --toast-scale from tokens.css if kit-toast-in was their only reader. 88 lines, no markup change.

source: Disabled and inactive states are drawn by fading the element, at three
tell: tell 14 (one fade standing in for two different meanings)
title: Pending is drawn as disabled: 29 of the 31 files that disable a control during an in-flight operation show no busy indicator
why: 87 `disabled={...pending|busy|sending|saving|submitting}` bindings across 31 files, and only 2 of those files contain any spinner - the whole repo has 5 animate-spin/<Spinner> occurrences (account-security-settings.tsx:850,1120; connect-channel-sheet.tsx:488,509; ui/sonner.tsx:29). So for 29 files the ONLY feedback that a request is in flight is the same opacity fade that means 'you may not do this', drawn with the same multiplier. meet-agent.tsx:604 is exact: disabled={sending || !draft.trim()} with one disabled:opacity-60 covering both meanings, so 'sending your message' and 'your message is empty' are byte-identical pixels. aria-busy is applied at 20 places, which is the correct semantic half - screen readers are told the difference and sighted users are not. And the loading vocabulary forks a fourth way: two unrelated skeletons (ui/skeleton.tsx:7 animate-pulse bg-muted vs kit/skeleton.tsx:14-16 animate-none plus a 1.6s shimmer), one motion-safe:animate-pulse dot (kit/transcript.tsx:421), one animate-pulse badge (kit/step-journey.tsx:178). Spinner, pulse, shimmer, and bare fade are four answers to one question.
fix: Give the two button bases (ui/button.tsx:13, kit/atomics/button-class.ts:73) a data-busy branch that keeps the face at full opacity and swaps the label for a spinner or a verb ('Sending...'), wired to the aria-busy the callers already pass. Reserve the fade for the genuinely-inert case, so the two states stop sharing pixels.

source: Entire product surfaces cite pixel authority that was never drawn — th
tell: fabricated pixel authority (citation to a source that does not exist)
title: 79 citations name artboards that were never drawn; five product surfaces totalling 33 shipping routes have zero pixel authority
why: This is the half of the 143/317 aggregate that actually indicts the repo, and it is categorically different from rename rot. design/coach/canvas.json declares exactly 22 artboards on 3 pages and every one is a coach surface; nothing named Admin*, Landing, Login, Affiliate, Consumer*, MeetYourAgent, InboxEmpty or EyeRule exists in either the manifest or the directory. Yet 79 citations point at them, by filename and often by line number. Breakdown: the Admin* family 36 (AdminClients 8, AdminOverview 5, AdminSupportTeam/AdminRevenue/AdminProvisioning/AdminImpersonation 3 each, AdminSystem/AdminRequests/AdminMoneyRefused 2 each, AdminPlans/AdminInbox/AdminClientDetail/AdminAgentPerformance/AdminAffiliates 1 each), MeetYourAgent 17, the Consumer family 7, Login 4, Affiliate 4, Landing 3, InboxEmpty 3, EyeRule 2, CoachPlanChange 2, Redesign 1. The surfaces these dress are the 25-route admin console, 2 affiliate routes, 1 consumer route, 4 auth routes and the landing page — 33 shipping routes with no drawing behind them anywhere in the repo. docs/REDESIGN-CANVAS.md:3 shows why: a first canvas ('55 artboards, coverage complete', 2026-09-01) existed only as a published artifact with no working files, and its coverage list at :82-91 promises 'Owner console (25)', 'Affiliate and lead (6)' and 'Signup and onboarding (6)'. The 2026-09-04 canvas that shipped files (:189, 'Twenty-two artboards on three pages') is coach-only. So a value presented as 'from AdminRevenue.dc.html:266' cannot be checked by anyone, ever, and the repo's whole defence — that its numbers came from a canvas — does not extend to a third of its routes. landing-page.tsx:10 is the most naked form: '`Landing.dc.html` on the redesign canvas is the authority for every word and every measurement here.'
fix: Mark every class-B citation as unresolvable rather than deleting it: replace `AdminRevenue.dc.html:266` with a form that states the provenance honestly, e.g. `(2026-09-01 artifact canvas, no working file in repo — unverifiable)`. Then, for each of the five surfaces, either export the artboards from the published artifact into design/ so the citations resolve, or demote the comments from 'traced from' to 'chosen because', which is what actually happened. A one-line grep guard in the existing test suite (every `*.dc.html` token in src/ must name a file in design/coach/) stops the class from growing.

source: There is dead CSS and there are orphaned assets, inside a hard budget
tell: orphaned dead code — an unimported stylesheet, the exact defect the repo already documented and deleted once
title: src/components/agent-flow.module.css is 71 lines imported by nothing, and its comment asserts the opposite cursor decision from the live rule in globals.css
why: Grepping every CSS import across src/ finds exactly six: coach.css, meet-your-agent.css, meet-your-agent.module.css, consumer.css, console.css, coach.css again, tokens.css and globals.css. `agent-flow.module.css` is in none of them, and the string "agent-flow.module" appears nowhere in src/, e2e/, evals/, scripts/ or docs/. agent-flow.tsx — the only file it could belong to — imports @xyflow/react and motion/react and no stylesheet at all. So its four `.node[data-status=...]::after` halo rules, its `@keyframes haloPulse`, its three `.pulse` fills and its own prefers-reduced-motion block have never rendered. This is character-for-character the defect css-budget.test.ts:18-27 records finding and deleting on 2026-09-01: "`onboarding/onboarding.css` ... was 2,620 lines defining a complete second palette ... and it was imported by nothing: `grep` for a `.css` import across `src/app` and `src/components` did not name it." The same grep, run against src/components today, still does not name this file. Worse, the two sheets disagree in writing: agent-flow.module.css:47 says "Panning and zooming are disabled so the graph stays composed; don't offer a grab cursor the canvas won't honour" and sets `cursor: default`, while the reachable globals.css:1056-1062 sets `cursor: grab` and `cursor: grabbing`. Two stylesheets state opposite decisions about the same element and only one of them is wired up — nobody reconciled them because nobody could see the second one was inert.
fix: Delete src/components/agent-flow.module.css. Before deleting, decide the cursor question once: if panning really is disabled, move `cursor: default` into globals.css:1056 and drop the `:active` grabbing rule at 1060-1062; if it is not, the module's premise was already wrong. Then extend css-budget.test.ts (or token-references.test.ts) with an assertion that every .css and .module.css under src/ is named by an import, so the onboarding.css precedent cannot recur a third time.

source: There is dead CSS and there are orphaned assets, inside a hard budget
tell: imported wholesale rather than derived — a vendored token library, 43% of it never spent
title: 37 of the 87 motion tokens copied verbatim from an external skill file are read by nothing, and globals.css spends 24 more lines collapsing tokens no element reads
why: tokens.css:298 labels the block "Motion tokens, copied from .agents/skills/transitions-dev/_root.css" — an admission that this is an import, not a decision. Resolving every `var(--x)` and Tailwind arbitrary `(--x)`/`[--x]` in src/ against the 87 declarations in lines 297-402 leaves 37 with no reader: --duration-micro, --duration-medium, --duration-very-slow, --ease-linear, --ease-bounce, --ease-bounce-strong, --distance-medium, --distance-large, --scale-large/-medium/-tiny, --blur-medium, --blur-large, --panel-translate-y/-blur/-ease, --pulse-dur/-count/-min, --tabs-ease, --tt-delay, --acc-expand/-collapse/-chevron/-ease, --toggle-dur/-travel/-ov1/-ov2/-track/-ease, --check-delay, --check-uncheck, --text-swap-dur/-translate-y/-blur/-ease. Whole named components — the accordion (4 tokens), the toggle (6), the text-state swap (4) — are specified to the millisecond and animate nothing. The cost compounds: globals.css's reduced-motion block, itself justified as a CLAUDE.md hard rule, spends 24 of its 65 override lines zeroing tokens nothing reads (1858, 1861, 1863, 1878, 1883-1886, 1889-1890, 1893-1894, 1909-1910, 1912, 1914-1915, 1917-1918, 1920, 1930-1931, 1933, 1936), and one of them carries a hand-written justification — 1914's `--toggle-travel: 16px; /* the thumb still has to reach the other end; only the time is gone */` — reasoning carefully about a thumb that does not exist. source: Focus indicators were not in any of the 20 scopes, and there are at le
tell: one indicator, fifteen spellings — boilerplate accreted rather than a decision applied
title: Fifteen mutually independent implementations of a focus ring the design doc defines exactly once
why: docs/DESIGN.md:465-467 states the rule in one sentence: "Focus is `2px solid var(--focus-ring)` at `outline-offset: 2px`, applied globally on `:focus-visible` — never a border-colour change alone." tokens.css:976 implements exactly that. Then 52 other sites implement something else. The census: (1) the global at tokens.css:976; (2) the documented FieldShell fork, tokens.css:983-987; (3) shadcn `focus-visible:border-ring + ring-3 + ring-ring/50`, 10 sites (button:13, input:12, textarea:10, checkbox:16, switch:19, select:359, accordion:37, field:109, input-group:17, kit/date-field.tsx:88); (4) the identical thing spelled `ring-[3px]`, 4 sites (tabs:102, toggle:9, badge:8, scroll-area:21) — Tailwind v4 emits byte-identical CSS for `ring-3` and `ring-[3px]`, so this is two spellings of one number and nothing else; (5) tabs:102 and scroll-area:21 stack a third layer, `focus-visible:outline-1`; (6) hand-rolled `outline-2 + outline-[var(--focus-ring)]`, 11 sites (app-sidebar:602,765; kanban-card:148; kanban-board:577; admin-help:154,251,359; notification-bell:189; optin-artifact:89; transcript:390; data-table:950); (7) hand-rolled `ring-N + ring-[var(--focus-ring)]`, 6 sites (app-sidebar:255,541; persona-switcher:44; kanban-board:541; admin-money-affiliates:480; date-field:88); (8) an arbitrary-property outline computed off the spacing scale, `focus-visible:[outline:calc(var(--s-1)/2)_solid_var(--focus-ring)]`, filter-bar:438,505 — 4px/2 to say 2px; (9) globals.css:334-336 .agent-shell on an alias token; (10) globals.css:1367-1369 .share-field as a box-shadow; (11) consumer.css:120-122 .consumer-shell; (12) globals.css:94 universal `outline-ring/50`; (13) view-switch.tsx:62 `focus-visible:rounded-[var(--r-control)]`; (14) coach.css:1423 reusing --focus-ring for a drag drop-target; (15) the documented FieldShell tint. Offsets alone come in three values (0, 1px, 2px) and widths in four (1px, 2px, 3px, 4px-as-calc). The design canvas is silent: all 22 design/coach/*.dc.html declare --focus-ring at line 40 and not one draws a focus state, so none of these fourteen alternatives was extracted from the pixel authority. This is the single design value in the repo with the most spellings and the least authorship.
fix: Delete the focus half from every consumer. The unlayered tokens.css:976 rule already paints on all of them (see the doubling pattern), so removing `focus-visible:border-ring`, `focus-visible:ring-*`, `focus-visible:outline-*` and the two filter-bar calc-outlines is a no-op on 40 of the 44 .tsx sites and a fix on the rest. Keep exactly two exceptions, both already documented: the FieldShell pair at tokens.css:983-987 and its tint at atomics/field.tsx. Then extend focus-ring.test.ts to fail on any new `focus-visible:` indicator utility outside that allowlist.

source: Focus indicators were not in any of the 20 scopes, and there are at le
title: The global focus rule forces `border-radius: var(--r-control)`, squaring every focused control from its own radius to 4px
why: tokens.css:976 is `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: var(--r-control) }`. The third declaration changes the element's own geometry, not the outline's, and being unlayered it beats every `rounded-*` utility. globals.css:43 maps `--radius-lg: var(--r-card)` = 14px, so button.tsx:13's `rounded-lg` is 14px at rest and 4px the instant it takes keyboard focus — a visible corner snap on all 121 `<Button` sites. switch.tsx:19 is `rounded-full` (--r-full: 999px) on the element that receives focus, so a focused Switch stops being a pill and becomes a rectangle. badge.tsx:8 is `rounded-4xl` (32px) -> 4px. input.tsx:12 and textarea.tsx:10 are `rounded-lg` -> 4px across 48 sites. There are 83 `rounded-full` occurrences in .tsx, and any of them on a focusable element inherits this. The repo knows: focus-ring.test.ts's third assertion is `expect(declaration(shell, "border-radius")).toBeNull()` with the comment "the ring follows that instead of squaring off to the 4px control radius" — the authors diagnosed the squaring precisely, exempted FieldShell from it by routing around the rule, wrote a test to keep the exemption, and left the cause live on everything else. tokens.css:243-249 gives seven deliberate radii with per-use comments; this one line collapses all seven to one whenever a key is pressed. Nothing in tokens.css, DESIGN.md or the playbook justifies the declaration, and focus-ring.test.ts pins only `outline` and `outline-offset`, so deleting it breaks no test.
fix: Delete `border-radius: var(--r-control)` from tokens.css:976. Modern browsers already follow the element's own border-radius when drawing an outline, which is the behaviour the declaration was presumably reaching for and the behaviour it prevents. Then add an assertion to focus-ring.test.ts that the global rule declares no `border-radius`, mirroring the assertion already made for the shell.
note: Real, visible, and a genuine self-inconsistency. tokens.css:976 is unlayered and sets `border-radius: var(--r-control)` (4px, tokens.css:243); every `rounded-*` utility sits in @layer utilities — a premise unlayered-cascade.test.ts asserts rather than assumes — so the global wins on the focused element itself, not just on the outline. Concretely: button.tsx:13 `rounded-lg` resolves through globals.css:41 to --r-card = 14px and drops to 4px on keyboard focus; kanban-card.tsx:148 is a `rounded-[15px]` lead card on a live board that loses its corners when tabbed to; badge.tsx:8 `rounded-4xl` and switch.tsx:19 `rounded-full` collapse to 4px. Nothing justifies it: DESIGN.md:465-466 specifies the ring as outline plus offset only and never mentions radius, and no comment near tokens.css:976 explains the declaration. source: shadcn
title: The radius shim inverts the semantic scale: every control renders at card radius
why: globals.css:40-44 maps --radius-sm:--r-control(4px) --radius-md:--r-input(6px) --radius-lg:--r-card(14px) --radius-xl:--r-panel(12px). Two things break. First, the scale is NON-MONOTONIC: rounded-lg resolves to 14px while rounded-xl resolves to 12px, so the larger t-shirt name yields the smaller radius. Second and worse, the untouched primitives use shadcn's t-shirt names, so each lands on the wrong semantic rung. tokens.css:243 reserves --r-control:4px for 'buttons, checkboxes, menu items' and --r-input:6px for 'inputs, badges, chips', yet rounded-lg (= --r-card 14px, documented as 'the artifact's card radius') is what button.tsx:13, input.tsx:12, textarea.tsx:10, toggle.tsx, field.tsx, input-group.tsx, accordion.tsx, popover.tsx and toggle-group.tsx all render. A 14px radius on button.tsx's default h-8 (32px) control is nearly a pill. The inversion is total: card.tsx:15, the one component that should be --r-card 14px, uses rounded-xl and gets --r-panel 12px. Same shim makes --r-chip:8px ('secondary buttons') and --r-well:11px unreachable from any Tailwind utility, which is why kit/atomics/button-class.ts:11-14 must write rounded-[var(--r-chip)] as an arbitrary value. Cross-check against pixel authority: design/coach/*.dc.html never draws a 14px control; its control radii are 9px (132x), 10px (98x), 8px (28x) and 6px (6x).
fix: Stop overloading the t-shirt scale with unrelated semantics. Either (a) make the shim monotonic and control-biased (--radius-sm:--r-control --radius-md:--r-input --radius-lg:--r-chip --radius-xl:--r-card), then sweep ui/ so cards use rounded-xl and controls rounded-sm/rounded-md; or (b) drop the --radius-* shim entirely and write rounded-[var(--r-control)] explicitly at each site, as select.tsx:32 and kit/atomics already do. Add a token test asserting the resolved --radius-* chain is strictly ascending.
note: Every load-bearing claim checks out and it is the one finding with real on-screen consequence. globals.css:40-44 is `--radius: var(--r-card); --radius-sm: var(--r-control); --radius-md: var(--r-input); --radius-lg: var(--r-card); --radius-xl: var(--r-panel);`. tokens.css:243-248 gives --r-control 4px, --r-input 6px, --r-card 14px, --r-well 11px, --r-chip 8px, --r-panel 12px. So rounded-lg = 14px and rounded-xl = 12px: the scale IS non-monotonic, and under @theme inline the utility emits `border-radius: var(--r-card)` directly. Note the shim is otherwise an identity map onto Tailwind's own defaults (sm 4, md 6, xl 12 are unchanged); the ONLY divergence is rounded-lg going 8px -> 14px, which is precisely the rung every control uses. Confirmed at button.tsx:13, input.tsx:12, textarea.tsx:10, and I additionally confirmed rounded-lg in accordion, field, input-group, popover, toggle, toggle-group, tabs, sidebar, command, file-upload, dropdown-menu and select -- 22 occurrences across 15 files, not 20. card.tsx:15 does use rounded-xl and lands on --r-panel 12px, the inversion the auditor describes. DOCS CHECK CUTS THE OTHER WAY: DESIGN.md:434 states 'Corner style: 14px (--r-card). Wells 11px, chips and secondary buttons 8px, buttons 9px, inputs 6px, micro-controls 4px', and :446/:449 restate primary radius 9 / secondary radius 8. Nothing in tokens.css, DESIGN.md (incl. Corrections) or COACH-REDESIGN-PLAYBOOK.md justifies a 14px control. The canvas census is exactly right: design/coach/*.dc.html draws 9px x132, 10px x98, 8px x28, 6px x6, and 14px exactly ONCE. I checked globals.css for a corrective override -- the [data-slot="button"] rules at 814/934/959/1372 set height/padding/width only, never border-radius. A 14px corner on the h-8 (32px) default button, imported in 40 files, is visible and is the divergence between a ui/ button and a kit/ button on the same page. --r-chip and --r-well are indeed unreachable from any Tailwind utility, which is why button-class.ts writes rounded-[var(--r-chip)] by hand.

why: coach.css:606 opens the phone step-down with "taken from `CoachHomeMobile.dc.html` rather than invented" — and `CoachHomeMobile.dc.html` does not exist. The real file is `HomeMobile.dc.html`. Worse, the line citations do not resolve either, and every claimed measurement is contradicted by the real artboard: coach.css:610 says "the phone artboard draws the same heading at 30px with -0.024em of tracking on a 1.1 leading -- looser than the desktop pair", but HomeMobile.dc.html:94 draws it at 34px / -0.026em / 1.05, which is *identical* to the desktop pair (coach.css:602-603), so the entire "looser, because tight negative tracking is what a big title can afford and a small one cannot" rationale is invented. coach.css:640 sets --coach-panel-name:19px citing ":99" and calls it "one step under the desktop's 20px"; the string `19px` appears zero times in the artboard, HomeMobile.dc.html:176 and :193 draw panel names at 20px, and line 99 is a horizontal-scroll chip row. coach.css:632 sets --topbar-h:60px citing ":62", which is a box-shadow custom-property declaration; the artboard's only 60px is the bottom tab-bar target height (HomeMobile.dc.html:243). It even quotes the greeting as "Welcome back, Marcus" when the artboard says "Welcome back, Reid". This is the single most damaging finding in a repo whose entire credibility rests on "every value carries written reasoning": the prose has the exact shape of measured design authority with nothing behind it, and it is the flagship responsive decision.
fix: Re-derive the four values from HomeMobile.dc.html and correct the prose: --coach-page-title to 34px, --coach-panel-name deleted from the 639 block (the artboard draws 20px on both densities, same as desktop), --topbar-h re-measured from the artboard's actual header rather than its tab bar. Fix all six dangling filenames to the real basenames. Then add a test in the shape of the existing tokens.test.ts that resolves every `*.dc.html` reference in a comment against design/coach/ and fails on a missing file, so a citation cannot rot or be invented again.
note: Verified in full and the finding UNDERSTATES the scope. `design/coach/CoachHomeMobile.dc.html` does not exist and never has (`git log --diff-filter=R -- design/coach/` shows no rename; the canvas has three commits and the file has always been `HomeMobile.dc.html`, 252 lines). Every measurement the phone step-down claims to have lifted from it contradicts the real artboard: coach.css:611 says 'the phone artboard draws the same heading at 30px with -0.024em of tracking on a 1.1 leading' — HomeMobile.dc.html:94 draws it at 34px, -0.026em, 1.05, and the file contains no 30px font-size anywhere. coach.css:622 says '60px, which CoachHomeMobile.dc.html:62 draws' — line 62 is `--primary-shadow`, and the phone top bar (line 81) is 64px; the 60px in that artboard is the *bottom tab* height (line 241 comment: '60px targets'), so the number was lifted off the wrong element. coach.css:635 says '19px, from CoachHomeMobile.dc.html:99' — line 99 is the date-range scroller div, and the file contains no 19px at all (its only two panel headings are 20px, lines 176 and 193). coach.css:682 says '11px ... per CoachHomeMobile.dc.html:104' — line 104 is a pill button at `border-radius: 999px`. coach-pillbar.tsx:35/145/185 cite lines 160 and 165 for the tab label and the amber badge; those lines are a card wrapper and a padding declaration (the tabs are at 242-246). Repo-wide the pattern is far larger than n=7: 30 distinct `.dc.html` filenames are cited that do not exist on disk across ~155 citation sites, including 19 to `CoachError.dc.html`, 16 to `MeetYourAgent.dc.html`, 14 to `CoachHomeMobile.dc.html`, 8 to `AdminClients.dc.html`, and a whole `Admin*`/`Consumer*`/`Login`/`Landing` family for which no canvas exists in the repo at all. This is the exact tell: confident measured prose citing a pixel authority that was never opened. All five cited lines check out.

source: src/lib was in no scope, yet it is a presentation layer: it holds the
tell: a canonical module declared 'the one place' and bypassed everywhere
title: format/datetime.ts claims to be the only date formatter and is bypassed 10 times, including three with no timeZone at all
why: datetime.ts:2 opens 'The one place a workspace surface is allowed to turn an instant into display text', and :4-8 names the exact failure it exists to stop: a formatter without an explicit timeZone renders UTC on Vercel and the viewer's zone in the browser, which is React 19 error #418. Three sites do precisely that. impersonation-banner.tsx:95 calls `expires.toLocaleTimeString("en-US", {hour, minute})` with no timeZone, on a banner mounted on every impersonated page. connect-channel-flow.ts:131 constructs `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-GB", {day, month, year})` with no timeZone. agent-simulator.ts:129-137 -- rendered by meet-your-agent.tsx and agent-flow.tsx -- builds a slot label with no timeZone and then splices a hardcoded ', 2:30 PM' onto it (:140), so the date half moves with the runtime's zone while the time half is a string constant that never can. Separately, datetime.ts:18 pins `LOCALE = "en-US"` and seven sites construct en-GB formatters instead, so the same fact renders in two orders inside one console: /admin/help prints '4 Sep 2026' (admin-help.tsx:68) while /admin/audit prints 'September 4, 2026' (admin-audit-log.tsx:143). Three more (admin-overview.tsx:103, owner-overview.tsx:77, :91) render dates in `timeZone: "UTC"` with no zone marker printed -- the ambiguity datetime.ts:64-71 argues against by name when it makes utcTimestampLabel append a literal ' UTC'.
fix: Add the two missing shapes to src/lib/format/datetime.ts (a time-only formatter and a long-date formatter, both pinned to LOCALE and WORKSPACE_DISPLAY_TIMEZONE), then replace the ten bypasses with imports. Add a test that greps src/components and src/app for `Intl.DateTimeFormat` / `toLocale*` outside src/lib/format and fails on any construction lacking an explicit timeZone, with a named exemption for the two viewer-zone sites that argue for themselves (consumer-experience.tsx:228, signup-form.tsx:295).

source: The owner console's actual UI implementation — the largest single body
tell: self-inconsistency (two full implementations of one screen shipped side by side)
title: Nine finished console screens are unreachable: the pre-rehaul implementations were never removed, and ~3,600 lines of dead UI are still pinned by ~2,800 lines of tests
why: COACH-REDESIGN-PLAYBOOK.md:183-185 records the owner rehaul ran behind SETTERFI_UI_REHAUL 'until the flag was deleted in 99eb3c5 and the rehaul simply became the app.' The new screens landed; the old ones were never deleted. A repo-wide scan for each exported screen component, excluding tests and its own defining file, returns ZERO render sites for: AdminCompliance (admin-compliance.tsx:513, ~702 lines; /admin/compliance renders OwnerCompliance and takes only ComplianceHeader from this file), AdminInboxSurface (admin-inbox.tsx:148, ~617; /admin/alerts renders OwnerInbox and takes only AdminInboxUnavailable), AdminAuditLog (admin-audit-log.tsx:1139, ~635; /admin/audit renders OwnerAudit and takes only types + AUDIT_ACTION_FILTER_OPTIONS), AdminMoneyBilling (admin-money-billing.tsx:804, ~498; owner-money.tsx imports only its label helpers), AdminSupport (admin-support.tsx:569, ~323) and AdminSupportTeam (admin-support-team.tsx:143, ~290) whose routes are redirect stubs, MoneyBlockingBanner (admin-money-tiers.tsx:722, ~350), AdminOverviewSurface (admin-overview.tsx:1383; /admin/overview renders OwnerOverview), AdminMoneyCorrections (admin-money-corrections.tsx:671), MovementDisclosure (admin-money-billing-revenue.tsx:159). That is ~3,624 lines of console UI that cannot be reached, each still carrying a full test file — admin-audit-log.test.tsx 903 lines, admin-compliance.test.tsx 499, admin-money-billing.test.tsx 492, admin-support.test.tsx 447, admin-inbox.test.tsx 278, admin-support-team.test.tsx 215, ~2,834 lines total — so the tree reads as maintained while half the bulk of the largest console files is not on screen. A designer opening admin-audit-log.tsx cannot tell which of the two audit tables ships. This also explains the audit gap the completeness critic found. The same playbook's trap list says 'reclaim dead rules rather than raise [the CSS cap] a third time' — that discipline was applied to stylesheets and not to components.
fix: Delete the nine superseded components and their tests. If any is deliberately kept as a rollback, say so in a docstring at each export and add one test asserting it has no render site, so the intent is legible. Start with the four whose routes are settled: AdminAuditLog, AdminCompliance, AdminInboxSurface, AdminOverviewSurface.

source: Every design guard in the repo roots its scan at src/ or narrower, so
title: tokens.css's light palette is hand-transcribed into public/site/index.html, the exact defect two guards were written to stop
why: public/site/index.html:15-29 declares nine values that are byte-for-byte copies of tokens.css: 0.9612 0.0042 262 (tokens.css:34 --canvas), 0.9905 0.0026 262 (:43 --card), 0.983 0.0048 262 (:49 --well), 0.4349 0.039 262 (:107 --faint), 0.5261 0.041 262 (:124 --overline), 0.44 0.165 264 (:141 --accent-text), 0.2325 0.023 262 (:104 --ink), 0.3604 0.036 262 (:106 --muted), rgba(60, 90, 150, 0.13) (:89 --line). source: typography
tell: (4) Inter font everywhere / (19) Space Grotesk + Instrument Serif — the shipped public marketing site runs on Inter, Roboto and Geist, not the documented Archivo/IBM Plex Mono pair
title: The public marketing site downloads Inter and Roboto and sets SetterFi's own product cards in Inter
why: This is the first surface a prospect sees and it is the one place in the repo where the documented type pair loses. index.html:10 requests four families from Google Fonts — Archivo and IBM Plex Mono, plus Roboto and Inter. Line 31 declares `--ui: "Inter", -apple-system, "SF Pro Text", "Roboto", system-ui` with Inter FIRST, so Inter always wins even on the surfaces where the fallbacks were the point. Three rules consume it: :181 (.phone__screen, an iPhone/Messenger mock that renders in Inter rather than the SF Pro it lists second), :271 (.meta, a Meta Events Manager mock), and — the one that is not defensible as pastiche — :323 (.card), whose own comment two lines above reads "The two late cards: refusals, and the follow-up ladder. Product-console styling." That is SetterFi's own console, drawn on its own marketing page, set in Inter at a hardcoded #181e28. Separately, public/site/scrollcraft.css:31-33 still carries the stock scrollcraft token block — "Instrument Sans", "Geist", "Geist Mono" — three families the page never loads. index.html:21-22 overrides display and text with Archivo but never overrides --sc-font-mono, so the .sc-label rule at scrollcraft.css:158 still points at an unloaded "Geist Mono" and silently resolves to ui-monospace. source: unlayered-cascade.test.ts attributes classes per-file, so a collision
title: Nine padding and radius declarations written on <Surface> callers are dead; the element draws the recipe and the author's number never renders
why: `.surface-card` declares `padding: 16px 17px` and `border-radius: var(--r-card)` (14px) at globals.css:149-155, and `.surface-well` declares `padding: 12px 13px` at :189-195, all unlayered. Every padding or radius utility a caller passes to <Surface> therefore does nothing. All seven padding sites and both radius sites are dead: metric-card.tsx:61 writes `p-[15px_16px]` and draws 16px 17px - and this is a kit component, so the miss multiplies across every screen that renders a MetricCard; optin-artifact.tsx:134 and :181 each write `p-[var(--s-6)]` (24px) and `rounded-[var(--coach-panel-radius)]` (24px 24px 17px 17px) and draw 16px 17px at a uniform 14px; get-started-checklist.tsx:569 writes `p-[var(--s-4)]` (16px) on a well that draws 12px 13px; affiliate-money.tsx:843 and affiliate-home.tsx:543 each write `p-[var(--s-5)]` (20px) on a well that draws 12px 13px; atomics-sheet.tsx:177 writes `p-[10px]`. source: Orphaned dead CSS — named in the audit brief as a tell-adjacent axis,
title: Half the .t-* type layer is dead, and coach.css spends an override block re-sizing the dead half

Seven have zero call sites anywhere in src/**, design/coach/*.dc.html or public/site: .t-metric (1002), .t-money (1005), .t-transcript (1006), .t-nav (1010), .t-th (1012), .t-badge (1013), .t-count (1014). source: Entire product surfaces cite pixel authority that was never drawn — th
tell: uncited appeal to authority ("the canvas draws…" with nothing behind it)
title: console.css builds a 735-line second design language on eight appeals to a canvas that never drew a console screen; its signature values appear in zero artboards
why: console.css carries two filename citations and six bare appeals, and not one is checkable. The two named: :196 drops a fill 'rather than replaced by the white alpha `AdminPlans.dc.html:263` draws on the Growth card' and quotes the artboard's value as 14%; :381 sets `gap: 13px` as '13px, from `AdminRevenue.dc.html:266`. It was 12, which is the table row's padding rather than this row's ... the drawing gives it the extra pixel for that', then adds a second claim about the same nonexistent line ('The same line draws a fourth track, `30px minmax(0, 1fr) auto 16px`, for a trailing chevron'). Neither file exists. The six bare ones are worse because they cannot even be looked up: :45 'The canvas draws it at 58px; this holds it at 46'; :308 'The canvas draws the hero with no band at all'; :364 'This is the shape the canvas draws for every "needs a human" list'; :492-494 'The canvas draws the strip at exactly this radius ... the drawn admin affiliates and admin agent-performance screens both put four figure tiles at `15px 15px 11px 11px`'; :510 'the artboards cited above draw the strip a component away from where the code drew it'; :572 'The vertical 13px is the canvas's'. Corroboration check across all 22 boards, VOCABULARY.md, DESIGN.md, REDESIGN-CANVAS.md and the playbook: `58px` — zero hits. `15px 15px 11px 11px` — zero hits. `gap: 13px` — zero hits. `13px 18px` — zero hits. `13.5px` — the only survivor, and it is corroborated by REDESIGN-CANVAS.md:60's density table, not by a drawing. So every number this file presents as traced is in fact chosen, and :492-510 goes further: it settles a live disagreement between two rules ('two rules about one strip, disagreeing, with the drawing behind the second') by deferring to a drawing that does not exist. console-stat-deck.tsx:22 then repeats the same two artboard names as the reason the strip takes 15/11.
fix: Rewrite the eight appeals as decisions with owners. The values are defensible on their own arguments — a 24px top corner on a 90px tile does eat the label — so the comments lose nothing by saying 'chosen 2026-09-0X because…' instead of 'the canvas draws'. Critically, :492-510 must stop resolving a real rule conflict by citing a missing drawing; state which corner the strip takes and why, on the merits.

source: Date, number and locale formatting consistency — no scope owned it, no
title: An en-GB date cluster inside a locale-pinned en-US product, with the locale never chosen — only patched around
why: datetime.ts:18 pins `const LOCALE = "en-US"` and the module docblock (:2-13) states it is "the one place a workspace surface is allowed to turn an instant into display text". Seven sites across six files construct en-GB formatters instead (also src/components/workspace/admin-help.tsx:68 and src/components/workspace/rehaul/connect-channel-flow.ts:131), so today's date reads "4 Sep 2026" on those surfaces and "Sep 4, 2026" on the canonical ones. Not one of the seven carries a comment justifying en-GB — remarkable in a repo where nearly every other formatter is preceded by a paragraph of reasoning (owner-system.tsx:264-267, affiliate-money.tsx:220-224, trend-panel.tsx:54-56 all justify their timeZone choice in prose). The one comment that does exist proves the locale was inherited rather than decided: owner-overview.tsx:102-103 says "en-GB puts a comma after the weekday; the artboard does not, and the comma is the only difference between the two spellings", then does `.replace(",", "")` at :104. The artboard is the pixel authority; the author reached for en-GB, found it disagreed with the authority, and stripped a character instead of switching locale. en-US with the same options needs no strip. The drift has since been cemented: src/components/workspace/admin-help.test.tsx:47 asserts `/Generated 24 Aug 2026 with 12 operator guides/`, so a regression test now pins the wrong locale's output.
fix: Replace all seven en-GB constructors with the canonical exports: `workspaceDateFormat` for the day+short-month+year sites (admin-help.tsx:68, admin-overview.tsx:103, admin-measurement-tables.tsx:26, owner-overview.tsx:91), and en-US equivalents for owner-overview.tsx:77 and owner-clients.tsx:211. title: kit/motion.ts declares itself "the one place the scale is restated in JS"; there are seven, and five of them hardcode values that are on no rung
why: kit/motion.ts:8 states the rule in its own header: "this is the one place the scale is restated in JS. Keep it in step with tokens.css." Seven files restate it. src/components/motion/tokens.ts:1-15 is a second full DURATION/EASE table. command-palette.tsx:106-108 declares PALETTE_OPEN_TRANSITION as `{duration: 0.25, ease: [0.22,1,0.36,1]}` -- byte-identical to INDICATOR_TRANSITION, redeclared rather than imported. data-state.tsx:188 inlines the same `{duration: 0.25, ease: [0.22,1,0.36,1]}` a third time. icons.tsx:313 inlines `duration: 0.5` with the same bezier. The magic bezier [0.22,1,0.36,1] is hand-copied into five separate files. Worse, the values then drift off the seven-rung scale entirely: meet-your-agent.tsx:705 and :1049 use 0.22s, :846 uses 0.16s; motion/index.tsx:133 uses 0.24s with `ease: "easeOut"` and :143 uses 0.22s -- in the same file that imports DURATION and EASE two lines up. source: Disabled and inactive states are drawn by fading the element, at three
title: The identical accent-fill CTA is disabled at 50% in three files and 60% in three others
why: Six hand-written primary CTAs share the same face token-for-token - [background:var(--accent-fill)] or bg-[image:var(--accent-fill)], border-[var(--accent-line)], text-[color:var(--on-accent)] - and split three-three on the disabled multiplier: 50 at coach-agent.tsx:149, coach-support-bubble.tsx:84 and coach-settings-notifications.tsx:170; 60 at step-shell.tsx:66, connect-channel-sheet.tsx:71 and meet-agent.tsx:604. source: auth+entry
title: Padding utilities on <Surface> never apply: three inert p-* declarations, in the exact failure mode the repo already diagnosed in writing
why: globals.css's `@layer base` block closes at line 132; `.surface-card { padding: 16px 17px }` at globals.css:149-155 is therefore UNLAYERED author CSS. Tailwind emits every utility inside `@layer utilities`, and unlayered author CSS beats any cascade layer regardless of specificity. cn() is twMerge (src/lib/utils.ts:5), which cannot dedupe a Tailwind utility against a plain class, so the utility ships and is inert. Three call sites on this surface pass padding to a default- or card-variant <Surface>: atomics-sheet.tsx:177 `p-[10px]` (the 'card, open' swatch, which therefore renders at 16/17px like its six siblings -- the class string is the only thing distinguishing it); optin-artifact.tsx:134 and :181 `p-[var(--s-6)]` (24px intended on the hosted consent/terms/privacy documents a lead opens from an SMS link, rendering at 16/17px). Surface itself supplies the sanctioned escape hatch -- `is-flush` (surface.tsx:61, globals.css:163) -- and none of the three uses it. This is verbatim the defect auth-shell.tsx:188-220 spends thirty lines diagnosing ('none of them had ever applied... A dead declaration reads exactly like a live one'), written on this same surface. The pattern was found once, documented at length, and never swept for: 5 instances survive repo-wide.
fix: On src/app/design/atomics-sheet.tsx:177, drop the dead `p-[10px]` (the swatch should show the card recipe's real padding, which is the point of a surface ladder). On src/components/onboarding/optin-artifact.tsx:134 and :181, either accept the recipe's 16/17px and delete `p-[var(--s-6)]`, or add `is-flush` and set the padding deliberately. Then add a guard in the shape of entry-surfaces.test.ts asserting no <Surface> call site carries a p/px/py utility without is-flush -- 5 repo-wide, so the register starts small.
note: Mechanism verified end to end. globals.css @layer base opens at :92 and closes at :132; .surface-card at :149-155 declares padding: 16px 17px unlayered; Tailwind emits utilities inside @layer utilities, so the utility loses at any specificity -- globals.css:157-162 states this defect in its own words and ships .surface-card.is-flush (:163) as the sanctioned escape, which surface.tsx:61 uses for variant='panel'. Surface defaults variant='card' (surface.tsx:48,58), so a caller passing padding through className gets the recipe. I scanned every <Surface> in src: exactly 3 card-variant sites pass a padding utility -- atomics-sheet.tsx:177 p-[10px], optin-artifact.tsx:134 and :181 p-[var(--s-6)] -- plus 2 well-variant sites against .surface-well's own padding: 12px 13px (globals.css:193): affiliate-home.tsx:543 and affiliate-money.tsx:843. That is 5 repo-wide, exactly as claimed. THE FINDING IS ACTUALLY UNDERSTATED: both optin sites also pass rounded-[var(--coach-panel-radius)], which loses to .surface-card's border-radius: var(--r-card) (globals.css:152). --coach-panel-radius is 24px 24px 17px 17px (coach.css:60); the card renders at 14px -- and the comment at optin-artifact.tsx:129-133 immediately above it explicitly asserts the opposite ('The deck panel's asymmetric radius -- larger on top -- rather than the console's even --r-card ... a lead who lands here from a text message ... should not meet two different products'). That is a stated design intent silently defeated on a public, force-dynamic, SMS-reachable page. ONE CORRECTION: the repo HAS swept for this. src/app/unlayered-cascade.test.ts is a 605-line guard that compiles utilities through the project's own Tailwind and diffs them against every unlayered declaration, with a KNOWN backlog. It misses these three because unlayered-cascade.test.ts:346-352 resolves 'styled' classes from the same className string literal, and 'surface-card' is added inside the Surface component -- so utilities passed through a component prop are its blind spot. 'Never swept for' is wrong; 'the sweep cannot see prop pass-through' is right, and is the more actionable statement. atomics-sheet:177 has no visual consequence (it renders like its six siblings); the two optin sites do.

source: Responsive thresholds are the only design axis in the repo with no tok
tell: self-inconsistency — one visual relationship reflows at four different widths across sibling components in the same kit
title: The 'stacked → row with trailing block pushed right' recipe ships at 420, 440, 448 and 520px across four settings atomics that render on the same screen
why: Four components run the byte-identical recipe — `flex-col` base, then `flex-row` + `items-center` + `gap-[14px]` + `ml-auto` on the trailing block — at four thresholds spanning 100px. NoteStrip (queue-item.tsx:115) at 420; SettingRow (setting-row.tsx:69) at 440; CollapsedSettingCard (setting-row.tsx:230) and SettingSection (setting-row.tsx:311) at 520; the vendored Field (ui/field.tsx:63) at @md = 448. Two of these live in the same file 161 lines apart, and account-security-settings.tsx puts a 520px section toggle (line 278) directly above 440px setting rows (line 347) inside one pane — so between 440 and 520 CSS px that screen renders its rows horizontally while the section header above them is still stacked, a visible 80px dead zone in a single card. SettingRow's own docstring (lines 50-53) states the rule as 'the control drops under the text at the point the row itself runs out of width', which is a real principle; the four different answers to 'what point' are what was never decided. 420 vs 440 is 20px apart doing the same job, and 440 vs the framework's own 448 is 8px apart doing the same job.

source: Responsive thresholds are the only design axis in the repo with no tok
tell: self-inconsistency — code violates a rule its own adjacent comment states
title: One named container, four two-up thresholds: the onboarding wizard's five steps go multi-column at 640, 720, 860 and 900px against the same measured column
why: `@container/onboarding` is declared exactly once, at onboarding-shell.tsx:196, and the comment immediately above it (lines 185-188) states the intent outright: 'Every two-up and three-up on the five step screens measures this column'. They do measure that one column — and they switch against it at four different widths: calendar grid-cols-2 at 640 (line 238), profile grid-cols-2 at 720 (lines 137/166/210), offer grid-cols-2 at 860 (line 52), connect grid-cols-3 at 900 (line 114) and sms at 900 (line 196), with the shell's own footer row going flex-row at 720 (line 120). The per-step `maxWidth` prop does not explain the spread: it only caps the column at 1080/1160/1200, so below ~1080px every step measures an identical width, and 640 vs 720 sit far beneath every cap. The observable result is that a coach resizing the window while walking the wizard sees step 4 (calendar) two-up at 700px, step 2 (profile) still stacked, step 3 (offer) stacked until 860 — the same wizard chrome reflowing at four different moments. All four are the same relationship: a grid of equal-weight field pairs or review cards going from one column to two.
fix: Collapse the five steps onto one two-up threshold and one three-up threshold against @container/onboarding — e.g. 720 for grid-cols-2 and 900 for grid-cols-3 — editing onboarding-calendar.tsx:238 (640→720), onboarding-offer.tsx:52 (860→720) and leaving profile/connect/sms as the anchors, so the shell comment's claim becomes true.

source: Date, time and number formatting has no audit scope and is systematica
title: The repo's own formatting guard test is currently red, and its scope and regexes exempt the exact failure modes it exists to catch
why: datetime.test.ts:66-76 asserts `expect(offenders).toEqual([])` for any `new Intl.DateTimeFormat` lacking a timeZone under src/app and src/components. I re-ran that exact scanning logic in node against the current tree: it returns one offender, src/components/workspace/rehaul/connect-channel-flow.ts:131, whose `longDate()` builds `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-GB", { day, month, year })` with no timeZone and is rendered into shipped copy at line 125 ("Connected to {label} on {longDate(date)}"). A guard that the tree already fails is a guard nobody has run. Three further holes make it decorative even when green: (1) line 51 scans only ["src/app", "src/components"], so all of src/lib is unguarded — src/lib/agent-simulator.ts:134 constructs a timeZone-less formatter and is imported by two "use client" components; (2) line 62's regex is /toLocale(String|DateString|TimeString)\(\s*\)/, which matches only empty parens, so every real call — all of which pass a locale argument — walks straight past it; (3) the describe block at line 50 is titled "no surface formats against the ambient zone **or locale**" and contains zero assertions about locale, while seven en-GB formatters ship. The test's name promises an enforcement its body never implements.
fix: Add `timeZone` to connect-channel-flow.ts:131 (WORKSPACE_DISPLAY_TIMEZONE, or route it through workspaceDateFormat) to make the suite green. Then extend the scan root at datetime.test.ts:51 to include "src/lib" (excluding src/lib/format), relax the toLocale regex to /\.toLocale(String|DateString|TimeString)\(/ with a named allowlist for the two number-only call sites, and add the locale assertion the describe block already claims: no `new Intl.*Format` outside src/lib/format may pass a locale literal other than "en-US", except the four documented en-CA ISO-key sites.
note: I replicated the test's exact scan in Node (readdirSync over src/app + src/components, same two regexes). It returns one offender: src/components/workspace/rehaul/connect-channel-flow.ts, whose longDate() at :131 builds `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-GB", {day,month,year})` with no timeZone. `expect(offenders).toEqual([])` at datetime.test.ts:75 therefore fails — the guard is red against shipped source, not a fixture. The two exemption claims also hold on reading. (a) The bare-toLocale regex at :62 is `toLocale(String|DateString|TimeString)\(\s*\)` — zero-argument calls only — so src/components/kit/impersonation-banner.tsx:95 `expires.toLocaleTimeString("en-US", {hour, minute})` passes it while doing exactly what the rule forbids: reading the ambient zone. My replication confirms the toLocale check returns []. (b) The scan roots at :51 are only ["src/app","src/components"], so every formatter in src/lib is unaudited (agent-simulator.ts, booking/service.ts, notifications/events.ts, brain/render-placeholders.ts, quiet-hours/window.ts). All five cited lines are real and point at what is claimed. Caveat noted and set aside: the authority here lives in a test file, but the violation is in shipped source, so this is a genuine self-inconsistency rather than a test-file nit.

source: icons
title: Two mutually contradictory icon authorities: the canvas says 24-grid stroke at 20px, the kit ships filled Phosphor at 16px
why: The approved design canvas is unambiguous. VOCABULARY.md:71-72: "Icons are inline stroke SVG on a 24 viewBox, drawn at 20px (24px in the bubble and phone tabs): stroke: currentColor; fill: none; stroke-width: 1.75; round caps and joins" - and the canvas backs it with 262 icons, every one on viewBox="0 0 24 24", against `.i { width: 20px; height: 20px; stroke: currentColor; fill: none; stroke-width: 1.75 }`. src/components/kit/icons.tsx then declares itself the single authority ("Two families live here and nothing else does") and ships something that disagrees on all four axes: Phosphor rather than bespoke inline SVG, a 256 grid rather than 24, KIT_ICON_SIZE = 16 (icons.tsx:104) rather than 20, and filled paths rather than 1.75 stroke - icons.test.tsx:30 pins `fill` to currentColor, and the wrapper hard-sets weight="regular" with fill, never a stroke. Neither document cites the other; there is no correction note reconciling them, unlike the palette change which got a dated Corrections entry in DESIGN.md:664. The product splits along that seam: coach surfaces follow the canvas (23 inline 24-grid stroke SVGs across 17 files), console/kit surfaces follow icons.tsx (Phosphor 16px filled), rehaul surfaces follow lucide. Three families rendering concurrently is the state icons.tsx:11 claims to have fixed.
fix: Pick one authority and write the decision down where the other lives. Either (a) restate the canvas rule as superseded with a dated entry in DESIGN.md Corrections and note in VOCABULARY.md:71 that shipped code uses Phosphor at 16, or (b) if the canvas is still pixel authority, retune icons.tsx to 20px stroke glyphs. Until one is chosen, every new surface picks a family by accident.

source: public/site/ — the page actually served at `/` in production — was in
title: The page's own exits do not work: the in-world CTA can never exceed 15.6% opacity and stays pointer-events:none, and both footer links 404
why: index.html:961 computes ctaOn = Math.max(1 - ramp(t,0.6,1.3), ramp(t,15.9,16.3)) on a track whose maximum value is 16, not 17. The only in-flow element is the spacer, which scrollcraft.js:566 sizes to (W.total + 1) * vh = 17vh (W.total = 16 from data-sc-w at index.html:478); everything else is position:fixed, so max scrollY = 17vh - vh = 16vh and index.html:863's trackT() tops out at exactly 16. ramp(16, 15.9, 16.3) = smooth(0.25) = 0.15625. So at the very bottom of the page the reply-bubble CTA -- which index.html:361 calls 'the CTA lives in the world, where the header put it' and index.html:960 calls 'present at the wide shot' -- renders at opacity 0.156, with pointerEvents 'none' and tabIndex -1 (index.html:964-965). The TOTAL = 17 constant at index.html:726 is described as 'the leg (16vh) plus the engine's landing viewport', but that landing viewport is what the spacer's +1 already consumes, so no scroll position ever produces t > 16. Separately, docs/SETUP.md:216-218 records that /privacy and /terms 'do not exist yet' and there is no privacy/ or terms/ directory under src/app, so index.html:685-686 ship two 404s in the footer of the page served at /. A designer reading a scroll story whose climax beat is a CTA that fades to 15% and cannot be clicked would say the numbers were written, not walked.
fix: Change ramp(t, 15.9, 16.3) at index.html:961 to a window that closes at or before 16 (e.g. 15.6 to 16.0), or bump the spacer to W.total + 2. Verify by asserting cta.style.opacity === '1.000' and cta.tabIndex === 0 at scrollY = document.body.scrollHeight - innerHeight. Ship /privacy and /terms, or point the footer at real destinations.

source: motion
tell: (14) hover effect inconsistency + duration mix on one surface
title: One component's hover lift has three implementations on three clocks, two distances, two CSS properties and two easings
why: `<DeckPanel liftable>` emits one attribute, `data-liftable="true"` (deck-panel.tsx:189). Three separate places animate it. coach.css:706 uses `transition: translate 160ms var(--ease-smooth-out, ease-out)` with `translate: 0 -2px` at L710. console.css:135 uses `transition: transform 140ms ease, border-color 140ms ease` with `transform: translateY(-2px)` at L139 -- a different property, a different duration, and plain `ease` instead of the token. motion/index.tsx:110's useHoverLift moves `calc(var(--distance-micro) * -1)` = -4px over DURATION.quick = 150ms with EASE.smoothOut. So the same card lifts 2px in 160ms on coach, 2px in 140ms on admin, and 4px in 150ms in the dead JS -- and none of the three is 150ms/--duration-quick, the token that exists for exactly this gesture. 140ms and 160ms appear nowhere in tokens.css. The `var(--ease-smooth-out, ease-out)` fallback in coach.css is also dead weight: the token is unconditionally defined at tokens.css:306. Reading these three side by side, nobody decided the lift; three passes each guessed at it.
fix: Pick one: `transition: translate var(--duration-quick) var(--ease-smooth-out)` with `translate: 0 calc(var(--distance-micro) * -1)`, defined once on `.coach-panel[data-liftable="true"]` in globals.css. Delete the coach.css and console.css copies (keeping console.css's border-color change, which is the correct non-fade hover), drop the redundant `, ease-out` fallback, and delete useHoverLift with the rest of src/components/motion/.

source: cards
tell: self-inconsistency — the four-ground model bypassed by hand-rolled surfaces that duplicate token values
title: Three dark "drench" card faces are hand-built from raw OKLCH literals that are verbatim copies of tokens, ignoring the drench token system built for exactly this
why: The repo has a complete, documented drench system: `--console-drench-live: linear-gradient(158deg, oklch(0.28 0.08 262), oklch(0.17 0.04 265))` (console.css:83, coach.css:92), plus a token-remap block at coach.css:1022-1060 that redeclares --ink/--body/--muted/--faint/--well/--band/--line/--accent-edge for a dark subtree with measured contrast ratios in the comments. src/components/kit/app-shell.tsx:373 consumes it correctly as `var(--console-drench-live, ...)`. These three surfaces do not. owner-overview.tsx:531-537 — the file's own comment at line 525 calls it "the one drenched surface the screen is allowed" — paints `linear-gradient(160deg, oklch(0.30 0.07 262), oklch(0.19 0.045 262) 70%)` with `border: 1px solid oklch(0.22 0.04 262)`. owner-money.tsx:263 paints a third gradient, `160deg, oklch(0.2905 0.045 262) → oklch(0.2325 0.023 262)`, with `border-transparent`. context-eye.tsx paints a flat `oklch(0.2325 0.023 262)`. Four dark grounds, three of them invented, two at 160deg against the token's 158deg, no two matching. Worse, the literals are verbatim retypes: `oklch(0.2325 0.023 262)` IS `--ink` (tokens.css:104), `oklch(0.6409 0.115 71)` IS `--warning` (:156), `oklch(0.6503 0.135 32)` IS `--failure` (:192), `oklch(0.6237 0.095 164)` IS `--good` (:163) — and they are the LIGHT palette's values, frozen, so these cards do not flip under [data-theme=dark] while everything around them does. Because none of them carries the remap block, any kit component nested inside draws light-palette hairlines on a dark ground — the precise bug coach.css:1029-1037 documents having already fixed once ("a near-white chevron on a near-white square at about 1.02:1").
fix: Give each surface the drench token as its background (`var(--console-drench-live)`) and apply the `[data-drench]` remap block so nested tokens resolve against the dark ground, rather than each file inventing a gradient and hardcoding four text colours. The status-bar tones at owner-money.tsx:218-220 should read `var(--warning)`/`var(--failure)`/`var(--good)` so they follow the palette.

source: coach-css+pages
tell: 15 — inconsistent spacing (compounded by a fabricated source citation)
title: .coach-panel--page invents a 15px/30px box model and attributes it to an artboard that does not exist
why: The comment at coach.css:310-330 is the single most confident justification in the file, and every load-bearing claim in it is false. (1) It cites `CoachError.dc.html:96` and `:106`; no such file exists — the error artboard is `ErrorState.dc.html`. (2) It says the artboard draws a `15px 30px` band; `ErrorState.dc.html:113` draws `padding: 19px 20px` — byte-identical to the deck panel it claims to differ from. (3) It says the body is `28px 30px 30px` on a 24px gap; `:123` draws `padding: 26px 20px 28px` with no gap (the button below takes `margin-top: 24px`). (4) Its stated motivation — "squeezed a 620px card's body into a 20px gutter" — is contradicted by the artboard, whose gutter IS 20px. (5) It says the tile and name are "centred against each other" and ships `align-items: center`; the artboard uses `align-items: flex-start`. (6) It says the artboard draws the hero radius `30px 30px 17px 17px`; `ErrorState.dc.html:112` draws `24px 24px 17px 17px`, and the hero radius appears only in Billing/HomeFirstRun/Vocabulary. Confirming the invention: across all 22 artboards, `15px` never appears as a padding (only font-size/width/height) and `30px` never appears as a padding (only border-radius/width/height). Either way, correct the citation to `ErrorState.dc.html:113`/`:123`.

source: Date, number and locale formatting consistency — no scope owned it, no
title: Ambient-timezone formatting reintroduced on the workspace root layout — the exact React #418 the canonical module was written to stop
why: datetime.ts:4-8 names the defect precisely: a `timeZone`-less formatter reads the ambient zone, "Vercel's server runs UTC and a browser runs the viewer's zone, so the same instant serialised as 'Aug 17, 4:35 PM' in the SSR HTML and then re-rendered as 'Aug 17, 10:05 PM' after hydration — React 19 error #418". Two sites reintroduce it. impersonation-banner.tsx:95 calls `expires.toLocaleTimeString("en-US", { hour: "numeric", minute: "2-digit" })` with no timeZone; it is a "use client" component mounted from the workspace root layout at layout.tsx:122 ("the only server boundary above all thirty shell mounts"), so it server-renders on every page of an impersonation session. The author demonstrably knew the pattern — the sibling clock at :217 is gated `now === null ? "counting" : elapsedLabel(...)`, the standard hydration-safe shape — but :242 renders `expiryLabel(expiresAt)` ungated. connect-channel-flow.ts:131 is the second: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-GB", { day, month, year })`, no timeZone, feeding user-visible copy at :125. The repo's own guard already catches that one: replicating src/lib/format/datetime.test.ts:66-76 verbatim over its 671-file source set returns exactly `['src/components/workspace/rehaul/connect-channel-flow.ts']`, so `npm test` is red at HEAD. Git confirms the direction: the guard landed in 3616f66, the offender in b690925, 44 commits later. The guard cannot see impersonation-banner.tsx:95 at all, because its bare-call regex requires empty parens (`toLocale(String|DateString|TimeString)\(\s*\)`) and its DateTimeFormat regex never inspects `toLocale*` with arguments.
fix: impersonation-banner.tsx:92-98 — add `timeZone: WORKSPACE_DISPLAY_TIMEZONE` or, better, reuse a shared time-only export. connect-channel-flow.ts:131 — swap to `workspaceDateFormat`. Then widen the guard at datetime.test.ts:60-64 from `\(\s*\)` to any `toLocale*String(` call whose argument list lacks `timeZone`, so the escape hatch closes.

source: Every design guard in the repo roots its scan at src/ or narrower, so
title: Two guards enumerate the files they govern by hand while a third guard in the same suite argues at length that this is the bug
why: agent-surface.test.ts:87-102 states the principle explicitly -- 'Every stylesheet in the tree, found rather than listed. The floor used to be asserted against three sheets named by hand, which is how src/app/onboarding/onboarding.css came to carry 24 declarations under it... Walking for them means a stylesheet is covered by existing' -- and backs it with a control at :109-116. Two other guards do the opposite. css-budget.test.ts:50 uses a NON-RECURSIVE readdirSync on src/app, so it charges only globals.css and tokens.css; :28-40 then names three deferred sheets by hand. unlayered-cascade.test.ts:36-43 hardcodes six sheets under a comment that says 'The sheets that are imported plainly' -- and layout.test.ts:17-21 asserts the root layout plainly imports a seventh, @xyflow/react/dist/style.css, which is absent from that list. The arithmetic: the repo carries 8,318 lines of CSS; the 3,100 'app CSS budget' governs 3,076 of them (37%). meet-your-agent.css (344), agent-flow.module.css (71) and meet-your-agent.module.css (31) are neither charged nor printed in the deferred diagnostics. public/site/scrollcraft.css (432) and its source copy scrollcraft/builds/setterfi/scrollcraft.css (432) are invisible to both. A new stylesheet at src/app/anything/new.css escapes the cap entirely because the readdir is not recursive, and a sixth top-level sheet would be charged but a nested one would not -- the cap's answer depends on which directory the author happened to type in.
fix: Replace css-budget.test.ts:50's readdirSync with the recursive walk agent-surface.test.ts:95-102 already provides, charging every sheet under src/app and explicitly subtracting the deferred set by path so an unknown sheet fails loudly rather than costing nothing.
