source: contrast
title: The documented --smoothing fork never reaches the page: tokens.css's own unlayered body rule hard-codes it
why: docs/DESIGN.md's 2026-09-04 Corrections entry ships a four-row table of palette-forked tokens whose last row is `--smoothing | antialiased | auto | body, in globals.css`. globals.css:113 does read it -- but that body rule is inside @layer base (opened at globals.css:91), and tokens.css:958-966 declares an UNLAYERED body { ... -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; ... }. Unlayered author declarations outrank every cascade layer at any specificity, so the hard-coded `antialiased` wins in all four themes and `--smoothing: auto` (tokens.css:456, :610) is dead. The other three rows of the same table do work, because tokens.css's body rule sets no font-weight, so --w-body/--w-row/--w-mono reach the page through --t-body-w. One of four forked tokens is inert, and it is the one whose only consumer is the exact property tokens.css itself hard-codes. The failure is invisible in light (intended value and hard-coded value are both `antialiased`) and degrades dark only -- the palette the whole 2026-09-04 entry exists to fix ("Alec read the console on a dark screen and said the text was hard to read... a glyph drawn light on dark loses apparent stroke width"). The repo has a guard for precisely this cascade hazard, unlayered-cascade.test.ts, but it resolves Tailwind utilities against unlayered author CSS and never considers author-layered against author-unlayered, so this sits in the guard's blind spot.
fix: Change tokens.css:965 to `-webkit-font-smoothing: var(--smoothing);` (or delete the line, since globals.css:113 already declares it), and extend unlayered-cascade.test.ts's premise checks to flag any property declared both unlayered in tokens.css and inside @layer base in globals.css.
note: Every element of this checks out and I could not break it. tokens.css:958-967 is a bare, unlayered `body { ... -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; ... }` -- the first @layer in tokens.css does not appear until line 972, and tokens.css is a plain `import "./tokens.css"` in layout.tsx:4, so nothing wraps it. globals.css:113 reads `-webkit-font-smoothing: var(--smoothing)` inside the @layer base opened at globals.css:92 (the prose says 91; the cited evidence line 113 is correct). Unlayered author declarations outrank every author cascade layer at any specificity -- a rule this repo states verbatim in its own unlayered-cascade.test.ts docstring -- so the hard-coded `antialiased` wins in all four themes and `--smoothing: auto` at tokens.css:456 and :610 is dead. ripgrep confirms those are the only two -webkit-font-smoothing declarations anywhere under src. The DESIGN.md:723 table row `--smoothing | antialiased | auto | body, in globals.css` is real, and the auditor's control is right too: the other three rows survive because tokens.css's body rule sets no font-weight, so --w-body/--w-row/--w-mono reach the page through --t-body-w (I checked --t-body is 13px, matching the hard-coded 13px, so no other property in that rule silently drifts). The guard blind spot is real: unlayered-cascade.test.ts resolves compiled Tailwind utilities against unlayered author CSS and never author-layered-base against author-unlayered. Visually consequential on macOS, where antialiased vs auto is exactly the apparent-stroke-width difference the 2026-09-04 Corrections entry was written to fix, in the one palette it was written for.

source: layout-cliche
title: The 590-line marketing page cannot render: the flag that switches it on also rewrites / away from it
why: Two authorities key off one env var and cancel each other. next.config.ts:16-19 registers a beforeFiles rewrite of / to /site/index.html when SETTERFI_PUBLIC_LANDING_LIVE === "true"; src/app/page.tsx:133 returns <LandingPage> under the same condition. beforeFiles runs ahead of filesystem routes, so with the flag on the static scroll site serves and the React page never mounts; with the flag off page.tsx returns the RolePicker. LandingPage is unreachable in both branches. The repo's own prose confirms the collision rather than resolving it: docs/SETUP.md:209-215 describes the rewrite AND says "With the flag off, / still renders the React landing page in src/app/page.tsx" (it renders the role picker), while public-landing-flag.test.tsx:152 asserts "renders the marketing page when the flag is on" -- true of Home() in jsdom, false of the route. This is the signature of a surface assembled in two passes without either pass reading the other, and it is why the layout tells below are cheap to fix but also why nobody caught them: nothing renders them.
fix: Decide which / is the product's front door. If the scroll site wins, delete src/components/marketing/landing-page.tsx, its test, and the LandingPage branch in page.tsx (plus the landingPlans catalogue read). If the React page wins, drop the rewrite from next.config.ts and correct docs/SETUP.md:209-215. Either way, add an assertion that binds the rewrite and the page branch so one flag cannot mean two things again.
note: Every citation checks out and the collision is real. next.config.ts:16 is exactly `rewrites: async () =>` returning `{ beforeFiles: [{ source: "/", destination: "/site/index.html" }] }` when SETTERFI_PUBLIC_LANDING_LIVE === "true"; src/app/page.tsx:133 is `if (publicLandingLive()) return <LandingPage plans={await landingPlans()} />;` under the identical gate (src/lib/env-contract.ts:575-577 reads the same var, no second flag). beforeFiles overrides filesystem routes, so with the flag on the static site wins and with it off page.tsx returns RolePicker. I grepped every reference to LandingPage: only src/app/page.tsx:133 and its own test file. It renders nowhere. Supporting evidence the auditor missed makes this stronger, not weaker: src/app/public-surfaces.test.ts:29 maps the key "/ (marketing, flagged)" to components/marketing/landing-page.tsx, so a second test suite also believes that file is what / serves; and the docblock at src/app/page.tsx:17-21 claims the flag "went live (2026-09-02, seen in production)" and that the React page's own metadata was the bug being fixed, which cannot be true if the rewrite was already in place. I checked SETUP.md, DESIGN.md (both Corrections entries), REDESIGN-CANVAS.md and the COACH-REDESIGN-PLAYBOOK for any note reconciling the two authorities: there is none. Two citations are softer than presented. docs/SETUP.md:209 anchors the paragraph, not the quoted sentence, which is at :215; and "the React landing page in `src/app/page.tsx`" is ambiguous prose that can be read as "the React page at that path" rather than as a claim about LandingPage. src/app/public-landing-flag.test.tsx:152 is a test file, corroboration rather than the defect. Neither is load-bearing: next.config.ts:16 against src/app/page.tsx:133 settles it alone. Also confirmed: design/coach/ holds 22 .dc.html artboards and Landing.dc.html is not among them anywhere in the repo, so the authority the file cites at line 10 does not exist. High severity stands: a 590-line component, a 250-line test suite and a metadata fork are all dead, and two test suites assert behavior of a route that does not exist.

source: Date, number and locale formatting consistency — no scope owned it, no
title: A documented rounding fix landed in one twin and not the other, so coach KPI tiles print raw floats
why: admin-measurement-view-models.ts:81-89 carries a nine-line docblock describing a shipped defect: "percent used to interpolate the raw number, which was invisible for as long as the console read the stored preview snapshot, because those values were written already rounded. Reading the real projection, a churn rate of one cancellation in twenty-four is 4.166666666666667, and the card printed all seventeen digits and overflowed." The fix is PERCENT_FORMATTER at :90. source: Orphaned dead CSS — named in the audit brief as a tell-adjacent axis,
title: agent-flow.module.css is imported by nothing — 71 lines, and its absence ships the wrong cursor on a canvas that cannot pan
why: The whole 71-line CSS module (.node, .canvas, .pulse, @keyframes haloPulse, a reduced-motion block) has zero importers — `grep -rn "agent-flow.module" src/` returns nothing, and agent-flow.tsx imports @xyflow/react and `@/components/kit/icons` but no stylesheet. It is not merely inert: the two files carry contradictory reasoned comments about the same cursor and the dead one loses silently. The module says 'Panning and zooming are disabled so the graph stays composed; don't offer a grab cursor the canvas won't honour' and sets `cursor: default`; globals.css:1056-1062 sets `cursor: grab` / `:active { grabbing }`. agent-flow.tsx:350-357 passes `panOnDrag={false} panOnScroll={false} zoomOnScroll={false} zoomOnPinch={false}`, so the shipped surface really does advertise a grab handle over a canvas that cannot move. source: motion
title: The entire src/components/motion/ module is unimported dead code, and it is the only place in the repo that implements the scroll-reveal tells
why: `rg 'components/motion' src/ e2e/ scripts/ design/` returns zero matches. Nothing imports this module except its own count-up.test.tsx (L38, `from "./index"`). It is 159 lines exporting five primitives -- CountUp (L82), useDrawIn (L94), useHoverLift (L102), Crossfade (L116), fadeInProps (L140) -- plus a duplicate DURATION/EASE table (tokens.ts). Two of them are gated on `useInView(ref, { once: true })` (L39 amount 0.5, L96 amount 0.4): a figure that counts up when you scroll to it and a bar held at zero until it scrolls into view. That is precisely the scroll-triggered content reveal, and it exists in this repo only here, in code that never renders. `fadeInProps` (L140) is a bare unconditional opacity 0->1 with no reduced-motion path at all, exported for anyone to spread onto anything. Meanwhile the live surfaces have zero scroll-driven motion. The tell is not that these ship -- they don't -- it is that a scroll-reveal library was generated alongside a design system that deliberately has none, and nobody noticed it was never wired up. useHoverLift (L110) also duplicates a gesture the CSS already owns (see the hover-lift pattern) at a different distance and a different clock.
fix: Delete src/components/motion/ (index.tsx, tokens.ts, count-up.test.tsx). If CountUp is genuinely wanted, kit/animated-number.tsx already does digit entry on the --digit-* tokens without a scroll trigger; re-point any future need there. If the module is kept, at minimum drop useDrawIn and the useInView trigger on CountUp so the entrance is tied to mount or to a data change, not to scroll position, and give fadeInProps a useReducedMotion path like Crossfade has.

source: crossvector
tell: arbitrary value bypassing a documented scale
title: 1005 hardcoded pixel font sizes across 33 distinct values against a 16-token scale, including 99 that retype --coach-body
why: DESIGN.md:376 ("The 11px Floor Rule") claims tokens.test.ts "asserts both that floor and the exact count of type tokens (16), so a new size has to be looked at rather than added quietly." 33 distinct sizes ship as `text-[Npx]` literals across 1005 sites — 12.5, 17, 10.5, 18, 19, 21, 25, 26, 27, 28, 34, 38, 40, 52, 72 and 76 among them — so sizes are in fact added quietly; the token count guards the tokens, not the scale. The sharpest instance is on the coach side, where the repo has already been burned by it: coach-type.ts:29-33 explains that COACH_EYEBROW_CLASS "shipped as a text-[12px] literal while coach.css declared --coach-eyebrow: 14px beside it, so ten callers rendered two pixels under a floor SIMPLIFICATION-SPEC §5 calls absolute -- and the drift was invisible because two places held one number and only one of them was ever read. Referencing the token makes a repeat structurally impossible." It is not impossible: --coach-body: 16px (coach.css:26) is retyped as `text-[16px]` 99 times in coach-*.tsx (coach-inbox.tsx alone 17, coach-leads.tsx 15) against 71 uses of COACH_READING_CLASS, which reads the token. coach-type-floor.test.ts only catches sub-14px literals, so the exact two-places-one-number condition its own docblock exists to end is unguarded above the floor. text-[17px] (58) and text-[20px] (42) are the same shape against --coach-row-name and --coach-panel-name; two of those are correctly registered in DELIBERATELY_UNBOUND, the rest are not.
fix: Replace `text-[16px]` in coach-scoped modules with COACH_READING_CLASS (or `text-[length:var(--coach-body)]`), and the same for the 17px and 20px literals that are genuinely the row-name and panel-name roles. Then widen coach-type-floor.test.ts's existing literal scan from `size < 14` to "any literal equal to a declared --coach-* type token's value", which turns the documented lesson into the guard the docblock already claims it is.
note: The counting is very close to exact: 1003 `text-[Npx]` literals across exactly 33 distinct values in non-test .tsx/.ts, and the coach sub-claim is dead on — 99 `text-[16px]` in coach-*.tsx, with coach-inbox.tsx at 17 and coach-leads.tsx at 15, against --coach-body: 16px. The coach-type.ts:28-32 docblock does claim referencing the token makes a repeat "structurally impossible," and coach-type-floor.test.ts really only guards below 14 (`.filter((size) => size < 14)` at :40, `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(14)` at :85 and :96), so the two-places-one-number condition is genuinely unguarded above the floor. Downgraded because: two citations are wrong; COACH_READING_CLASS is used 69 times, not 71; the DESIGN.md rule the auditor calls falsified says only that no `--t-*` token drops below 11px and that the token COUNT is pinned (tokens.test.ts:164 `expect(typeSizes).toHaveLength(16)`) — both of which are true, so "sizes are added quietly" argues against a claim the doc never made; the --t-* console scale and the --coach-* scale are two different scales being conflated; and the visual consequence today is exactly zero, since `text-[16px]` and `var(--coach-body)` render the same pixel. This is a drift-risk finding, not a defect a designer can see.

source: Responsive thresholds are the only design axis in the repo with no tok
tell: two parallel systems for one job with no stated rule for choosing between them
title: Viewport variants (419 uses) and container queries (140 uses) are mixed with no documented rule for which measures what
why: The repo knows the distinction and argues it well in two places — setting-row.tsx:50-53 ('The layout is container-queried, not viewport-queried. The same row renders in a full-width agent config pane and in a 380px drawer') and onboarding-shell.tsx:185-188 ('Named, not bare... an anonymous container would bind them to whichever @container happens to be nearest at runtime'). But nothing writes the rule down where a next author would find it: DESIGN.md and the playbook are silent, and 419 viewport-variant uses (sm 233, max-sm 75, lg 60, md 31, xl 20) sit alongside 131 arbitrary and 9 named container uses with no principle separating them. The cost shows inside single files: owner-brain.tsx queries /mission-row at 640 (line 1042) and /snapshot-row at 560 (line 1182) — two adjacent row types in one page going multi-column 80px apart against two containers, which may be right but is unprovable either way with no rule to check against. Three spellings of the same scale also coexist: `sm:` (640), `@min-[640px]` (onboarding-calendar.tsx:238), and `@media (min-width: 640px)` (coach.css:561).
fix: Add a short section to docs/DESIGN.md stating the rule the two good comments already imply — component-internal reflow is container-queried against a named container, page-level chrome is viewport-queried — and name the canonical spelling for each, so the three ways to write 640 collapse to one per context.

source: There is dead CSS and there are orphaned assets, inside a hard budget
tell: orphaned dead code — modules nothing imports, three of them described in live comments as though they render
title: Seven never-imported modules, 555 lines, under src/components/ — beyond motion/ and the shadcn primitives
why: Resolving every import specifier across src/, e2e/, evals/ and scripts/ against the 272 non-test modules under src/components/ leaves seven unreached, and each was re-confirmed by grepping its exported symbols: escalation-panel.tsx (186 lines; `EscalationPanel` and `escalationClockLabel` each appear exactly once, on their own definition line), review-checklist.tsx (109; `ReviewChecklist` and `ReviewChecklistUntracked`, same), onboarding-stage.tsx (106; `OnboardingStage`), channels.ts (58; `CHANNEL_IDS` and `isProvisioningChannel` appear only on their definitions, and the `CHANNELS` hits elsewhere are an unrelated local const in coach-agent.test.ts), methodology-note.tsx (36; `MethodologyNote`), ui/index.ts (35, the barrel that makes the shadcn primitives look reachable), onboarding-experience.tsx (25; `OnboardingExperience`). These are excluded from the two already-established orphans — motion/ and the eleven shadcn primitives — and ui/index.ts is included because it is the barrel that hides them. What makes this a design finding rather than a housekeeping one is that live code narrates them as real: coach-type.ts:138 says "`escalation-panel.tsx` is the third caller and is an instance of the shape rather than a...", meet-your-agent-contract.test.ts:52 says "the root mounted `onboarding-experience.tsx` and that component decides...", and coach-type.ts:38 reasons about the coach scale arriving "through `OnboardingStage`". Three separate comments reason from the behaviour of components that never mount, so the prose the repo is otherwise scrupulous about is now describing a system that does not exist.
fix: Delete the six leaf modules and either delete ui/index.ts or wire it up as the real import surface. Then fix the three comments that cite them — coach-type.ts:38 and :138 and meet-your-agent-contract.test.ts:52 — so the reasoning names whatever actually carries the scale and the escalation shape today. If any of the six is a staged next feature, move it behind a flag and import it, so the type checker and the guards can see it.

source: The owner console's actual UI implementation — the largest single body
title: Sibling screens in one folder disagree on how to spell the same value and never mix: the colour-utility dialect splits 194/232 cleanly by file, and six shipped screens split 3/3 on how to write 10px
why: The cleanest arithmetic proof in the console that files were written one at a time without reading each other. Colour utilities take two forms — text-[color:var(--x)] (194 uses) and text-[var(--x)] (232) — and the split is by file, not by role: owner-inbox 52/0, owner-system 26/0, owner-brain 20/2, admin-money-tiers 39/0, admin-inbox 12/0 against owner-clients 0/67, owner-overview 0/42, owner-money 0/28, owner-audit 0/20, admin-money-billing 0/17. Nine files pure one way, eight pure the other. The 10px gap is the same with no overlap at all: owner-audit.tsx:216, owner-clients.tsx:804 and owner-money.tsx write gap-2.5; owner-brain.tsx:323, owner-inbox.tsx and owner-overview.tsx write gap-[10px]; not one of the six mixes them. Tailwind v4's (--x) shorthand appears in exactly one console file — admin-money-billing.tsx, 5 times — against 796 bracket forms elsewhere. And the 200-character drawer chrome is pasted four times (admin-money-billing.tsx:565, admin-money-affiliates.tsx:394, admin-money-tiers.tsx:774 and :876) as a byte-identical copy of the string kit/confirm-flow.tsx:559 already owns, with the billing copy the one that drifted to the other syntax. Every one of these renders identically, which is why none was caught; the cost is that no reader can tell a deliberate difference from a typing difference anywhere in this tree.
fix: Pick one dialect per axis and lint it — text-[color:var(--x)] is the safer form since it survives a token whose value is not obviously a colour, and the bracket form is the overwhelming majority. Extract the drawer chrome to a ConsoleDrawer wrapper over SheetContent (confirm-flow.tsx:559 is already that string) and have the three money screens take it.

source: crossvector
tell: arbitrary value bypassing a documented scale
title: 91 off-rung border radii, and the coach deck panel's corner re-typed inline in six files against a rule the repo wrote down by name
why: tokens.css:243-249 declares seven rungs (4/6/8/11/12/14/999) and DESIGN.md §5 adds 9px for buttons and 13px for the strip. 91 radius utilities land off all nine: 37 at 10px (ui/button.tsx:31, toggle-group.tsx:45, select.tsx:359 and 34 more via `min(var(--radius-md),10px)`, which names a token and then reaches past it to a smaller literal), 12 at 7px across the kit atomics (button.tsx:71, field.tsx:183, setting-row.tsx:185, segmented.tsx:54), then 5px, 3px, 2px, 1px, 15px, 16px, 17px, 18px, 20px, 22px, 24px, 32px. Named Tailwind radii are not the problem — rounded-md/lg/xl resolve through @theme to --r-input/--r-card/--r-panel (globals.css:41-44); the arbitrary values are. Worse, the asymmetric "deck panel" corner exists in 20 distinct spellings across 37 uses: 24/24/17/17, 22/22/17/17, 22/22/15/15, 20/20/15/15, 20/20/14/14, 16/16/13/13, 16/16/12/12, 15/15/11/11 and 14/14/11/11 for one panel idea, plus twelve spellings of the message bubble at four sizes and three tail radii (12/4, 13/4, 14/5, 18/6) under a DESIGN.md section that claims the owner inbox and the shared Transcript "draw the same two bubbles". coach.css:60 declares --coach-panel-radius for exactly this and .coach-panel reads it (coach.css:207), yet six files retype the literal (coach-setup.tsx:946, affiliate-home.tsx:72, meet-agent.tsx:274, coach-leads.tsx:635, coach-support-bubble.tsx:305, step-shell.tsx:58). console.css:454 names this failure in the repo's own words: "A pass that instead wrote rounded-[24px_24px_17px_17px] into each screen's class strings is the failure mode the 2026-08-30 craft audit recorded -- seven lanes, nine class strings, slightly different values, all of it visible to the reader." That is the state of the code, and it breaks DESIGN.md §5's "Reach for the recipe rather than re-rolling a card inline -- the failure this system was previously graded down for was not missing craft but unadopted craft."
fix: Point the six hand-rolled PANEL_CLASS strings at DeckPanel/.coach-panel, or at minimum `rounded-[var(--coach-panel-radius)]` as landing-page.tsx:80 and optin-artifact.tsx:134 already do. Collapse the nine deck variants onto the two tokens that exist (--coach-panel-radius, --console-tile-radius) and the twelve bubble spellings onto one. Then extend token-references.test.ts, which already walks the --r-* family, to reject a `rounded-[Npx]` whose N is not a declared rung.
note: The strongest sub-claim verifies perfectly: all six retypes of `rounded-[24px_24px_17px_17px]` exist at the exact lines given (coach-setup.tsx:946, affiliate-home.tsx:72, meet-agent.tsx:274, coach-leads.tsx:635, coach-support-bubble.tsx:305, step-shell.tsx:58) while coach.css:60 declares --coach-panel-radius and coach.css:207 reads it, and console.css:454 does name this exact failure in the repo's own words, verbatim. The radius bulk is roughly right: 82 off-rung radius utilities in non-test .tsx (62 single-value + 20 multi-value carrying an off-rung number), rising to ~100 with the .css files. But three things are wrong or unfair. (1) "34 more via min(var(--radius-md),10px)" is false — that construction occurs 4 times total, in 3 files; the 10px total is 33 direct + 4 min = 37, so the headline number survives but the stated mechanism does not. (2) Several of the "20 spellings" are declared tokens, not drift: 24/24/17/17 is --coach-panel-radius (coach.css:60), 30/30/17/17 is --coach-panel-radius-hero (:61), and 15/15/11/11 is --console-tile-radius (console.css:476) — the auditor lists that last one as evidence of re-rolling. (3) Four of the six retypes are structurally forced and the repo documents why: .coach-panel is scoped `[data-shell-role="coach"]` (coach.css:203), and step-shell (onboarding), affiliate-home, meet-agent (also mounted in the admin eval playground) and coach-support-bubble all mount outside that root, where the token resolves to nothing — the same trap coach-type.ts:157-163 spells out. Visually, every value agrees today; a designer sees nothing.

source: contrast
title: --overline is under AA on every ground it is actually drawn on, in dark only
why: tokens.css:458 and :612 annotate the dark --overline with a bare "4.8" -- one unqualified number. Every role above it on the same ramp carries two grounds ("17.1 on canvas / 16.0 on card"). 4.8 is the canvas figure, and canvas is the one ground this role is essentially never drawn on. Measured against the grounds it IS drawn on, dark oklch(0.5871 0.0471 261.6) gives: card-top 4.17, --raised (drawer/popover face) 4.17, --well 4.42, card 4.52, rail stops 4.52/4.70. Composited films are worse: --row-hover over card-top 3.98, --band over card 3.96, --band over card-top 3.59. docs/DESIGN.md:354 defines the Overline as "mono 500, 9.5px, 0.09em, uppercase, --overline" and overline-size.test.ts pins that size, so this is the smallest text in the product and squarely 1.4.3 small text at a 4.5:1 floor. The light block's identical bare "4.8" (tokens.css:124/819) is the WORST case there -- light measures 4.80 canvas up to 5.33 card-top -- so the same annotation is a floor in one palette and a ceiling in the other, and the failure exists only in dark. tokens-contrast.test.ts never measures --overline in either base palette; it appears only in the drench table (line 528), where console.css:634 correctly lifts it to oklch(0.9 0.012 265). The role is guarded exactly where it is not broken.
fix: Lift dark --overline from oklch(0.5871 0.0471 261.6) to about L=0.605 in tokens.css:458 and :612, which puts --band over --card-top at ~4.5 and every flat ground at 4.8+; then add --overline (and the row-hover / band films) to the base-palette assertions in tokens-contrast.test.ts so the ground it is drawn on, not the ground it is annotated against, is what is pinned.
note: All five citations verified as real shipped code (tokens.css:458 and :612 are the dark --overline declarations with the bare "4.8"; grid-table.tsx:103, type.tsx:30 and app-shell.tsx:317 all paint --overline). I reproduced every number to 0.01 with the repo's own srgb()/over()/contrast() math: dark --overline measures card-top 4.17, raised 4.17, well 4.42, card 4.52, canvas 4.81, pane 4.73, band-over-card 3.96, band-over-card-top 3.59, row-hover-over-card-top 3.98; light measures canvas 4.80 up to card-top 5.33. So the annotation really is a floor in light and a ceiling in dark, and the coverage gap is real -- tokens-contrast.test.ts carries --overline only in the drench table (line 528), never in the base palettes, and console.css:634 explicitly classes --overline as "text, so it holds AA", which is the repo's own stated floor. BUT the headline claim is false on the auditor's own figures: --overline CLEARS 4.5 on --canvas (4.81), --pane (4.73), --card (4.52) and both rail stops (4.52/4.70). It is not "under AA on every ground it is actually drawn on" -- it is under AA on card-top/raised/well and on the composited band and row-hover films, roughly three of seven real grounds, and the worst realistic case (4.17 on the lit top stop of a card, where surface.tsx:186 and metric-card.tsx:84 do put eyebrows) is a 7% shortfall. Severity downgraded from high to medium: the intent-vs-measurement inconsistency is genuine and documented against the repo's own rule, but the visible deficit is marginal and palette-and-ground dependent, not universal.

source: icons
title: strokeWidth is a no-op on every Phosphor-backed kit icon, yet 42 call sites pass one in four different values
why: icons.tsx:121-122 states the contract outright: "`size` and `className` stay open ... weight and colour are not adjustable at all." The wrapper enforces it by spreading `{...rest}` first and then hard-setting `weight="regular"` (icons.tsx:129-137), and Phosphor's regular weight draws a filled path - icons.test.tsx:30 and :50 both assert the rendered svg carries fill=currentColor, and the module's own stroke assertions (icons.test.tsx:69, "draws %s on the 16px grid at 1.5 stroke") apply only to the six bespoke marks, never to a Phosphor glyph. So a `strokeWidth` prop rides `{...rest}` onto an svg where nothing is stroked and changes nothing. 42 call sites across 13 files pass one anyway, and not at one value: 1.75 (app-topbar.tsx:508, app-sidebar.tsx:555), 2 (connect-channel-sheet.tsx:470), 2.25 (coach-setup.tsx:1007), 2.5 (connect-channel-sheet.tsx:430, :607). Four intended weights, all inert. This is lucide syntax that survived the migration by copy-paste: authors believed they were tuning icon weight surface by surface, the render never moved, and nobody noticed - which is precisely the 'generated, not decided' signature. app-topbar.tsx alone carries 14 of them.
fix: Delete strokeWidth from all 42 kit-icon call sites - they are dead props. To stop it recurring, drop `strokeWidth` from KitIconProps by narrowing the type from `Omit<SVGProps<SVGSVGElement>, "ref">` to an explicit prop set (className, size, label, aria-*), so a stroke prop on a Phosphor glyph becomes a type error instead of silent no-op.

source: The owner console's actual UI implementation — the largest single body
title: One card face, five paddings and nine radius spellings: rounded-[14px] x17 against rounded-[var(--r-card)] x4, with --d-card-p spent by no console screen
why: tokens.css:243-249 declares seven radii with a role each; tokens.css:286 declares --d-card-p: 16px as 'card padding'. Across the 23 files the radius reaches a token 9 times and is written as a literal or Tailwind alias 31 times: rounded-[14px] x17 (the literal for --r-card, which admin-support.tsx:253 correctly writes as rounded-[var(--r-card)] on the same shape), rounded-[11px] x6 (--r-well), rounded-[8px] and rounded-lg (--r-chip, two spellings), rounded-md x2 and rounded-[6px] x2 (--r-input, two spellings), rounded-sm x2 (--r-control), plus rounded-[10px] x4, rounded-[3px] x2 and rounded-[2px] which map to no token at all. The padding on the identical card face — same rounded-[14px], same border-[var(--line)], same bg-[var(--card)] — takes five values across two sibling screens: owner-overview.tsx:588 px-[18px] py-[16px]; owner-overview.tsx:644 and :683 px-[20px] py-[18px]; owner-system.tsx:313 px-5 py-4 (20/16 in Tailwind's vocabulary); owner-system.tsx:565 p-[18px_20px]; owner-clients.tsx:804 p-[16px_18px], which inverts owner-overview:588's axes. Three of the five are off the 4px grid. --d-card-p is read by no file in this tree. A reader moving between Overview and System sees the same card breathe differently with no way to tell which is intended.
fix: One card recipe. The kit already holds the shape at callout.tsx:48 (rounded-[var(--r-card)] + p-[var(--d-card-p)]); promote it to a Surface/Card export and have the console screens take it. Where a screen genuinely needs a looser card, that is a second named padding token, not a sixth literal.

source: Orphaned dead CSS — named in the audit brief as a tell-adjacent axis,
title: Bulk-imported motion token dump: 37 of 104 never read, 24 of them re-declared a second time in the reduced-motion block
why: The section header at tokens.css:296 states the provenance outright: 'Motion tokens, copied from .agents/skills/transitions-dev/_root.css'. Copied, not chosen — and it shows. Of the 104 tokens declared between :297 and :404, 37 are never read by any var() in any stylesheet and never named in any .ts/.tsx (checked with an underscore-tolerant boundary so Tailwind's `[animation:kit-shake_var(--shake-dur)]` forms are correctly counted as reads). Whole named groups are dead end to end, not stragglers: accordion (--acc-expand/-collapse/-chevron/-ease, :369-372), toggle (all six, :381-386), text-swap (all four, :394-397), pulse (all three, :352-354), and the shipped easing vocabulary is largely unused (--ease-linear, --ease-bounce, --ease-bounce-strong at :309-311). The cost is doubled because 24 of the 37 are re-declared a second time in globals.css's reduced-motion block at :1856-1935 to be zeroed — so every dead accordion, toggle and text-swap token is two maintained lines in two files, and that block's own careful comments ('Durations alone are not enough...') are explaining why values nothing consumes must be collapsed. Compare the one place the file does show a decision: :404, 'Row hover is deliberately instant; nothing reads from a token here on purpose.' That line proves the author can tell a decision from a default — the 37 are what happens when a whole file gets pasted instead.
fix: Delete the 37 unread declarations from tokens.css and their 24 mirrors in the globals.css reduced-motion block. That is 61 lines off the two budgeted sheets. If any group is a deliberate forward-looking API (the accordion set, say), keep it and say so in one line the way :404 does, so the next audit does not re-flag it.

source: Disabled and inactive states are drawn by fading the element, at three
tell: tell 14 (the visual affordance and the pointer affordance were written by different passes)
title: 31 of 43 disabled sites fade with no cursor change, and 3 declare cursor-not-allowed where pointer-events-none makes it unreachable
why: Only 12 of the 43 fade sites pair disabled:cursor-not-allowed, and the split is not semantic - it is exactly the shadcn form-control set (checkbox, command, input, label, select, switch, textarea) plus five coach files, while every button base fades with no cursor at all. Worse, three sites declare both disabled:pointer-events-none and disabled:cursor-not-allowed on the same class string - input.tsx:12, label.tsx:12, select.tsx:359 - where pointer-events-none suppresses hover entirely, so the not-allowed cursor can never render. That is stacked boilerplate, not a decision: two mutually exclusive affordances shipped together because both appear in upstream snippets. Meanwhile ui/input.tsx:12 and ui/textarea.tsx:10 stack THREE disabled treatments at once (disabled:bg-input/50 + disabled:opacity-50 + dark:disabled:bg-input/80), double-fading the placeholder, while ui/toggle.tsx:9 and ui/tabs.tsx:102 fade with neither cursor nor background change.
fix: Pick one rule and encode it in the shared bases only: pointer-events-none on anything that is genuinely inert (it already blocks hover, so drop the paired cursor-not-allowed at input.tsx:12, label.tsx:12, select.tsx:359), and cursor-not-allowed only on the wrapper label of a control that stays hoverable - which is what kit/matrix-checkbox.tsx:61 already does correctly with has-[:disabled]:cursor-not-allowed.

source: Responsive thresholds are the only design axis in the repo with no tok
tell: citations to a pixel authority that does not resolve — the traceability is asserted rather than checkable
title: 33 of 54 cited .dc.html artboards do not exist, including the one that anchors the repo's single reasoned breakpoint
why: design/coach/ holds 22 .dc.html files; src/ cites 54 distinct artboard filenames, of which 33 are not on disk anywhere (verified by find across the whole tree) — CoachHomeMobile, MeetYourAgent, CoachError, CoachSetup, Landing, Login, Affiliate, AdminOverview, AdminRevenue, AdminPlans, Consumer*, EyeRule, Redesign and 20 more. This lands on the responsive axis directly: coach.css:622 justifies the one breakpoint in the repo that argues from the canvas — the 639/640 phone line — with '60px, which CoachHomeMobile.dc.html:62 draws', and CoachHomeMobile.dc.html does not exist. The real mobile artboard is HomeMobile.dc.html, whose line 62 is a --primary-shadow custom property. To the repo's credit the *value* survives: HomeMobile.dc.html:243-247 genuinely draws 60px tab targets, so the number is right and the artboard agrees with the code. What is broken is the chain — the artboards were renamed (Coach* prefix dropped) and line numbers drifted, and ~200 citation sites were not updated, so every 'the canvas draws this' claim now has to be re-derived by hand. tokens.css:4 names Redesign.dc.html as the source the whole token set was extracted from, and that file is gone too.
fix: Rewrite the stale citations to the surviving filenames and current line numbers (CoachHomeMobile→HomeMobile with :243 for the 60px tabs, and the same for the other 32), then add a test in the style of container-queries.test.ts asserting every `*.dc.html` string in src/ resolves to a file in design/coach/ — cheap to write and it pins the pixel-authority chain the same way the contrast suite pins ratios.

source: public/site/ — the page actually served at `/` in production — was in
title: A second full design system ships on the production route, is then bypassed, and the replacement drifts 33 values off the product's own grid
why: scrollcraft.css:18-93 declares a complete parallel token system on the same page tokens.css governs: six colour roles, three font families, an eight-step clamp() type ramp (:37-44), four tracking values (:46-49), three leading values (:51-53), an eleven-step spacing scale (:58-60), four radii (:68), three elevation rungs (:74-80), three easings and three durations (:87-90). index.html:14-32 overrides eight of those, and reads only four --sc-* variables in the entire 1031-line file (--sc-accent x7, --sc-accent-ink x2, --sc-font-display x4, --sc-font-text x1). The type ramp, spacing scale, radius scale, elevation scale, easing set and duration set are all unread. Only three sc-* classes appear in the markup (sc-world, sc-world__seg, sc-world__scrim), so the entire typography layer (.sc-display, .sc-lede, .sc-body, .sc-label), the entire layout layer (.sc-wrap, .sc-section, .sc-stack, .sc-rule) and all seven scrim variants are inapplicable. The page re-declares its own ramp and rhythm in 450 lines of inline <style> instead -- and the replacement does not land on the product's grid. tokens.css:238 heads the scale '---- Spacing (4px grid) ----' and :291 states 'Each step aliases a --s-* rung so the rhythm cannot drift off the 4px grid'. Excluding the three device mocks (Chrome/Calendar, iOS/Messenger, Meta), SetterFi's own surfaces carry 29 off-rung spacing declarations -- 18px x8, 22px x5, 10px x4, 14px x4, plus 3, 7, 9, 26, 44 -- concentrated in .card/.tl (index.html:328, 331, 340, 341, 343, 349), .cta (:364, :365), .copy/.foot (:406, :417, :421) and .nav (:435, :439). Four radii are off tokens.css:243-249's scale of 4/6/8/11/12/14/999: 16px on .console (:255) and .card (:320), 10px (:337) and 30px (:367). The 16px card radius is particularly telling next to --r-card:14px on a block whose own comment claims 'Product-console styling'.
fix: Two separable jobs. (1) Strip scrollcraft.css's token block down to the values this page actually reads, or accept it as vendored and stop treating it as a floor. (2) Snap the SetterFi-authored blocks onto the rungs: 18 -> 16 or 20, 22 -> 24, 10 -> 12 or 8, 14 -> 16, and set .console/.card radius to var(--r-card) 14px. Leave the three device mocks alone -- their off-grid values are fidelity to Google, Apple and Meta chrome and are correct as they stand.

source: shadcn
title: src/components/ui/ is stock shadcn; the real adapted kit is a separate folder
why: 34 of 35 styled primitives carry ZERO repo color tokens. Measured shadcn-vocabulary references vs repo-token references per file: sidebar 52/0, button 35/1, dropdown-menu 31/0, badge 24/1, checkbox 15/0, tabs 14/0, file-upload 14/0, field 13/0, input 12/0, switch 12/0, textarea 11/0, toggle 11/0, input-group 11/0. The only repo tokens appearing anywhere outside select.tsx are a single var(--critical-text) in button.tsx:25 and badge.tsx:16, and one var(--s-4) in dropdown-menu.tsx:64. Meanwhile src/components/kit/atomics/ is the exact inverse: 14 files, ZERO shadcn references, 100% repo tokens, with paragraph-length reasoning comments (button-class.ts:7-15 explains why the three heights are 26/30/34px because 'the artifact draws exactly these three'). So somebody genuinely did the design work, in kit/. The ui/ folder was shadcn-add-ed and never opened. docs/ENGINEERING-BRIEF.md:39 states the rule the folder breaks verbatim: 'themed to SetterFi tokens (src/app/tokens.css). Never ship stock shadcn styling.' This is not dead code either: ui/button is imported in 46 places, ui/input 21, ui/select 15, ui/dropdown-menu 13, ui/textarea 12, ui/sheet 10.
fix: Treat kit/atomics as the target vocabulary and port ui/ primitive-by-primitive, highest import count first (button, input, select, dropdown-menu, textarea, sheet). For each, replace bg-primary/text-primary-foreground -> --accent-fill/--on-accent, border-input -> --line, text-muted-foreground -> --muted, bg-popover -> --raised, bg-card -> --card. Where a kit/atomics equivalent already exists (button, field, progress, segmented, surface), delete the ui/ twin and re-point imports rather than porting.
note: Real but materially inflated. VERIFIED: ui/ has exactly 35 non-test .tsx primitives; kit/atomics/ has exactly 14 .tsx files with ZERO shadcn-vocabulary hits (I grepped bg-primary|text-muted-foreground|border-input|bg-popover|rounded-lg|... across all of them: zero matches) and 100% repo tokens, so the inverse claim holds. ENGINEERING-BRIEF.md:39 is verbatim ('SetterFi tokens (`src/app/tokens.css`). Never ship stock shadcn styling.'). The shadcn-vocabulary counts are near-exact (my census: button 35, badge 24, dropdown-menu 30, sidebar 46, input 12, switch 12, textarea 11, toggle 11, input-group 11 -- auditor within 1-6 on every one). WRONG: (1) 'ZERO repo color tokens in 34 of 35' -- true number is 32 of 35; select.tsx, button.tsx and badge.tsx all carry repo color tokens. (2) 'The only repo tokens outside select.tsx are --critical-text x2 and one --s-4' is false: 10 files outside select.tsx reference repo tokens (button 14 refs, sidebar 10, dropdown-menu 10, dialog 8, alert-dialog 8, sheet 6, popover 5, checkbox 5, tabs 4, badge 1). (3) 'shadcn-add-ed and never opened' is contradicted by evidence in the same folder: checkbox.tsx:15 carries a hand-written two-beat animation comment on --check-box/--check-ease, button.tsx:7-12 a six-line motion rationale, select.tsx a 260-line hand-authored overloaded API, and the sizes are non-stock (h-8 default, xs/icon-xs/icon-sm rungs). (4) Import counts inflated: button 40 not 46, input 18 not 21, textarea 11 not 12, sheet 9 not 10 (select is 16, one MORE than claimed). (5) Most important: globals.css's @theme inline maps every shadcn color utility onto repo tokens, so these primitives DO render in the SetterFi palette -- 'zero repo tokens in the file' is not 'stock colors on screen'. What actually survives is geometry and focus, i.e. pattern 2, not a whole-folder color failure. button-class.ts's height comment is at lines 6-10, not 7-15.

source: public/site/ — the page actually served at `/` in production — was in
title: The engine ships whole to drive one segment: 28 of 39 attributes and ~42% of its JavaScript are unreachable, and nothing in the repo's eight-test enforcement suite can see the file served at /
why: index.html applies 11 data-sc-* attributes, all in the worldflight family, to one segment with no video and no clip. The engine registers 28 more that can never fire here. Whole sections are dead on arrival: collect-acts (scrollcraft.js:318-416, 99 lines, zero [data-sc-act] on the page), text splitting for kinetic type (:206-266, 61), number formatting and entry counters (:267-280 and :511-551, 55), flow reveals via IntersectionObserver (:488-510, 23 -- tell 12), video and clip priming (:623-681, 59), image sequence (:682-713, 32), the video seek loop (:989-1092, 104), and pointer devices (:1093-1152, 60 -- tell 13). That is roughly 515 of 1211 lines, 42%, on the marketing critical path at 58KB raw / 18KB gzipped, plus 20KB of stylesheet whose entire device layer is inapplicable. The engine even keeps writing a scale() transform every frame to the empty hidden placeholder at index.html:479 (scrollcraft.js:766-768), because s.clip is null and op is always ~1. The compounding problem is that no test covers any of it: src/app/glow-budget.test.ts:26, em-dash.test.ts, measures.test.ts, css-budget.test.ts:16 and token-references.test.ts:82-83 are every one of them rooted at src/, so the eight guards this repo built to pin the glow budget, token references, overline sizes, measures and punctuation have zero reach over the file next.config.ts:16-19 serves at /. docs/platform-diagram/EVIDENCE.md:31 confirms nobody has actually looked: it records GET / with the flag ON as returning title 'SetterFi -- your funding DMs answered, qualified and booked' and body text about plans not loading, which is src/app/page.tsx's React landing page. The real title at index.html:6 is 'SetterFi. The AI setter for funding coaches.' The repo's own evidence record describes the wrong page for its own production route.
fix: Two independent fixes. (1) Ship a trimmed engine build for this page -- the worldflight path plus layout and wiring is roughly 400 lines -- or accept the payload and say so in a comment at the top of index.html. (2) More important: point at least token-references.test.ts, glow-budget.test.ts and em-dash.test.ts at public/site/ with raw-CSS patterns alongside the Tailwind ones, and re-run the / row in docs/platform-diagram/EVIDENCE.md against the page actually served.

source: Entire product surfaces cite pixel authority that was never drawn — th
tell: prose that asserts provenance the file cannot have
title: Auth, landing and the agent preview declare missing artboards to be the authority for values that were chosen in code
why: Three surfaces state the claim in its strongest form. landing-page.tsx:10: '`Landing.dc.html` on the redesign canvas is the authority for every word and every measurement here.' auth-shell.tsx:202 and :213 justify inline styles — chosen specifically to outrank the cascade, i.e. the highest-commitment form of a value — against 'the login artboard's 28px/600/-0.02em/1.15 title (`Login.dc.html:74`)' and 'the artboard's `15px` header padding (`Login.dc.html:72`)'. coach-agent-preview.tsx spends 10 citations on MeetYourAgent.dc.html for tone assignments (:182, :206), a chip recipe (:206: 'The radius and the padding are the artboard's; the size is not'), and three button recipes given to the pixel (:223/:231 '48px, `0 20px`, radius 11, 16px', :239 '56px, `0 20px`, radius 12, 17px'). None of these files exists. The tell is sharpest where the same comment reasons *about* the drawing's authority: coach-agent-preview.tsx:18 argues that building `MeetYourAgent.dc.html` literally 'would have deleted working admin capability to conform to a canvas that is still unsigned' — a careful judgement about a document nobody in the repo can open. auth-shell.tsx:201-205 is the self-aware version: it records that a previous audit 'recorded "Code: 28px" off the class string and was wrong ... a dead declaration reads exactly like a live one'. A citation to a nonexistent artboard is the same failure one level up — an unverifiable provenance reads exactly like a verified one.
fix: Downgrade the claim to what is true. landing-page.tsx:10 should say the 2026-09-01 artifact canvas informed the page and that no working file exists to check against. auth-shell.tsx:202/:213 should keep the inline styles (the cascade argument is sound and independent) but attribute the 28px title and 15px band to whoever chose them. coach-agent-preview.tsx should keep its recipes and drop the eleven line numbers, or export MeetYourAgent from the published artifact into design/ so they resolve.

source: Orphaned dead CSS — named in the audit brief as a tell-adjacent axis,
title: public/site/scrollcraft.css ships a second, unused design system — 24 of 41 classes dead, and the one page that loads it re-implements them locally
why: public/site/index.html:12 is the only thing that loads this sheet, and it uses almost none of it — it consumes the `data-sc-*` attribute API and then defines its own `.copy`, `.copy--hero`, `.copy--night`, `.over`, `.scrim-top` in an inline <style> at index.html:65-389. The result is that 24 of the sheet's 41 classes have no reference in index.html or scrollcraft.js: the entire typography layer (.sc-display + --xl/--lg/--md, .sc-lede, .sc-body, .sc-label, :135-162, 28 lines), the entire layout layer (.sc-wrap, .sc-section, .sc-stack x3, .sc-rule, :165-172), the .sc-copy family (:253-263), six of the seven .sc-scrim variants (:211-246 — only --band is live, written by scrollcraft.js:80), and .sc-grain (:380-386). About 82 rule lines of a 432-line sheet, 19%. Two details make it dead rather than merely optional-library-surface. First, `.sc-stage__poster` (:186, :195, :196) is a stale pre-rename twin of the live `.sc-world__poster` (:341, :347, :413) — same job, same comment energy ('The poster is a live frame-holder, not a placeholder'), one of them wired up. Second, the responsive block at the bottom spends nine more lines re-overriding dead selectors: :418 `.sc-copy`, :419 `.sc-copy--trail`, and :425-431 re-declaring the whole `.sc-scrim--trail` gradient with a four-line comment explaining the contrast failure it prevents on a class nothing wears. Thirteen `--sc-*` tokens (--sc-t-4xl/-3xl/-2xl/-lg/-xs, --sc-measure, --sc-maxw, --sc-section, --sc-4, --sc-7, --sc-track-tight, --sc-track-wide, --sc-leading-none) have exactly one reader each and that reader is a dead rule, so the scale tails off with them.
fix: Decide whether scrollcraft.css is a reusable engine or this page's stylesheet. If it is this page's: delete the typography (:134-162), layout (:164-172), .sc-copy (:248-263), the five unused scrim variants, .sc-grain (:377-386), .sc-stage__poster (:195-196 and the `.sc-stage__poster` term in the :is() at :186), the mobile overrides at :418-419 and :425-431, and the 13 orphaned --sc-* tokens. If it is an engine, move it out of public/ into a source location, and pull index.html's local .copy/.over/.scrim-top onto the engine's classes so one of the two systems actually wins.

source: motion
title: The motion block is the only part of tokens.css with no design-canvas authority: it cites a skill file that is not in the repo, and 24 of its ~56 tokens are referenced zero times
why: tokens.css:296 labels the block "Motion tokens, copied from .agents/skills/transitions-dev/_root.css". That path does not exist in the repo, and none of the 22 approved canvases in design/coach/*.dc.html contains a single `transition`, `animation` or `@keyframes` (rg exits 1 on all three). Every other value in tokens.css is extracted from the canvas with a measured justification; the motion scale alone was pasted in wholesale from a generic external library. The symptom is that nearly half of it was never needed. Zero references anywhere in src/: the entire toggle group (--toggle-dur, --toggle-travel, --toggle-ov1, --toggle-ov2, --toggle-track, --toggle-ease, L381-386), the entire text-swap group (L394-397), the entire skeleton-pulse group (--pulse-dur, --pulse-count, --pulse-min, L352-354), three of the seven duration rungs (--duration-micro L299, --duration-medium L302, --duration-very-slow L304), three of six easings (--ease-linear L309, --ease-bounce L310, --ease-bounce-strong L311), --distance-medium/-large (L316-317), --scale-large/-medium/-tiny (L319-322), --blur-medium/-large (L325-326), --check-delay/-uncheck (L390-391). And globals.css's reduced-motion block then dutifully collapses 18 of these phantom tokens (L1878, L1889-1894, L1909-1920, L1930-1936) -- maintenance on values nothing reads. The tightest proof this was pasted rather than derived: --pulse-dur:1000ms was minted for the skeleton loader, and the skeleton shimmer at globals.css:1473 hardcodes `1.3s` instead.
fix: Delete the 24 unreferenced tokens and their 18 lines in the reduced-motion block; keep the 32 the product actually reads. Point globals.css:1473 at var(--pulse-dur) if the pulse group is kept, or drop it. Replace the tokens.css:296 provenance comment with the real one: this scale is authored, not canvas-derived, and here is why each rung exists.

source: There is dead CSS and there are orphaned assets, inside a hard budget
tell: orphaned dead code — colour roles forked across every palette block and spent nowhere, two of them pinned by the contrast suite
title: Five colour roles are declared in all four theme blocks (two of them in six), carry measured contrast ratios in their comments, and no element reads any of them
why: `--dim` is declared six times (tokens.css 125, 459, 613, 820; coach.css 1090; console.css 635), `--info-wash` six times (tokens.css 213, 541, 695, 908; coach.css 1144; console.css 729), and `--negative`, `--neutral-line` and `--slot-on` four times each — once per theme block, exactly the discipline the system asks for. Not one of the 24 declarations is ever read: no `var(--dim)`, `var(--slot-on)`, `var(--negative)`, `var(--neutral-line)` or `var(--info-wash)` exists anywhere in src/, in any stylesheet or any Tailwind arbitrary value. Several carry measured ratios in their comments — coach.css:1090 reads `/* 3.52 / 8.4 -- shape floor, 1.4.11 */`, tokens.css:201 reads `/* 3.99 canvas / 4.34 card / 4.43 card-top */` — measurements of contrast between a value and a ground it never meets. The contrast suite then pins two of them: tokens-contrast.test.ts:291 asserts "keeps the --negative dash visible as a shape on --$ground" and :740 puts --dim in SHAPE_ROLES, so the repo has green tests measuring the legibility of marks nothing draws. The third is louder still — state-palette.test.ts:37 asserts a block does *not* match `--info-wash`, so one token's only mention outside its declarations is a test insisting it stay unused. That is a palette generated to be complete and then partly abandoned, with the ceremony (four-block fork, measured comment, pinned ratio) applied uniformly to the live roles and the dead ones alike.
fix: Delete --slot-on (tokens.css 146, 480, 634, 841) and --neutral-line (220, 548, 702, 915) outright — 8 lines, no test references them. For --dim, --negative and --info-wash, decide first: if the shape roles are meant to be spent by a component that was never built, either build it or drop the role and the tokens-contrast.test.ts assertions that pin it (279-295, 364-376, 735-740); leaving a measured token nobody spends is what makes the next reader trust a ratio that guards nothing. Also drop --d-page-x (285), which no surface reads.

source: Every design guard in the repo roots its scan at src/ or narrower, so
title: The CSS cap was raised twice by documented ruling while ~20 dead rules sit inside the sheets it counts
why: css-budget.test.ts:7-14 records two rulings: 2,500 -> 3,000 for the pass-2 token expansion, then 3,000 -> 3,100 on 2026-09-04 because 'the two stylesheets stood at 2,999 against the 3,000 cap, so a fix... could not land at all without moving the number', and insists 'The 100 buys the fork and its comments and nothing else; it is not headroom for a new surface.' The sheets now measure 3,076, leaving 24 lines. Inside those 3,076 lines are rules no markup names: globals.css:1451-1484 is a complete agent-loading skeleton (.agent-loading, .skeleton, .skeleton::after, .loading-topbar, .loading-panels, .loading-heading, .loading-message, .loading-message--wide, .loading-composer, .loading-trace, .loading-receipt) plus its @media companions at :1492-1503 and :1843-1844 -- a repo-wide grep for those class names returns nothing outside globals.css and one comment in ui/select.test.ts:61; .admin-version at :467 and :1747-1755 likewise; and tokens.css:1002,1005,1006,1012,1014,1109 declare .t-metric, .t-money, .t-transcript, .t-th, .t-count and .t-hero, plus .i-sm/.i-lg, none of which appears in any .ts/.tsx in the tree. That is more dead lines than the remaining headroom, so the second ruling bought space the sheets already held. The guard measures lines, not liveness, which is why it could not say so. Two smaller tells sit in the same file: the assertion's own name at :49 still reads 'below 3,000 lines' after the constant at :15 became 3_100, and the comment at :31 says coach.css is deferred 'for the same reason as the two above' when consumer.css is the only entry above it -- the second was removed with onboarding.css and the sentence was not re-counted.
fix: Delete the dead blocks (globals.css:1451-1484 and its two media companions, :467/:1747-1755, tokens.css's six unused .t-* and two .i-* utilities), then lower APP_CSS_BUDGET to the new total plus a stated allowance. Add a second assertion that every class selector in the counted sheets is named somewhere in the tree, so the budget measures live CSS. Fix the :49 title to name the real cap and re-count :31's 'two above'.

source: There is dead CSS and there are orphaned assets, inside a hard budget
title: The type scale ships a full set of roles: 9 of the 26 .t-* classes are worn by nothing, and coach.css re-authors five of the dead ones at a second size
why: `.t-metric` (1002), `.t-section` (1003), `.t-money` (1005), `.t-transcript` (1006), `.t-nav` (1010), `.t-th` (1012), `.t-badge` (1013), `.t-count` (1014) and `.t-hero` (1109) return zero matches as class tokens anywhere in src/ — the loose greps that appear to hit them are all matching the `--t-*` custom properties, which are a separate, live mechanism. Their siblings in the same run (.t-title, .t-row, .t-body, .t-muted, .t-faint, .t-overline, .t-id, .t-page-title, .t-label, .t-figure, .t-mono-meta, .t-mono-crumb) are all worn, which is what makes the nine read as fill rather than omission: a scale written out complete, then used where it was needed. `.t-hero` is the clearest case — tokens.css:1108 documents it as "One hero figure per page, Overview only: the number the owner opens the page for," and no page anywhere renders it. The same shape repeats in two other forms: `svg.i.i-sm` and `svg.i.i-lg` (995-996) size an icon variant nothing requests, though the base `svg.i` at 994 is used everywhere; and globals.css:75-77 declares `--text-nav`/`--text-nav--line-height`/`--text-nav--font-weight` inside `@theme inline`, generating a Tailwind `text-nav` utility that appears in zero class strings — the nav role is dead in both its class form and its utility form. The compounding tell is coach.css:1682, where a carefully specificity-reasoned `:is(.t-faint, .t-nav, .t-overline, .t-th, .t-badge, .t-count, .t-id)` re-authors four dead members out of seven, and 1677's `:is(.t-body, .t-muted, .t-transcript)` re-authors a fifth — a second sheet was written to override classes nobody wears.
fix: Delete tokens.css lines 995-996, 1002, 1003, 1005, 1006, 1010, 1012, 1013, 1014 and 1109, and globals.css lines 75-77. Trim .t-transcript from coach.css:1677 and .t-nav, .t-th, .t-badge, .t-count from coach.css:1682, keeping the live members and the specificity comment above them. If a role is genuinely wanted for a future screen, it belongs in DESIGN.md as prose, not in the sheet as a rule the budget charges for.

source: icons
tell: mixed 14/16/18px sizes across the same surface
title: Icon boxes land on arbitrary off-ladder values (15, 17, 21, 22, 26px) that match neither authority
why: Both authorities name a single default: icons.tsx:104 sets KIT_ICON_SIZE = 16 and icons.tsx:110 permits deviation only where "a caller has a specific reason -- an empty-state glyph, say"; VOCABULARY.md:71 sets 20 with one documented exception (24 in the bubble and phone tabs). Shipped icon boxes instead run 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 20, 21, 22, 24, 26, 28. The sanctioned exceptions account for the 24s and 28s (empty states, the bubble). What they do not account for are the sixteen instances at 15, 17, 21, 22 and 26 - values on no rung of either system and off the 4px grid tokens.css:291 pins for the spacing scale. onboarding-connect.tsx:34-36 sets all three channel tiles to size-[21px]; account-sheet.tsx:214 and :230 use size-[15px]; coach-settings-notifications.tsx:428 passes size={15}; connect-channel-sheet.tsx:364 and :437 use 22 and 18 in the same sheet; impersonation-banner.tsx:291 defaults its Glyph to size = 17. 21px and 15px are not decisions anyone would defend in a review - they are the numbers you get when an icon is nudged until it looks right next to one specific string, which is the failure mode a fixed icon size exists to prevent.
fix: Round the sixteen off-ladder boxes to the nearest sanctioned rung (15 and 17 to 16, 21 and 22 to 20, 26 to 24) and pass them through the `size` prop rather than a size-[Npx] utility so the value is greppable. Where a surface genuinely needs a non-default box, note the reason inline as icons.tsx:110 already asks callers to do.

source: crossvector
tell: token bypass / hardcoded value that cannot theme
title: The light-palette --shadow-card is inlined verbatim in 5 places, and the whole overlay layer takes Tailwind's stock shadows instead of the documented rungs
why: Five call sites paste the exact string `0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.6) inset, 0 1px 2px rgba(28,42,82,0.04), 0 8px 20px -14px rgba(28,42,82,0.16)` — character for character the light-palette --shadow-card at tokens.css:231 (_primitives.tsx:307, coach-setup.tsx:949, affiliate-home.tsx:74, meet-agent.tsx:270 and :277). In the two dark blocks that token is `0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.05) inset, 0 16px 34px -20px oklch(0 0 0)` (tokens.css:553, :707), so these panels render a 0.6-alpha white inset — twelve times the intended brightness — over a near-invisible drop shadow on navy. tokens.css spends paragraphs solving every alpha so "the fill RENDERS at the same ratio its dark counterpart renders at"; these five bypass all of it. They slip the palette guard by construction: palette-literals.test.ts:152 drops any line matching SPECULAR (`shadow-[` or `box-shadow`) before testing, an exemption written for the primary button's specular highlight that now blanket-exempts every shadow in the repo. Separately, @theme inline (globals.css:7-80) declares no --shadow-* keys, so the eight `shadow-sm`/`shadow-md`/`shadow-lg` uses on ui/sheet.tsx:66, popover.tsx:40, dropdown-menu.tsx:64 and :158, select.tsx:401, tabs.tsx:64, sidebar.tsx:246 and :311 compile to Tailwind's stock flat-black shadows — the same "invisible on this canvas" failure tokens.css:947 describes for bg-black/10. DESIGN.md:390 assigns drawer and popover faces to --shadow-raised and calls the three overlay rungs load-bearing ("tokens.test.ts asserts every rung is declared in all four palettes, so a surface can always reach the right one"), but --shadow-modal is reached by exactly two call sites and ui/dialog.tsx:57 and ui/alert-dialog.tsx:55 carry no shadow at all. Declared in four palettes, reached by nobody. Plus six further one-off shadows (context-eye.tsx:270 and :355, coach-inbox.tsx:1042, coach-pillbar.tsx:206, button-class.ts:58, sidebar.tsx:485).
fix: Replace the five inlined copies with `shadow-[var(--shadow-card)]`, already the spelling used at 20 other sites. Point ui/sheet.tsx at --shadow-drawer, ui/popover.tsx / dropdown-menu.tsx / select.tsx at --shadow-raised, and ui/dialog.tsx / alert-dialog.tsx at --shadow-modal. Narrow palette-literals.test.ts's SPECULAR exemption to inset-only shadows so a pasted drop shadow is caught.
note: The core is real and the dark-mode consequence is real: src/lib/theme.ts implements a light/dark/system preference and tokens.css carries live dark blocks at :411 and :565, so the four surfaces that inline `shadow-[0_1px_0_rgba(255,255,255,0.6)_inset,0_1px_2px_rgba(28,42,82,0.04),0_8px_20px_-14px_rgba(28,42,82,0.16)]` do render a 0.6 white inset over navy in dark, where the token would give 0.05 (tokens.css:553, :707). The Tailwind half verifies exactly: the @theme inline block declares no --shadow-* key, and all 8 cited shadow-sm/md/lg lines are correct to the line (sheet:66, popover:40, dropdown-menu:64 and :158, select:401, tabs:64, sidebar:246 and :311) with the only 9th hit being a test file. --shadow-modal really is reached by just 2 call sites (confirm-flow.tsx:535, command-palette.tsx:346) and dialog.tsx:57 / alert-dialog.tsx:55 really carry no shadow. Downgraded because: it is 4 exact copies, not 5; the exact string is on a documented allowlist — coach-surface-fills.test.ts:58-62 lists it by exact string with written reasoning ("a raised panel's top-edge highlight is white-on-white by design and reads as a bevel"), i.e. a recorded decision rather than drift; and 3 of the 6 "further one-off shadows" are wrong (two nonexistent paths, one is the documented kit constant). Corrected total ~16.

source: typography
tell: self-inconsistency — a type size that appears in no token, no doc and no artboard is the most common micro-size in the console
title: 10.5px is a phantom type size: 14 sites, zero authority, and the repo's own notes already flag it
why: docs/DESIGN.md:354-357 names exactly three sub-12px roles — Overline (mono 500, 9.5px, 0.09em), Badge/count (mono 500, 10px, 0.08em), Mono meta (mono 400, 12px) — and the 11px Floor Rule at DESIGN.md:365-368 enumerates "the 9.5px overline and 10px badge" as the only two utility-class exemptions. 10.5px is neither, appears in no --t-* token, in no line of docs/DESIGN.md's type roles, and in none of the 20 design/coach/*.dc.html artboards (grep for 10.5 across design/ returns only two SVG path coordinates). Yet it is the size at 14 real code sites: provenance-chip.tsx:51, app-shell.tsx:226, app-sidebar.tsx:546, bar-sparkline.tsx:148, cell-two-line.tsx:63, review-checklist.tsx:69, admin-audit-log.tsx:730/737/749, account-sheet.tsx:142/458/526, owner-audit.tsx:435, owner-inbox.tsx:558, atomics-sheet.tsx:127/479. What makes this a tell rather than a nit is the contrast with how this repo treats a half-pixel it actually decided: tokens.css:1069-1078 spends ten lines justifying --t-mono-crumb at 11.5px, counting occurrences on the artboards ("the breadcrumb trail on all 24 admin artboards... the mono count beside a nav item 216 times") before committing. 10.5px got no such paragraph anywhere, thirteen times over. The team has already noticed: docs/plans/2026-09-04-coach-rehaul-notes.md:407 records "`ProvenanceChip` is 10.5px uppercase mono, three ways under the coach" as a defect.
fix: Decide the value once. Either collapse the 14 sites onto the documented 10px badge role, or promote 10.5px to a named token in tokens.css beside --t-mono-crumb with the same kind of measured justification, add it to DESIGN.md's type-role list and to the 11px Floor Rule's exemption sentence, and route all 14 sites through it. Either way the answer is one declaration, not fourteen literals.

source: The owner console's actual UI implementation — the largest single body
title: Two button systems on one console, three files carrying both, and the 32px target console.css spends fourteen lines declaring is read by no console screen
why: console.css:55-68 sets --console-target: 32px ('30-34px is fine for someone using this all day with a mouse') and re-points --t-target at it, commenting that it is 'written as a reference rather than a second 32px, so the two cannot drift'. var(--t-target) has exactly two consumers repo-wide — meet-agent.tsx:318 and account-security-settings.tsx:1189 — and neither is a console screen. Meanwhile the console runs two button vocabularies: 10 of the 23 files import shadcn's ui/button, whose variants live on shadcn's parallel semantic layer (bg-secondary, text-secondary-foreground, border-ring, --radius-md, text-[0.8rem]) rather than on --accent / --line / --r-control / --t-body; 5 import KitButton, whose three sizes are h-[26px]/12px, h-[30px]/12.5px and h-[34px]/13px (button-class.ts:12-14) — none of them 32, and the lg rung takes a raw rounded-[9px] where the radius scale runs 4/6/8/11/12/14. Three files carry both systems at once: admin-money-affiliates.tsx, admin-money-tiers.tsx, owner-clients.tsx. Four sites spend shadcn's size=sm, which is h-7 = 28px, four pixels under the console's declared floor: admin-audit-log.tsx:1027 and :1126, owner-clients.tsx:377 and :1168, plus <Button size="sm"> at owner-clients.tsx:962, :1058 and :1199.
fix: Pick one. Either restyle ui/button's variants onto the SetterFi tokens and delete KitButton, or wrap ui/button so console screens never see the shadcn size names. Either way derive the size rungs from --t-target so a control cannot ship under the console's own floor, and give the three dual-system files a single import.

source: public/site/ — the page actually served at `/` in production — was in
title: Thirteen font faces across four families on a two-family system: the pinned Archivo axis is contradicted, two weights are downloaded unused, three declared weights cannot render, and SetterFi's own product console is drawn in Inter
why: design/coach/VOCABULARY.md pins the exact font link: 'Archivo:wght@400;450;500;540;600&family=IBM+Plex+Mono:wght@400;500'. index.html:10 requests Archivo 400;500;600;700;800 -- dropping 450 and 540, which are the two weights tokens.css:114-115 and the --w-body / --w-row fork are built on ('Archivo is variable, so 450 and 540 come off the same axis at no download cost'), and adding 700 (used 6 times) and 800 (used zero times). It requests IBM Plex Mono 400;500;600 where tokens.css:115 says 'IBM Plex Mono ships 400 and 500 only, which is why --w-mono has two steps and not four'; the page then uses 600 (index.html:67) and never uses 500. Inter and Roboto are downloaded on top. Roboto -> --gsans -> the Chrome chrome and Google Calendar body: legitimate mock fidelity. Inter -> --ui -> index.html:181 (iOS/Messenger), :271 (Meta Events Manager), AND :323 .card -- which index.html:318's own comment calls 'The two late cards: refusals, and the follow-up ladder. Product-console styling.' Those two panels (index.html:602-620) depict SetterFi's own product and render in Inter, not Archivo. index.html:31 also lists 'Inter' BEFORE -apple-system and 'SF Pro Text', so on Apple hardware the downloaded generic beats the authentic system face the stack was reaching for. And three declarations ask for Inter 700 (index.html:193, 277, 289) which is never downloaded, while scrollcraft.css:110 sets font-synthesis-weight:none, so all three silently render at 600. Finally scrollcraft.css:33 leaves --sc-font-mono at 'Geist Mono', a family the page never downloads and index.html:14-32 never overrides (it declares a separate --mono at :30 instead) -- dormant only because no .sc-label exists on the page.
fix: Replace the index.html:10 href with VOCABULARY.md's pinned link plus the two mock faces actually needed: Archivo 400;450;500;540;600, IBM Plex Mono 400;500, Roboto 400;500, Inter 400;500;600. Move .card (index.html:323) off --ui onto var(--sc-font-text). Reorder --ui (index.html:31) to put -apple-system and 'SF Pro Text' ahead of Inter so the iOS mock gets the real face. Change index.html:193, 277, 289 from 700 to 600, or add 700 to the Inter request.

source: typography
tell: self-inconsistency — one named type role hand-typed at eight trackings and six sizes, alongside a token-driven population of the same role
title: The uppercase micro-label is written by hand at eight tracking values while the kit's own tables read the token
why: docs/DESIGN.md:354-356 names three tracking values for uppercase labels: 0.09em (overline), 0.11em (rail group labels), 0.08em (badge/count). Shipped code carries eight: 0.04em (admin-money-tiers.tsx:302, app-shell.tsx:227), 0.06em (account-sheet.tsx:526, :675), 0.07em (provenance-chip.tsx:51, app-shell.tsx:307), 0.075em (tokens.css:1012 .t-th), 0.08em (account-sheet.tsx:142, owner-inbox.tsx:379/446, app-sidebar.tsx:548), 0.085em (tokens.css:1011 .t-overline), 0.09em (type.tsx:30, grid-table.tsx:103, table-group-header.tsx:74), 0.12em (error.tsx:21) — across six sizes (9.5, 10.5, 11, 11.5, 12, 14px). Only the three 0.09em/9.5px sites match the named role. The tell is that the correct pattern already exists in the same codebase: data-table.tsx:701, data-table-toolbar.tsx:207/224, record-sheet.tsx:245 and admin-audit-log.tsx:1100 all write `tracking-[var(--t-label-tr)]` or `tracking-[var(--t-over-tr)]`. Two populations of the same role coexist — one referencing a token, one typing a number nobody chose. error.tsx:21 is the clearest instance: an uppercase mono label on a top-level route error page at `text-xs` (Tailwind's default 12px, not a repo token) and 0.12em, a tracking that exists nowhere else in the product. tokens.css:291's own stated principle — a step "aliases a --s-* rung so the rhythm cannot drift off the 4px grid" — is precisely the discipline missing here.
fix: Add --t-over-tr's counterparts for the badge and rail roles if they genuinely differ, then convert the 10 non-conforming sites to `tracking-[var(--t-over-tr)]` / `tracking-[var(--t-label-tr)]`, matching what data-table.tsx:701 and data-table-toolbar.tsx:224 already do. Fix error.tsx:21 to read the type tokens rather than Tailwind's `text-xs` and 0.12em. Extend token-references.test.ts to refuse a literal `tracking-[Nem]` on any element that also carries `uppercase`, so the next one is a red test.

source: crossvector
title: DESIGN.md §2/§4/§5 still prescribe dark-palette-only literals with no SUPERSEDED marker, including retired teal and a raw hex
why: The Corrections section states its own contract: "the superseded sentence gets a marker pointing here." It marked the frontmatter and §2 Primary and stopped. Twelve prescriptive values further down are dark-only and unmarked, several provably retired. §5:452 specifies the dashed-add button as "1px dashed rgba(80,200,222,.35)" and §5:570 the active rail pill as "rgba(80,200,222,.22)" — that is the teal the accent moved off on 2026-09-01, and grepping src/ for 80,200,222 returns zero hits, so only the doc still carries it. §5:572 specifies rail group labels "in #63728e", a raw hex in a document whose own §6 Don't says "Don't re-derive a token value or introduce a raw hex literal"; app-shell.tsx:158 records having removed exactly that literal because it "reads as a mid-slate on navy and as an illegible one on white". §5:428 gives .surface-strip as "rgba(255,255,255,.02) on rgba(120,150,200,.1)" while globals.css:212 documents that recipe as the bug fixed on 2026-09-01 ("rgba(255,255,255,0.02) over a near-white card is nothing at all"). §4:384/386 give --shadow-card / --shadow-open as the black-cast dark values; the default light palette is slate-cast with a 0.6 white inset (tokens.css:231-232). §4:393 gives --scrim as oklch(0 0 0 / 0.6); light is oklch(0.28 0.03 262 / 0.32). §4:407 asserts hairlines "stay translucent slate at rgba(120,150,200,α)" and that tokens.test.ts pins the channels — the test pins two channel sets (tokens.test.ts:347 and :352) and light uses rgba(60,90,150,α). §5:568 gives the admin rail as "200px"; app-shell.tsx:123 ships 246px. Also unmarked: §2:267, §5:449, §5:458, §5:567. A reader implementing from §5 today ships a teal dashed border and an invisible strip.
fix: Add the inline SUPERSEDED markers §2 already uses to DESIGN.md:267, 384, 386, 393, 407, 428, 449, 452, 458, 567-568, 570, 572, and extend the Corrections table with a "§4 and §5 recipes" row. Replace the literals with the token names (--shadow-card, --scrim, --control-fill, --line, --accent-edge, --overline, --sidebar-w) so the doc stops holding a second copy of the palette — which the Corrections preamble already says is what caused this.
note: Every one of the 13 cited lines is real and says what is claimed, and every supporting citation is exact: DESIGN.md:452 and :570 do carry rgba(80,200,222,...) and `grep -r '80,200,222' src/` returns 0 hits; :572 carries #63728e while app-shell.tsx:158 records removing exactly that literal because it "reads as a mid-slate on navy and as an illegible one on white" and DESIGN.md:646 forbids raw hex; :428 gives the .surface-strip recipe that globals.css:212 documents as the bug fixed 2026-09-01; :568 says 200px for the admin rail while app-shell.tsx:123 ships `admin: "246px"`; tokens.css:231-232 and tokens.test.ts:347/:352 are line-exact. The Corrections section does state the marker contract and does place 9 markers (lines 4, 22, 175, 178, 191, 196, 205, 255, 312), all of them at or above §3, none in §4/§5. Downgraded for three reasons. (1) The repo documents a deliberate mitigation twice and prominently: DESIGN.md:144-145 ("src/app/tokens.css is the source of truth for every value in this document") and the Corrections preamble ("Read values from src/app/tokens.css, never from this document") — so the "a reader implementing from §5 ships a teal border" scenario requires ignoring the doc's own first instruction. (2) Roughly half the list is not false, only theme-partial: :384, :386, :393, :449, :458 and :267 remain literally correct in the two dark blocks (tokens.css:553-554, :583, :427), and §4:394 already qualifies the scrim with "in dark." The provably-retired-regardless-of-theme subset is 7: :407, :428, :452, :567, :568, :570, :572. (3) Zero shipped-UI consequence — nothing in the product renders wrong; this is visible only by reading the doc against tokens.css.

source: motion
tell: self-inconsistency (durations off the stated scale, in CSS)
title: Five hand-picked CSS/JS durations sit on no rung of the seven-rung scale, in a repo whose reduced-motion block collapses that scale by name
why: The scale is 80/150/250/350/400/500ms (tokens.css:299-304) and DESIGN.md:644-645 makes using it a rule. Twelve sites don't. Off-scale values: 140ms (console.css:135, twice on one line), 160ms (coach.css:706), 220ms (globals.css:1071, three times on one line for the trace node's border/background/color), 300ms (ui/file-upload.tsx:1238, :1267, :1294), plus the JS 0.16/0.22/0.24 covered in the JS-scale pattern. Separately, five sites bypass the token while landing on the right number -- `duration-150` literal instead of `duration-[var(--duration-quick)]` at rehaul/context-eye.tsx:275, :305, :346, :356 and rehaul/coach-dashboard.tsx:377 -- which is harmless today and drifts the moment the rung moves. For scale: 62 sites across 39 files do use `duration-[var(--duration-*)]`, so these twelve read as the places the pass didn't reach rather than as decisions. 220ms in particular is a value no scale in the repo contains and no comment defends.
fix: console.css:135 -> var(--duration-quick); coach.css:706 -> var(--duration-quick) (same fix as the hover-lift pattern); globals.css:1071 -> var(--duration-fast); the five `duration-150` literals -> duration-[var(--duration-quick)]. ui/file-upload.tsx's three `duration-300 ease-linear` are on progress indicators in a file nothing imports -- delete the file or move them to var(--duration-medium) with var(--ease-linear), which is currently a zero-use token.

source: Responsive thresholds are the only design axis in the repo with no tok
tell: a guard that reads as coverage but proves a narrower property than the axis needs
title: container-queries.test.ts checks that queries resolve, never that widths agree — and scans only .tsx, leaving the CSS container query unguarded
why: Flagged for scope, not quality — this file is one of the better guards in the repo and its docstring is unusually honest, naming four failure modes it cannot catch (inline-style override, cross-file collision, resolving against the wrong container, unnamed queries binding to the nearest ancestor).
