But all 11 it() blocks test resolution only: 'grows no new collision' (404), 'no new query with no container anywhere in its file' (408), 'never points a named query at a container nothing declares' (412), 'adds no new unnamed query' (465). Not one compares two widths. So the 420/440/520 spread in the kit atomics and the 640/720/860/900 spread in the onboarding wizard are all fully green — every one of those queries resolves against a real container, and that is the whole question the suite asks. Separately, line 76 filters to `/\.tsx?$/`, so the hand-written `@container (max-width: 380px)` at coach.css:406 is outside the scan entirely; the docstring's aside that 'No CSS file in this repo sets container-type' is true but reads as though CSS carries no container queries, which it does. Anyone reading a green run as 'responsive layout is guarded' would be wrong in exactly the way the docstring warns about for its other blind spots.
fix: Add one it() block that groups every arbitrary container width by the named container it queries and fails when a single container is queried at more than N distinct widths (start with the /onboarding container, which has four), and extend the line 76 filter to .css so coach.css:406 is at least counted. Add a line to the docstring saying width agreement is out of scope, matching how it already discloses its other four limits.

source: src/lib was in no scope, yet it is a presentation layer: it holds the
title: Money renders in three different shapes depending on which module built the string, including in messages sent to leads
why: src/lib/format/metric.ts:33-38 is the canonical `money(cents, currency)` and uses `style: "currency"`, so it renders $5,000.00. src/lib/brain/render-placeholders.ts:24 -- the module that substitutes {{funding_range}} and friends into the agent's OUTBOUND messages to leads -- hand-rolls its own: `` `$${new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", {maximumFractionDigits: 0}).format(cents/100)}` ``, giving $5,000 with a manually prefixed dollar sign. owner-clients.tsx:688 hand-rolls a third: `` `$${Math.round(mrr/100).toLocaleString("en-US")}` ``. So the same figure reads with cents on one console table, without cents on another, and without cents again in the text a lead receives -- and two of the three build the currency symbol by string concatenation rather than letting Intl place it, which is the thing `style: "currency"` exists to decide. Eleven separate NumberFormat constructions live outside src/lib/format (view-models.ts:752, admin-money-billing-costs.tsx:196, coach-agent-preview.tsx:131, meet-agent.tsx:65, offer-view-models.ts:49, stat-strip.tsx:151, columns.ts:153 among them). Inside metric.ts itself the discipline is also uneven: five formatters are hoisted as module constants (:3-31) and `money` alone constructs a new one on every call (:34).
fix: Hoist metric.ts's currency formatter to a module constant beside the other five, then route render-placeholders.ts:24 and owner-clients.tsx:688 through `money()`. If a no-cents shape is genuinely wanted for round figures, add it to src/lib/format/metric.ts as a named export (`moneyWhole`) so the choice is made once and is visible, rather than re-derived with a hand-typed '$' at each callsite.

source: public/site/ — the page that actually serves `/` in production — is 2,
title: Nine re-typed literals of variables declared 300 lines above, and a dim state that CSS specificity silently kills
why: Having declared --ink-now / --soft-now / --over-now at index.html:39-41 with a stated justification, the file then re-types the same three literal values inline nine more times instead of referencing them: #181e28 at :321, #333d50 at :333 and :347, #5e6b83 at :330, :336, :339, :340 and :348. DESIGN.md's Corrections section opens by saying a second copy of a value is how the first one became false; this is a third copy, in the same file, of a value the file already names. It has already produced a defect. index.html:347 `.tl li span { color: #333d50 }` has specificity (0,1,2); index.html:351 `.tl__off span { color: #9aa5b8 }` has (0,1,1), so the lower rule loses regardless of source order and the "off" treatment on the cancelled-follow-up row (index.html:618, "Remaining follow-ups cancelled") never renders. Its sibling at :352 carries `!important` and does apply, so the timeline dot dims while the text beside it stays full strength — a half-applied state, which is worse than either whole. Note the fix is not simply to raise the specificity: #9aa5b8 measures 2.42:1 against --card, far below AA for the sentence it colours, so the value is wrong as well as unreachable.
fix: Replace the nine inline literals with var(--ink-now) / var(--soft-now) / var(--over-now). Rewrite index.html:351 as `.tl li.tl__off span` to win on specificity, and change its value to var(--over-now) (#5e6b83, 5.24:1 on --card) rather than #9aa5b8.
note: Both halves verified exactly. The count is right on the nose: ripgrep over index.html gives #181e28 x2, #333d50 x3, #5e6b83 x6, #9aa5b8 x2 -- one of each is the declaration at :39-41/:44-46, leaving nine re-typings at :321, :333, :347 (#333d50); :330, :336, :339, :340, :348 (#5e6b83); :351 (#9aa5b8). Each duplicates a custom property declared in the same <style> block ~300 lines above, so the phase swap at :44-46 cannot reach any of them. The specificity kill is real and visible: `.tl li span` at :347 scores (0,1,2) and `.tl__off span` at :351 scores (0,1,1), so the dim grey never applies -- the "Remaining follow-ups cancelled" row at :618 renders at full body colour instead of the cancelled state it was written for. The smoking gun is the very next line: `.tl__off i` at :352 carries `!important`, because `.tl li i` at :345 loses the same race -- the author hit this exact collision one selector earlier, patched the dot, and missed the text. This is the one finding in the set with a defect a reader can see.

source: There is dead CSS and there are orphaned assets, inside a hard budget
tell: orphaned dead code — shipped binaries nothing references
title: Six .mp4 files ship in public/onboarding/ with zero references anywhere in the repo, and four .png masters sit beside the .webp the site actually loads
why: connect-social.mp4, choose-calendar.mp4, support-help.mp4, offer-layer.mp4, test-go-live.mp4 and prepare-text.mp4 (64 KB total, all genuine ISO Media MP4s) are named nowhere. The only `.mp4` strings in the entire tree outside package-lock.json are `leg1.mp4` and `leg1-m.mp4` in a documentation example inside public/site/scrollcraft.js:75 and its byte-identical copy under scrollcraft/builds/. There is no `<video>` element, no `poster=` and no `<source>` anywhere in src/ — grepping every .tsx returns nothing — so no code path could reach them even by constructed filename. Their names map one-to-one onto the onboarding steps that still exist as components (connect-step.tsx, calendar-step.tsx, offer-step.tsx, go-live-step.tsx), which places them with the same 2026-09-01 onboarding port that took onboarding.css and assembly-canvas.tsx out; the CSS went and the media did not. Separately, scrollcraft/builds/setterfi/assets/ holds handles.png, learned.png, numbers.png and takeover.png (340 KB) that no HTML or CSS names — public/site/index.html:559-598 and its build twin load only the .webp. That one is lower-confidence: docs/SETUP.md:211 calls the directory "the `assets/` screenshots" without saying the .png are sources, so they may be intended masters. The four .webp in public/site/assets/ are clean — all four are referenced.
fix: Delete public/onboarding/ and its six .mp4 files; nothing in the tree can reach them and they are served to the public at a guessable path. For the four .png, confirm with whoever owns the scroll site whether they are the masters the .webp were generated from; if they are, say so in docs/SETUP.md beside the existing `assets/` sentence so the next reader does not have to re-derive it, and if they are not, delete them.

source: The design system's own type-role utility layer is mostly dead, and on
tell: unused abstraction presented as a live API
title: 41% of the type-role class layer has zero consumers; the whole layer has 66 uses and one class owns 36% of them
why: tokens.css declares 22 `.t-*` classes as a complete, symmetric role vocabulary. Verified consumer counts across all non-test src/ TS/TSX: .t-metric 0, .t-section 0, .t-money 0, .t-transcript 0, .t-nav 0, .t-th 0, .t-badge 0, .t-count 0, .t-hero 0 — nine classes (41%) that no element in the product ever wears; their ONLY occurrences repo-wide are the CSS declarations themselves. Four more have exactly one consumer (.t-title, .t-section-title, .t-figure, .t-mono-meta). Total live uses across all 22 classes: 66, of which .t-muted alone is 24. A vocabulary this evenly declared and this unevenly used was generated as a complete-looking set, not grown from callsites — the giveaway is that the eight roles with the most specific semantics (metric, money, transcript, th, badge, count, hero, nav) are exactly the eight nobody reached for.
fix: Delete the nine zero-consumer declarations, or convert them to the `--t-*` token form so they cost nothing when unused. If any are intended as a forward API, say so in a comment naming the surface that will adopt them, the way tokens.css does for every other deliberate value.
note: Re-counted with PCRE2 word-boundary matching that excludes var(--t-*) token reads, across all non-test .ts/.tsx in src/, plus a repo-wide sweep excluding node_modules and .css. Nine of the twenty-two declared classes have zero consumers anywhere in shipped code: .t-metric (tokens.css:1002), .t-section, .t-money, .t-transcript (:1006), .t-nav, .t-th (:1012), .t-badge (:1013), .t-count (:1014), .t-hero (:1109). That is 9/22 = 41%. The probe put .t-section at one consumer; it is actually zero (its only hits are .t-section-title). The two remaining repo-wide hits for .t-th and .t-hero are prose in SIMPLIFICATION-SPEC.md and DESIGN.md, not consumers, and the design canvas (design/coach/*.dc.html) uses none of them. .t-muted at 24 is the largest single consumer. No justification survives: the header comment at tokens.css:999 sources the set 'from fonts/REPORT.md, verbatim', and no fonts/ directory or REPORT.md exists in the repo, so the stated provenance is dangling. Severity corrected from high to medium: unused CSS classes render nothing, so this is a dead-API tell with zero visual consequence, and coach.css:1614 documents a deliberate decision to keep the class layer alive for opt-in.

source: cards
tell: generic generated scaffolding left in place — a card treatment that contradicts the four-ground model
title: Stock shadcn Card ships unused but publicly re-exported, with a face that is a flat fill and a ring instead of the lit four-ground card
why: card.tsx is the untouched shadcn default: `rounded-xl` (12px, not `--r-card`'s 14px), a flat `bg-card` with no `--card-top` → `--card` gradient, `ring-1 ring-foreground/10` instead of `border 1px var(--line)`, no `--shadow-card` at all, and a `bg-muted/50` footer. DESIGN.md §4 is explicit that the card's inset top highlight carried inside --shadow-card "is what makes the face read lit" — this Card has none of it, so it is the one card shape in the tree that opts out of the mechanism the elevation section is built on. It has zero imports repo-wide (`<Card`, `from "@/components/ui/card"`, and `from "@/components/ui"` all return nothing), yet ui/index.ts:8 re-exports it, which makes `Card` the obvious name for the next contributor to reach for and the fastest way to silently land a non-system card. It is not alone: accordion, aspect-ratio, field, file-upload, form, progress, scroll-area and table are also zero-import and all re-exported from the same barrel. Every one of the twelve components in src/components/kit that I read carries a docstring arguing its shape; these nine carry the CLI's boilerplate and no argument, which is the difference between decided and generated.
fix: Delete card.tsx and the other eight zero-import primitives, and drop their lines from ui/index.ts. If Card is wanted as a future entry point, reduce it to a thin wrapper over `.surface-card` so it cannot draw a face the design system does not own.

source: There is no breakpoint scale, and no scope audited responsive behaviou
tell: Values with no written reasoning in a codebase whose stated convention is that every value carries reasoning
title: Nine of thirteen container-query widths carry no justification anywhere, and no test guards any width
why: I grepped every source comment in src/ (tests excluded) for each of the thirteen container widths. Nine have zero mentions: 300, 420, 560, 620, 720, 820, 860, 900, 1000. Of the four that appear, three are false positives about fixed panel widths rather than breakpoint rationale — auth-card.tsx:6 and login-form.tsx:21 describe a 440px card, account-sheet.tsx:57 a 520px panel — so the true count of container widths with written reasoning is one (surface.tsx/coach.css at 380). Representative bare values: coach-onboarding.tsx:513 switches to `grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_460px]` at 1000px with no note; admin-audit-log.tsx picks 860 at :737 and 720 at :743 six lines apart with no note on either; page.tsx:163 goes to three columns at 560px; admin-money-affiliates.tsx:425 uses 300px. Nothing tests any of it: container-queries.test.ts is a genuinely excellent guard, but it checks only that a query *resolves* against some container, and its own preamble (:40-44) says plainly "nothing here can decide" which container a query should name and "do not read a green run as 'every query measures the right thing'". Which width it fires at is outside its scope entirely, so thirteen numbers ship with one comment and zero assertions between them.
fix: For each of the nine, either write the one line saying what runs out of room at that width, or fold it onto the nearest neighbour — 420 onto 440, 620 onto 640, 820 onto 860 are each within 40px and plausibly the same decision made twice. Then extend container-queries.test.ts with a fourth check that fails on any arbitrary width outside the --bp-* family from pattern 2, which reuses the QUERY regex it already has at :64.

source: workspace
title: The page head -> first block gap takes 4 values through 5 different mechanisms across 12 surfaces; not one of them is the documented 20px
why: tokens.css:293 names this exact relationship once: `--d-head-gap: var(--s-5); /* 20px: page head -> first content block */`, and src/components/kit/templates/rhythm.ts:23 re-states it as BREAK.head. The workspace tree realizes it 12 different ways. Owner: gap-[var(--s-4)]=16px (owner-overview.tsx:479), gap-[16px]=16px (owner-inbox.tsx:180, owner-compliance.tsx:515), gap-4=16px (owner-money.tsx:913, owner-system.tsx:767, owner-clients.tsx:1088), gap-[14px] (owner-brain.tsx:1350), and mb-[14px] on the head itself (owner-audit.tsx:452). Coach: gap-[20px] (coach-leads.tsx:400, affiliate-home.tsx:280), gap-[24px] (coach-agent.tsx:1064), gap-6 (coach-setup.tsx:1232, coach-dashboard.tsx:494), gap-[var(--s-5)] (leads-surface.tsx:999), and two empty spacer divs on the SAME page at two different values - coach-billing.tsx:566 `<div className="mt-[var(--s-5)]" />` (20px) and coach-billing.tsx:1018 `<div className="mt-[var(--s-6)]" />` (24px) for the identical CoachPageHead -> first-card relationship. Worse, tokens.css:288-290 predicts this failure in advance: 'A template that separates its crumb, its title, its stat strip and its table by the same 16px reads as a single undifferentiated stack, which is the other half of why the console reads flat.' Six of eight owner surfaces do precisely that. The head's own internal gap drifts alongside it: gap-3 (owner-clients.tsx:1089, owner-money.tsx:914, owner-audit.tsx:452), gap-[12px] (owner-compliance.tsx:516), gap-[var(--s-3)] (owner-overview.tsx:480), gap-[16px] (owner-inbox.tsx:181). And owner-inbox.tsx:183 sets its h1 at text-[26px] where the other seven owner surfaces and COACH-REDESIGN-PLAYBOOK.md:137 all say 30px.
fix: Route every page root through the existing BREAK vocabulary in src/components/kit/templates/rhythm.ts (currently 0 imports in this tree): head block gets BREAK.head (20px), content stack keeps its own gap. Delete the two spacer divs in coach-billing.tsx (566, 1018) in favour of a gap on the parent. Correct owner-inbox.tsx:183 to text-[30px].
note: Every cited line is real and says what is claimed (owner-overview.tsx:479 gap-[var(--s-4)], owner-inbox.tsx:180 gap-[16px], owner-money.tsx:913 gap-4, owner-brain.tsx:1350 gap-[14px], live/coach-billing.tsx:1018 mt-[var(--s-6)], plus owner-audit.tsx:452 mb-[14px], owner-compliance.tsx:515, owner-system.tsx:767, owner-clients.tsx:1088, rehaul/coach-agent.tsx:1064, coach-setup.tsx:1232, coach-dashboard.tsx:494). But the headline is false twice. (1) The auditor's own list contains the documented 20px: live/coach-billing.tsx:566 is mt-[var(--s-5)], which is byte-identical to BREAK.head in rhythm.ts:23; leads-surface.tsx:999 is gap-[var(--s-5)]; coach-leads.tsx:400 and affiliate-home.tsx:280 are gap-[20px]. Four of the fifteen surfaces it lists ARE 20px. (2) The grep-only method is blind to composition: 14 other workspace surfaces (admin-overview, admin-support, admin-audit-log, admin-money-*, admin-compliance, admin-system-health, admin-testing, alert-settings, success-client-book, admin-support-team) import ListPage/DetailPage from kit/templates, and list-page.tsx:105/206/223 applies BREAK.head — the documented 20px — for them. The console's documented head gap ships; it just ships through the template rather than a literal in the page file. What survives: the 8 hand-rolled rehaul owner surfaces set their head gap at 14px or 16px through 5 spellings and none at 20px, and 6 of 8 use one root gap for head, stat strip and table alike (owner-overview.tsx:479 gap-[var(--s-4)] equals the KPI grid's own internal gap at :585) — the undifferentiated stack tokens.css:288-290 warns about. source: Date, time and number formatting has no audit scope and is systematica
title: Two date orders ship side by side: seven en-GB formatters render "4 Sept 2026" where the module that claims to own dates renders "Sep 4, 2026"
why: datetime.ts:18 pins LOCALE = "en-US" and the docstring says "Pinning the locale *and* the zone makes the two renders byte-identical". Seven shipped formatters pass "en-GB" instead. All seven are user-visible, verified at their call sites: admin-help.tsx:134 renders "Generated {formatGeneratedAt(...)}" inside a MonoMeta on the admin handover panel; admin-overview.tsx:112, admin-measurement-tables.tsx:37, owner-overview.tsx:104 and :114, owner-clients.tsx:219 all format straight into cells and captions. Rendered through ICU for 2026-09-04: admin-help.tsx:68 gives "4 Sept 2026" while workspaceDateFormat gives "Sep 4, 2026" — the day/month order flips and even the month abbreviation changes ("Sept" vs "Sep") on two admin pages a single operator moves between. The other three en-GB spellings are "Friday, 4 September 2026" (owner-overview.tsx:77), "3 Sept" (owner-clients.tsx:211) and "4 September 2026" (connect-channel-flow.ts:131). The rationalising comment is the tell: owner-overview.tsx:101-102 justifies en-GB with "en-GB puts a comma after the weekday; the artboard does not, and the comma is the only difference between the two spellings." I rendered both — en-GB is "Friday, 4 September 2026", en-US is "Friday, September 4, 2026". The day/month order flips and en-US carries a second comma. The comment's central claim is checkably false, which is what a rationale written alongside the code rather than against it looks like.
fix: Change all seven locale literals to "en-US" and, where the surface wants the canvas's day-first reading, get it from an explicit option set rather than by borrowing a foreign locale's ordering — then let pattern 4's decision settle which order is canonical. Add the locale assertion described in pattern 1 so an eighth cannot land.
note: The count is exact: ripgrep finds precisely 7 `"en-GB"` constructors in non-test src. I rendered both shapes in Node against 2026-09-04: canonical workspaceDateFormat gives "Sep 4, 2026", the en-GB day/month/year gives "4 Sept 2026", en-GB long gives "Friday, 4 September 2026". The order flip is real and visible. The strongest instance is one the probe under-sold: in owner-clients.tsx the SAME field `row.updatedAt` renders two ways on the same screen — `sinceLabel()` via the en-GB SINCE_FORMAT at :211 (used at :634, :873, :1047) and `timestamp()` via the canonical en-US workspaceTimestampFormat at :208 (used at :954, :1319). One value, one surface, two date orders, no comment anywhere. Trimmed by one: owner-overview.tsx:77 is documented deliberate — the comment at :102-103 says "en-GB puts a comma after the weekday; the artboard does not, and the comma is the only difference between the two spellings," and longDate() at :104 does strip the comma, so the code delivers exactly the fidelity the comment claims. Severity lowered from high to medium: admin-help.tsx, admin-overview.tsx and admin-measurement-tables.tsx are each internally consistent (all UTC, all the same en-GB shape), so the collision is genuinely same-screen only in owner-clients.tsx.

source: Disabled and inactive states are drawn by fading the element, at three
tell: unadapted stock vocabulary carried into the product
title: Four aria-disabled:opacity-50 rules that nothing in src can ever trigger, while the two elements that do set aria-disabled carry no rule
why: aria-disabled:pointer-events-none aria-disabled:opacity-50 is declared on four ui/ primitives, and grep for `aria-disabled=` across src finds it applied at exactly three places - breadcrumb.tsx:68, file-upload.tsx:852 and kit/step-journey.tsx:292 - none of which is an accordion trigger, a tab trigger or a sidebar menu button. So the four rules are dead CSS shipped in every bundle. The inverse also holds: breadcrumb.tsx:68 sets aria-disabled='true' on a span whose class is just `font-normal text-foreground` with no inactive treatment at all. This is the tree-concentration the state vocabulary makes visible - 23 of the 43 fade occurrences are in src/components/ui/ (stock shadcn), 16 in workspace/, and only 2 in the adapted kit/ tree (button-class.ts:73, impersonation-banner.tsx:271). The disabled state is the clearest place where unadapted upstream vocabulary is still driving the product rather than the design system.
fix: Delete the aria-disabled:* pairs from accordion.tsx:37, tabs.tsx:102 and sidebar.tsx:479/683 since nothing supplies the attribute, and either give breadcrumb.tsx:68 the real inactive treatment or drop its aria-disabled. Keep one spelling per element based on what actually sets the state (native disabled for buttons/inputs, data-disabled for the Radix/file-upload surfaces).

source: Every design guard in the repo roots its scan at src/ or narrower, so
title: The copy guards stop at src/components while the copy they govern ships from src/app and src/lib
why: em-dash.test.ts:36 computes SRC = src/ and then narrows both halves to src/components at :88 and :167; quote-entities.test.ts:56 covers src/components and src/app but not src/lib. The rule each states is about rendered copy, not about a directory: em-dash.test.ts:9-11 quotes DESIGN.md's 'Don't write an em dash in UI copy' and :12-17 says the ban is on 'the character outright in this directory'. Running the guard's own decoder and glyph carve-out over the rest of the tree finds 36 offending lines in src/app and 147 in src/lib under its literal stated rule, and six of them survive comment-blanking, i.e. they are shipping copy: src/app/page.tsx:27 sets the public marketing page's `<title>` to 'SetterFi — your funding DMs answered, qualified and booked' (a browser tab and a search snippet, which is UI copy by any reading), src/app/design/atomics-sheet.tsx:195, :294 and :485 put em dashes in three section headings on the design-system showcase page, src/lib/evals/judge.ts:64 splices one into a model prompt string, and src/lib/webhooks/process-inbound.ts:1823 formats every booking slot as `${slot.display} — [slot_id:${slot.id}]`. src/lib holds 277 non-test source files including src/lib/copy/{errors,states,audit-labels}.ts, src/lib/admin-help-guides.ts and src/lib/coach-nav-labels.ts -- modules that are copy by name. The em-dash guard's src/components scope is already on record; what is systemic is that both copy guards drew their perimeter around the directory the last sweep happened in rather than around the copy.
fix: Change em-dash.test.ts:88 and :167 from `sourceFiles(join(SRC, "components"))` to `sourceFiles(SRC)` and quote-entities.test.ts:56 to a single `sourceFiles(SRC)`, then fix or exempt the six live sites. If the docstring-heavy src/lib prose is genuinely out of scope for the Unicode half, say so with a filter on comment-blanked text rather than with a directory, so the rule stays about copy.

source: Every design guard in the repo roots its scan at src/ or narrower, so
title: Six guards assert an empty offender list without ever pinning their own walk as non-empty, the shape their siblings name and refuse
why: Four guards in this suite state the failure mode by name and then guard against it: container-queries.test.ts:338-353 asserts sites.length > 60 and ok > 25 before consuming the scan, ghl-branding-wall.test.ts:144-148 asserts modules.length > 50, font-utility-token.test.ts:145-153 asserts SITES.length > 50, coach-shared-type-floor.test.ts:170-184 pins both halves, and token-references.test.ts:41-44 writes the reasoning out ('A green check whose input is empty is indistinguishable from a green check whose subject is clean, and the empty one is the more likely of the two'). Six do not. glow-budget.test.ts:47 and :63 both reduce a 339-file walk to `expect([]).toEqual([])` with nothing pinning pages() as non-empty; its third test at :75 reads status.tsx by path, so it controls the atomic, not the walk. measures.test.ts:34 is the same shape over the same 339 files. em-dash.test.ts:88 and :167 walk 440 files uncontrolled -- and its docstring at :175-177 says 'a guard that cannot be shown to fire is indistinguishable from one reading an empty string', then controls the regex at :180-184 instead of the walk. quote-entities.test.ts:56 walks 671 files, controlled only by synthetic strings at :34-43. accent-fill-spelling.test.ts:65-74 looks like a control but reads its two files through `join(process.cwd(), "src", rel)`, bypassing sourceFiles() entirely, so it passes on an empty walk. palette-literals.test.ts:156-159 controls only the src/components walk (CLEAN_COACH_SURFACE is a components path); the second walk at :137-138 over src/app's stylesheets -- added, per :113-119, precisely because globals.css was missed the first time -- has no control at all.
fix: Add one line per guard asserting the walk found what it must: `expect(pages().length).toBeGreaterThan(300)` in glow-budget and measures, `expect(sourceFiles(...).length).toBeGreaterThan(400)` in em-dash and quote-entities, `expect(sourceFiles().map(f=>f.rel)).toContain('components/kit/atomics/button-class.ts')` in accent-fill-spelling, and in palette-literals a second control naming a src/app stylesheet (e.g. 'consumer/consumer.css') so the CSS walk is pinned too.

source: motion
tell: (12/14) entrance animation without a reduced-motion guard
title: Five live popup components carry ungated animate-in/fade-in/zoom-in entrances while their siblings in the same files are gated
why: Six ui/* files use `animate-in fade-in-0 zoom-in-* slide-in-from-*` with no `motion-reduce:` guard anywhere in the file: popover.tsx:40, alert-dialog.tsx:33/:55, dialog.tsx:35/:57, dropdown-menu.tsx:64/:158, tooltip.tsx:53, file-upload.tsx:949. All are live -- DropdownMenuContent is imported by 13 files, DialogContent by 9, TooltipContent by 6, SelectContent by 3 (onboarding/calendar-step.tsx:447, onboarding/profile-step.tsx:206, workspace/live/success-client-book.tsx:1038). The inconsistency is inside the files: ui/select.tsx holds two live Select implementations, and the repo's own `selectPopupClassName` (L37-38) ends in `motion-reduce:animate-none motion-reduce:transition-none` while shadcn's SelectContent 14 lines of class later (L401) has neither. ui/sheet.tsx:38 and kit/tooltip.tsx:48 both carry the guard; ui/tooltip.tsx:53 does not, and it also enters at `zoom-in-95` while tokens.css:363 defines --tt-scale as 0.98 for the same gesture. Honest qualifier, which is why this is medium and not high: globals.css:1941-1945 sweeps `*{animation-duration:0.001ms!important}`, so these do collapse in time under reduce. The defect is authorial consistency and the second untokenised motion vocabulary, not broken accessibility.
fix: Append `motion-reduce:animate-none motion-reduce:transition-none` to the popup class strings in popover.tsx:40, alert-dialog.tsx:33/:55, dialog.tsx:35/:57, dropdown-menu.tsx:64/:158, tooltip.tsx:53, select.tsx:401 -- matching what selectPopupClassName and ui/sheet.tsx already do. Swap the literal `zoom-in-95`/`zoom-out-95` in ui/tooltip.tsx:53 for `zoom-in-[var(--tt-scale)]`, or delete the duplicate SelectContent/TooltipContent now that kit/ owns both.

source: cards
title: Every backdrop-filter in the product is unowned: four radii, none tokenized, zero on the design canvas — and the dead bg-black/10 they sit beside still reads as the authority
why: Judged individually: the three modal scrims are the legitimate case (blur over content the reader is being told is out of reach) but each carries Tailwind's stock `supports-backdrop-filter:backdrop-blur-sm`, a radius nobody in this repo chose, while the one scrim the repo actually authored — globals.css:1312-1314 for the agent dialog — picks `blur(6px)` beside `color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 76%, transparent)`. So the same [data-slot=dialog-overlay] renders two different blurs and two different scrim alphas depending on which dialog opened. The repo went to real trouble on the colour half: tokens.css:936-953 adds an unlayered rule dressing all three overlays in `--scrim`, with a comment explaining that Base UI "painted a flat bg-black/10 that is all but invisible," and tokens.test.ts:287-298 pins the override. The blur half was never touched, and the now-dead `bg-black/10` was never deleted from the three class strings — a reader who greps the component finds a value that is both overridden and, per tokens.css:71, the thing the token exists to fix. The two kanban edge fades (kanban-board.tsx:727, 739) are the weakest of the six: a `--canvas` gradient already carries the scroll affordance, and `backdrop-blur-[2px]` on top smears content rather than fading it. DESIGN.md §4 grounds depth in "surface value plus a hairline, not from shadow," §6 Don't bans "decorative glassmorphism," and none of the 22 design/coach/*.dc.html artboards contains a single backdrop-filter.
fix: Add a `--scrim-blur` token, set it once on the same unlayered rule that already sets `background: var(--scrim)` (tokens.css:949-953), and strip `supports-backdrop-filter:backdrop-blur-sm` and the dead `bg-black/10` from all three primitives so the class string stops lying. Fold the agent-dialog override into the same token. Drop the two `backdrop-blur-[2px]` on the kanban fades and let the gradient do the work.

source: coach-css+pages
title: The account menu overrides every spacing value its own artboard draws, giving two adjacent rows 13px and 14px for the same icon-to-label gap
why: `AccountMenu.dc.html:178` draws the identity header as `gap: 12px; padding: 16px`; coach.css:1298-1300 ships `gap: 13px; padding: 16px 18px`. `AccountMenu.dc.html:186-188` draws each menu row as `gap: 12px; height: 44px; padding: 0 12px`; coach.css:1340-1342 ships `gap: 14px; min-height: 48px; padding: 0 12px`. So the artboard uses one gap — 12px — for both rows, and the stylesheet uses 13px for the top one and 14px for the ones directly beneath it, for the identical avatar/icon-to-label relationship, four lines apart, with no comment on either. `13px` appears as a gap nowhere in any of the 22 artboards (its only canvas occurrence is inside `border-radius: 16px 16px 13px 13px` in LeadsBoard). The 48px row height is the one value here that is argued for (:1332-1335); 13px, 14px and the 18px right/left inset are not. The menu's own radius shows the same drift: coach.css:1289 sets `20px 20px 15px 15px` where the artboard at :177 draws a flat `border-radius: 12px`, and 15px is not a radius value anywhere in the canvas.
fix: Set both to `gap: var(--s-3)` (12px, the artboard's value), drop the 18px to `padding: 16px`, and either cite a reason for the `20px 20px 15px 15px` menu radius or restore the artboard's `var(--r-panel)`.

source: The owner console's actual UI implementation — the largest single body
tell: 10 (lucide icons everywhere), as a violation of the rule the repo wrote against it
title: Two icon families on one console: five files import lucide-react directly for six glyphs the sanctioned barrel already exports under identical names
why: kit/icons.tsx:4-21 calls itself 'the one sanctioned icon entry for the kit', says 'Two families live here and nothing else does', and names what it replaced: importing outside it 're-opens the door to mixed weights and mixed sizes in the same row, which is what made the old lucide sprawl read as three different products stitched together.' Five rehaul files import straight from lucide-react anyway, and the names collide exactly with sanctioned exports: owner-inbox.tsx:29 takes CircleCheck, Search and X, all three exported as Phosphor wrappers at icons.tsx:178, :193 and :201; context-eye.tsx:3 takes Eye (icons.tsx:213), and ContextEye is mounted on four console screens (owner-clients.tsx:33, owner-money.tsx:77, owner-overview.tsx:19, owner-audit.tsx:34); onboarding-connect.tsx:2 takes Camera (icons.tsx:242); account-sheet.tsx:19 and meet-agent.tsx:25 take five more. The result is visible on screen: /admin/audit draws its Search and X as Phosphor glyphs at the barrel's fixed regular weight and 16px (owner-audit.tsx:30), while /admin/alerts draws the same two icons as lucide strokes at lucide's defaults (owner-inbox.tsx:29). Two adjacent console screens, same icons, two families, different stroke weight.
fix: Point the five imports at @/components/kit/icons — six of the twelve glyph names resolve with no other change. Add the remaining glyphs to the barrel as Phosphor wrappers, then lint-ban the lucide-react specifier outside src/components/ui/, where shadcn's own imports legitimately live.

source: public/site/ — the page that actually serves `/` in production — is 2,
title: Three different reduced-motion policies, one of them contradicting the repo's stated hard rule, and five animated declarations covered by none
why: globals.css:1848-1946 states the repo policy and cites CLAUDE.md as its authority: every duration token to 0.001ms, every distance, blur and scale to zero, plus a universal `*, *::before, *::after` rule, on the explicit reasoning that "reduced motion means no transform at all rather than a very fast one". scrollcraft.css:387-389 opens its own block with the opposite sentence, "Fewer and gentler, not zero." index.html:459-462 then writes a third policy that enumerates seven selectors (.b, .stamp, .seen, .typing, .console, .ev, .win, plus .cta .dots i and .typing i) and misses five animated declarations entirely: index.html:302 `.meta__bars i` (height 420ms plus background 300ms), :308 `.meta__row` and :331 `.card__row` (opacity 320ms plus a 420ms translateY(8px)), :343 `.tl li` (opacity 320ms plus a 420ms translateX(-6px)), and :359 `#lineRing` (opacity 400ms). Because globals.css never loads on this page, its universal back-stop cannot catch them, so a reduced-motion reader still gets 36 chart bars growing, four declined-lead rows sliding up and four timeline rows sliding in from the left. The page's JS side is well done by contrast — index.html:836-846 cuts the camera between keyframes rather than tweening, and scrollcraft.js:791 drops the copy transform — which makes the CSS gap read as an enumeration somebody stopped adding to rather than a policy.
fix: Replace the seven-selector list at index.html:459-462 with the repo's universal form: `*, *::before, *::after { animation-duration: 0.001ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important; transition-duration: 0.001ms !important; }`, matching globals.css:1938-1945, and add `transform: none !important` for the four translate-on-enter rules. If the softer scrollcraft.css:387 policy is a deliberate exception for a cinematic surface, it needs an entry in DESIGN.md's Corrections, because as written it contradicts a rule the repo calls hard.
note: The count is exactly right. index.html declares fourteen animated rules; its own reduced-motion block at :460-461 covers .b, .stamp, .seen, .typing, .console, .ev, .win and .cta .dots i -- which accounts for :78, :150, :158, :223, :224, :238, :240, :241, :375. Uncovered, exactly five: .meta__bars i (:302), .meta__row (:308), .card__row (:331), .tl li (:343), .line #lineRing (:359). scrollcraft.css:387-413 does not reach them either -- it targets [data-sc-in], [data-sc-parallax], [data-sc-reveal], [data-sc-copy] and .sc-world__poster, and the page uses only data-sc-copy. And the JS does not save them: index.html:700 reads the preference and honours it thoroughly for the camera and opacities (:875, :888, :890, :900, :955), but :951-953 toggles .is-in on the Meta rows unconditionally, so those 320-420ms fades still play. :302 additionally transitions `height`, which docs/DESIGN.md:644 rules out outright. The framing is what is overstated: scrollcraft.css:388-389 states its reasoning in the file ("Fewer and gentler, not zero. Opacity still carries the reveal so the page is comprehensible; every position change is dropped"), which is a documented deliberate policy, not a contradiction; and globals.css:1848-1946 is correctly scoped to the Next app.

source: src/lib was in no scope, yet it is a presentation layer: it holds the
title: workspace-navigation.ts declares two closed vocabularies, pins neither, and contradicts both
why: Lines 7-11 declare the glyph vocabulary in prose: 'a square is a list of things, a circle is people or threads, a bar is a report or a record, a diamond is a system the platform runs', and justify it with 'a rail of identical squares reads as a template'. The TYPE is closed at four values (:12) -- the icons scope was right about that -- but the ASSIGNMENTS are closed to nothing. Four of the fourteen contradict the stated meanings, and two of those contradict each other across roles: 'Inbox' is a diamond at :154 (admin, a queue of alerts) and a circle at :227 (coach, the same job); Billing is a bar at :162 (admin Money, href /admin/billing) and a diamond at :235 (coach Billing) -- so the same domain gets two shapes and the coach one calls a record a system; 'Agent' at :234 is a square though the file says a system is a diamond; both Overviews (:153, :219) are squares though neither is a list. workspace-navigation.test.ts contains zero occurrences of 'glyph' across its 500+ lines of assertions, and app-sidebar.tsx:381 silently defaults a missing glyph to 'square', so a new destination joins the vocabulary as a list-of-things by accident. The same file's second vocabulary breaks the same way: `initials` derives from the `workspace` string everywhere (:70 SetterFi platform->SF, :75 Your agent->YA, :82 Partner portal->PP, :94 Setup companion->SC, :101 Lead experience->LE) except demoReviewPersonas at :116-119, which derives from the label instead (SO, SA, SC) and then, for the affiliate, derives from neither -- landing on 'SF', the platform's own monogram, apparently to dodge a collision with 'SA'.
fix: Add a test to src/lib/workspace-navigation.test.ts asserting every item carries an explicit glyph (no reliance on app-sidebar.tsx:381's default) and pinning the fourteen assignments so a change has to argue with the comment at :7-11. Then reconcile the four: Inbox to circle in both roles, coach Billing to bar to match admin Money, Agent to diamond, and either move both Overviews off square or widen the square's stated meaning. Give demoReviewPersonas[3] a monogram derived like its siblings rather than reusing SF.

source: public/site/ — the page actually served at `/` in production — was in
title: Reduced motion is a hand-enumerated allow-list: four transitioning classes and the CTA's scroll-driven scale escape it
why: index.html:459-462 cancels transitions and animations on a literal seven-class list: .b, .stamp, .seen, .typing, .console, .ev, .win. Four classes with position or size transitions are not on it and still animate under prefers-reduced-motion: .meta__bars i (index.html:302, height 420ms cubic-bezier), .meta__row (:308, transform 420ms from translateY(8px)), .card__row (:331, transform 420ms from translateY(8px)), and .tl li (:343, transform 420ms from translateX(-6px)). All four are driven by an `is-in` class that index.html:951-954 toggles from the metaRows list built at :717 ('.meta__row, .meta__bars i[data-at], .card [data-at]'), with no reduce branch -- unlike every neighbouring effect in the same function, which all have one (:888, :890, :900, :908, :914, :921, :927, :938, :955). Separately index.html:961-963 computes ctaOn with no reduce guard and writes cta.style.transform = scale(0.9 + 0.1 * ctaOn) continuously; it is the only scroll-driven transform in the page's own script without one. This is what an enumerated list always becomes: the enumeration was correct when written and the four classes added afterward were never added to it. Contrast scrollcraft.css:387-414, which cancels by attribute selector and therefore cannot drift.
fix: Replace the class list at index.html:460 with a rule that cancels by property rather than by name -- add .meta, .meta__row, .meta__bars i, .card, .card__row, .tl li to the selector, or better, set `transition: none !important; animation: none !important` on `.obj, .obj *` inside the reduced-motion block and re-enable the two opacity fades the page needs for comprehension. Add `reduce ? (t >= 15.9 ? 1 : 0) :` to ctaOn at index.html:961, matching the pattern at :890 and :921.

source: workspace
tell: (6) tokens declared then bypassed by literals
title: --shadow-card is inlined as its light-mode literal in 4 places including the shared owner table primitive, so those surfaces keep a white inset highlight in dark mode
why: tokens.css:231 defines `--shadow-card: 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.6) inset, 0 1px 2px rgba(28,42,82,0.04), 0 8px 20px -14px rgba(28,42,82,0.16)` and forks it per palette - tokens.css:553, inside `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root:not([data-theme="light"]) }`, replaces it with `0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.05) inset, 0 16px 34px -20px oklch(0 0 0)`. Four sites paste the light-block value verbatim as a Tailwind arbitrary shadow, so it cannot fork: _primitives.tsx:307 (CARD_TABLE.card, the face behind all 78 owner table cells across five console surfaces), affiliate-home.tsx:74-75, coach-setup.tsx:949, meet-agent.tsx:277. In dark mode those cards render a 60%-opacity white inset top edge against a dark ground - twelve times the intended 0.05. It is a self-inconsistency, not a judgement call: 15 other sites in this same tree use `shadow-[var(--shadow-card)]` correctly, and coach-leads.tsx:635 applies the token to the byte-identical panel recipe that meet-agent.tsx:274-277 hardcodes.
fix: Replace the four inlined shadow literals with `shadow-[var(--shadow-card)]`. _primitives.tsx:307 is the highest-value single edit - it fixes every owner console table at once.
note: Verified end to end, and the count is low by one. tokens.css:231 defines --shadow-card with a 0.6 white inset; tokens.css:553 (system dark) and :707 (explicit dark) both fork it to a 0.05 inset. Five sites paste the light literal instead of the token: _primitives.tsx:307 (CARD_TABLE.card, imported by owner-brain.tsx:64 and owner-clients.tsx:45 and used as the face behind the rehaul console tables), affiliate-home.tsx:74-75, coach-setup.tsx:949, meet-agent.tsx:277, and meet-agent.tsx:270 - the phone shell, which the audit missed and which carries the same 0.6 inset. Dark mode genuinely ships: nothing in the app forces [data-theme=light], the system-dark block applies on preference alone, and there is a real user-facing control (app-topbar.tsx:322-323, :343-344, :469-470 and account-sheet.tsx:861 call applyTheme, which app-shell.test.tsx:319/355 asserts writes data-theme onto documentElement). So on a dark screen those cards draw a 1px 60%-white line across their top edge, twelve times the intended alpha, while every neighbouring card drawn with shadow-[var(--shadow-card)] draws it at 5%. It is a self-inconsistency rather than a judgement call, exactly as claimed: coach-leads.tsx:635 applies the token to the byte-identical rounded-[24px_24px_17px_17px] panel that meet-agent.tsx:274-277 and coach-setup.tsx:946-949 hardcode. It also violates a stated rule - DESIGN.md section 6: 'Don't re-derive a token value' - and escapes the guard only because tokens.test.ts checks for hex, not rgba. This is the one pattern of the eight that changes a shipped pixel.

source: Entire product surfaces cite pixel authority that was never drawn — th
tell: off-grid value excused as canvas-faithful, where the canvas that exists says otherwise
title: Off-grid literals on the zero-authority surfaces are defended by the missing artboards and contradicted by the drawings that are in the repo
why: tokens.css:291 states the rule that a step must alias a --s-* rung 'so the rhythm cannot drift off the 4px grid', and VOCABULARY.md:69 restates the canvas's own law: 'Spacing steps: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40.' Two deliberate departures are justified purely by artboards that do not exist, and both are refuted by artboards that do. (1) consumer.css:36 sets `--consumer-avatar-lg: 42px` with the argument at :22-30: '42px, a literal, because the canvas states it three times and the spacing scale cannot ... All three consumer artboards draw this mark at `42px` with a `12px` radius and no disagreement between them (`Consumer.dc.html:66`, `ConsumerOptOut.dc.html:66`, `ConsumerBooked.dc.html:65`)'. None of the three files exists; `42px` appears in zero of the 22 boards; and the same object — the brand mark — is drawn at `width: 38px; height: 38px; border-radius: 10px` on all 20 chrome-bearing boards (AccountMenu.dc.html:82 and siblings) and specified that way at VOCABULARY.md:103. So the two pixels the comment says the scale 'quietly cost' were taken away from a value the real canvas states 20 times. (2) meet-your-agent.css:232-233 ships `border-radius: 14px 14px 14px 5px; padding: 13px 17px` under a comment at :227-229 reading 'The radius follows the canvas -- one corner squared off toward the speaker'. The canvas does draw that corner, at Vocabulary.dc.html:402 and Inbox.dc.html: `padding: 14px 18px; border-radius: 16px 16px 16px 5px`. `14px 14px 14px 5px` appears in zero boards. The code kept the 5px corner (the part that reads as canvas-faithful) and moved the radius and both padding values off it, while the comment claims the whole thing follows.
fix: For consumer.css:36, either restore 38px/radius 10 to match the mark the canvas actually specifies twenty times, or keep 42px and say it is a consumer-surface decision — but delete the three-artboard corroboration, which is false. For meet-your-agent.css:232-233, adopt the drawn 16px/5px radius and 14px 18px padding (both on-grid, both in the repo) or state the departure. Same treatment for the button recipes at coach-agent-preview.tsx (48px/radius 11 at 'MeetYourAgent.dc.html:101', 56px/radius 12 at ':215') — those are inventions with a line number on them.

source: coach-css+pages
title: The pill control ramps non-monotonically across breakpoints and matches its artboard only at the widest one
why: `.coach-pillbar a` horizontal padding goes 18px at base (:524), 16px at ≥640 (:573), 26px at ≥1280 (:592) — it shrinks as the viewport grows, then more than doubles. A control tuned by a designer ramps in one direction; 18→16→26 is the signature of three rules written independently and never read together. The artboard draws one pill at every width it appears: `gap: 10px; height: 46px; padding: 0 26px` (Main.dc.html:89-90, ErrorState.dc.html:89), so the shipped control matches the canvas only above 1280px. Two related drifts sit in the same cascade: `min-height` is `var(--coach-target)` (44px) at :523 but a bare `46px` at :572, so the declared target token stops governing the control above 640px; and `gap: var(--s-2)` (8px) at :522 is never raised to the artboard's 10px at any breakpoint. Only the 26px step carries a comment (:588-589).
fix: Make the base `gap: 10px; min-height: 46px; padding: 0 26px` per the artboard and let the narrow breakpoint be the single documented reduction, rather than three unrelated steps. If 46px is the real target on this surface, raise `--coach-target` or add a `--coach-target-pill` rather than hardcoding it at one breakpoint.

source: Responsive thresholds are the only design axis in the repo with no tok
tell: arbitrary off-scale magic numbers with no reasoning, in a codebase whose house style is to justify every value inline
title: Four stylesheet breakpoints (959, 1180, 1600, 620) ship bare in sheets where every neighbouring value carries a paragraph of reasoning
why: This repo's stylesheets argue for their numbers at length — coach.css:395-405 spends ten lines explaining why its 380px query is on the container rather than the viewport, and coach.css:610-617 explains 46px→30px title sizing against a named artboard. Against that baseline, four breakpoints arrive with nothing. globals.css:1623 `@media (max-width: 959px)` is the starkest: 959 is off every scale in the project, and unlike coach.css's 639 it has no complementary 960 partner anywhere in the repo, so it is not a min/max pair — it is an orphan one below a round number nobody wrote. globals.css:1486 `min-width: 1600px` and console.css:355 `max-width: 1180px` are likewise bare, the latter sitting directly under a comment that explains the .console-deck--lead layout but never the 1180. consumer.css:1119 `max-width: 1023px` at least lands on lg-1, but is undeclared as such. These read as widths typed to make one screenshot look right rather than chosen from a ladder.
fix: Either give each a reasoning comment in the house style naming what breaks at that width, or snap them to the nearest declared step once a --bp-* family exists — 959→1023 (lg-1) and 1180→1279 (xl-1) are the near-misses; 1600 is a genuine ultrawide clamp and should say so.

source: Date, time and number formatting has no audit scope and is systematica
title: Same semantic role, many spellings: 44 date formatters outside the owning module produce 32 distinct locale/option combinations, including three competing spellings of "a calendar date with a year"
why: datetime.ts exports five pinned formatters covering exactly this ground and is imported by 53 files — yet 44 DateTimeFormat constructors are still built by hand outside it, and 18 of those import WORKSPACE_DISPLAY_TIMEZONE from the module while declining its formatters, so their authors demonstrably knew the module existed. Grouping the 49 total constructors by (locale, option-set) yields 32 distinct combinations. For the single role "a calendar date with its year" the product ships three: workspaceDateFormat's "Sep 4, 2026" (America/New_York), affiliate-home.tsx:134 and affiliate-money.tsx:229's identical field set in UTC, and admin-help.tsx:68's "4 Sept 2026". For "a date with no year" it ships "Sep 3" (day-counter.tsx:75), "3 Sept" (owner-clients.tsx:211), "September 3" (admin-audit-log.tsx:143) and "9/3/2026" (day-counter.tsx:9). For "a long date with weekday": "Friday 4 September 2026" (owner-overview.tsx:77 after its replace), "Tuesday, September 3" (coach-inbox.tsx:200) and "Friday, September 4, 2026" (coach-inbox.tsx:206). day-counter.tsx alone builds three formatters, two of which (lines 75 and 86) render the same visual shape in two different zones inside one function. This is the shape of many independent local decisions, none of which consulted the module written to prevent them.
fix: Fold the recurring shapes into src/lib/format/datetime.ts as named exports (a no-year date, a long weekday date, a month-year period label, an appointment) and replace the local constructors with imports. Keep local constructors only where a genuinely one-off shape is documented, and let the extended guard test from pattern 1 hold the line.
note: The headline number is exact — ripgrep confirms 44 `new Intl.DateTimeFormat` constructors in non-test src outside src/lib/format/datetime.ts. The competing-spellings sub-claim is not just true but understated: I found FOUR spellings of a dated calendar date, not three — "Sep 4, 2026" (canonical en-US), "4 Sept 2026" (en-GB, admin-help.tsx:68 / admin-overview.tsx:103 / admin-measurement-tables.tsx:26), "September 4, 2026" (en-US long, admin-audit-log.tsx:143), "4 September 2026" (en-GB long, connect-channel-flow.ts:131). Where it overstates is the framing "same semantic role." Dumping all 44 into one bucket conflates genuinely different jobs, several with their own reasoning in comments: coach-inbox.tsx:157 is an en-CA sortable day KEY, documented as such; coach-inbox.tsx:206 is the year-only-when-not-this-year heading, documented at :199; coach-setup.tsx:136 is a distinct weekday/long-month role; consumer-experience.tsx builds per-viewer and per-coach zone formatters for a LEAD-facing booking page, a different medium from a workspace surface; quiet-hours/window.ts uses en-CA h23 for computation, not display. My attempt to normalize option sets yielded ~43 raw distinct strings, but path noise inflates that and I could not verify "32" cleanly. Corrected to the sub-claim that actually holds: 4 competing spellings of one role.

source: Date, time and number formatting has no audit scope and is systematica
title: Money has four rendered shapes and a shadowed helper: the canonical money() always prints cents, the design canvas never does, and two files re-declare it byte-for-byte
why: metric.ts:33 exports `money(cents, currency)` with no fraction-digit options, so it always renders "$4,200.00". I inventoried every currency literal in design/coach/: 26 of 26 are written without cents ("$250,000", "$4,500", "$497", "$18"), zero with. So the shared helper contradicts the pixel authority, and the surfaces that noticed worked around it privately rather than fixing it — offer-view-models.ts:49, coach-agent-preview.tsx:131 and meet-agent.tsx:65 each declare their own maximumFractionDigits: 0 currency formatter, while onboarding/view-models.ts:69 and admin-money-pricing-history.ts:50 each independently reinvent the same conditional (`maximumFractionDigits: cents % 100 === 0 ? 0 : 2`). Two more are pure duplication with no behavioural difference at all: view-models.ts:752 (MOVEMENT_CURRENCY) and admin-money-billing-costs.tsx:196 (MARGIN_FORMAT) are `new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", { style: "currency", currency: "USD" })` in files that never import metric.ts — byte-identical output to money(), rebuilt from scratch. Two sites abandon Intl's currency style entirely and hand-prefix a dollar sign: render-placeholders.ts:24 and owner-clients.tsx:688 (`$${Math.round(mrr / 100).toLocaleString("en-US")}`). The naming makes the disconnection explicit: offer-view-models.ts:75 declares `function money(cents, absentText)` and admin-money-pricing-history.ts:49 declares `function money(cents)`, both shadowing the exported `money(cents, currency)` with a different signature and a different rendered shape. Three functions named money in one codebase, none of which agrees with the others on whether a dollar amount has cents.
fix: Give metric.ts's money() an explicit cents policy matching the canvas — e.g. `money(cents, currency, { cents?: boolean })` defaulting to no fraction digits for whole amounts — then delete MOVEMENT_CURRENCY and MARGIN_FORMAT outright and repoint the five bespoke currency formatters and two hand-prefixed sites at it. Rename the two local `money` helpers so they no longer shadow the shared export.
note: Four shapes is right and I verified each: (a) always 2 decimals — canonical money() at metric.ts:33 (pinned by metric.test.ts:11 to "$123.45"), plus view-models.ts:752 and admin-money-billing-costs.tsx:196; (b) 0 decimals — offer-view-models.ts:49, admin-measurement-view-models.ts:96-99; (c) conditional 0-or-2 — admin-money-pricing-history.ts:49-54, `maximumFractionDigits: cents % 100 === 0 ? 0 : 2`; (d) hand-built — owner-clients.tsx:688, `` `$${Math.round(mrr / 100).toLocaleString("en-US")}` ``. Two claims fail. "Byte-for-byte" is simply false: offer-view-models.ts:75 is `money(cents: number | null, absentText: string): OfferReviewValue` and admin-money-pricing-history.ts:49 is `money(cents: number)` — different signatures, different digit rules, different return types from metric.ts's `money(cents, currency)`. They shadow the canonical NAME with divergent behaviour, which is a fair finding, but not a duplicate. "The design canvas never [prints cents]" is unsupported: every amount in design/coach/*.dc.html is a round offer price or funding goal ($250,000, $497, $50) — round by nature, not a stated no-cents rule. And render-placeholders.ts:24 is agent message text substituted into SMS/DM copy sent to leads, outside datetime.ts's own stated scope of "a workspace surface."

source: kit-shell
title: One control's horizontal padding takes four different values across the canvas and two files
why: The coach pillbar tab is a single visual relationship — label inside a pill — and it is given four horizontal paddings by three authorities that never reconcile. The canvas draws `padding: 0 26px` (identically at AccountMenu.dc.html:89 and Main.dc.html:90). coach.css:524 sets the base rule to `padding: 0 18px`. coach.css:573 overrides it at min-width 640px to `padding: 0 16px`. coach-pillbar.tsx:109 overrides it below 640px to `max-sm:px-[4px]!` — with a bang, because it is fighting the 18px base rule from the other file. The canvas value of 26px is used at none of the three breakpoints, so the drawn control ships nowhere. The same drift hits the inner gap: the canvas pill is `gap: 10px`, coach.css:522 is `gap: var(--s-2)` (8px). None of the three shipped values is wrong on its own; the tell is that no file knows what the other two chose, and the override chain crosses a TSX/CSS boundary using `!important` to win.
fix: Pick one value per breakpoint and state it once. Put the tab's horizontal padding in coach.css only (it already owns min-height, border-radius and color for the same selector), as a token — the phone value is the deliberate one and the desktop value should be the canvas's 26px or a documented departure from it. Then drop the `max-sm:px-[4px]!` from coach-pillbar.tsx:109 so the `!` is no longer needed to cross the file boundary.
note: All five citations verify: Main.dc.html:90 and AccountMenu.dc.html:89 both draw the pill `padding: 0 26px; height: 46px; font-size: 17px; font-weight: 500`; coach.css:524 sets `padding: 0 18px`; coach.css:573 sets `padding: 0 16px` inside @media (min-width: 640px); coach-pillbar.tsx:109 ships max-sm:px-[4px]!. The gap drift verifies too (canvas gap: 10px vs coach.css:522 gap: var(--s-2)). This is the one finding with a real visual consequence: the well around the pills at coach.css:564-568 is byte-exact to AccountMenu.dc.html:88 (gap 4px, padding 5px, 999px radius, --line, --well) and the pill's height/size/weight/transparent hairline are byte-exact to :89 — so the single property that was NOT copied is the horizontal padding, 16px against a drawn 26px, five pills wide, on the coach's primary navigation. A designer holding the artboard next to the build sees a bar ~100px narrower. Two corrections. First, the 18px base at coach.css:524 is not a fourth shipping value, it is dead: max-sm covers <640px and the media query covers >=640px, so it is never the effective padding — which is worse than drift, but it is one dead declaration rather than a third live one. Second, the `!important` half of the complaint is documented, not slop: coach.css:552-556 explains that coach.css is unlayered and therefore beats bare Tailwind utilities, which is why the phone overrides carry the bang. Severity medium rather than high — one control, and the override mechanism is a stated architectural constraint.

source: cards
tell: (6)-adjacent — box-shadow stacks that fake depth on an already-layered ground system
title: Four bespoke shadow stacks at 2-3x the sanctioned alpha, none matching a token, on surfaces that already carry their own ground
why: tokens.css:222-230 states the light palette's whole shadow position: every rung casts the text ink tinted 262 "at a fifth of the opacity" of the dark palette's, because "on a light page that same shadow reads as dirt." The deepest rung a card on the page may take, `--shadow-open`, tops out at `rgba(28,42,82,0.2)`. owner-overview.tsx:535 casts `0 18px 40px -22px rgba(28,42,82,0.6)` — triple that — on a card that already has its own dark ground, so the shadow is doing nothing the ground separation is not. context-eye.tsx:355 is `--shadow-raised`'s exact middle layer geometry (`0 10px 26px -10px`, tokens.css:233) with the alpha raised 0.16 → 0.5, plus a `0_0_0_3px_rgba(176,116,32,0.25)` amber ring on a floating button at rest — DESIGN.md:399-400 names "a button at rest" as a defect case for a lit edge. The tell is the near-miss family: `0 18px 40px -22px` at 0.6, at 0.35 (meet-agent.tsx:270), and `0 18px 40px -18px` at 0.6 (context-eye.tsx:270) are three variants of one stack that nobody reconciled. For contrast, the design canvas writes a raw shadow exactly twice across all 22 artboards, and both are the same toggle knob (`0 1px 2px rgba(28, 42, 82, 0.3)`, Vocabulary.dc.html:284 and Inbox.dc.html:178) — faithfully reproduced at coach-inbox.tsx:1042.
fix: Map each to the rung it means: `var(--shadow-raised)` for the two popovers, `var(--shadow-card)` for the panel, and drop the extra layer on owner-overview.tsx entirely — a drenched card is already separated from the pane by its ground, which is the whole four-ground argument. Remove the amber ring at context-eye.tsx:355.

source: unlayered-cascade.test.ts attributes classes per-file, so a collision
title: KNOWN's explanatory comments describe seven collision rows that are not in the table, and the row-count warning is stale by an order of magnitude
why: The stale-entry assertion at :602-603 forces a row to be deleted the moment it stops colliding, but nothing deletes the paragraph that explained it, so three comment blocks now document rows that do not exist. :445-451 ends 'What is left here is one padding override that has no ruling yet' - there is no padding row anywhere in KNOWN (grep for a key containing `padding` returns 0). :453-458 explains rows for `.t-faint` on the exception tile, `.t-id` and `.t-body` on key-value, 'two channel-health colours' and 'record-sheet's `--t-body` on `.t-id`' - the table holds exactly one of those, exception-tile's `t-body color`. :472-473 ends the table with 'so all three of these spacings collapse to 0' followed immediately by the closing brace and no rows at all. Separately, :432-435 warns a reader to budget carefully against 'the nineteen `debt` rows... thirty places across thirteen files' - the table now holds 2 debt rows and 5 deliberate, 7 total. A lane reading this file to plan work is handed a backlog description that overstates the table by 9x while the actual backlog (11 live dead declarations from patterns 2 and 3) is absent from it entirely. The register is wrong in both directions at once.
fix: Delete the three orphaned comment blocks at :445-451, the unbacked clauses in :453-458, and :472-473, or restore the rows they describe if those collisions are real. Rewrite :432-435 to state the current counts, and add an assertion that every non-`*` KNOWN key's file appears in at least one comment and vice versa, so prose and rows cannot drift apart again.

source: coach-css+pages
title: The gap between a figure and the line beneath it takes three values, none of them the canvas's or the token's
why: `.coach-panel__sentence` (the caption under the deck figure) gets `margin-top: 10px` at :470. `.coach-notice__counter` gets `margin-top: 10px` at :835. `.coach-panel__stat-note` gets `margin: 8px 0 0` at :920. All three are the same relationship — a supporting line directly under the number it explains — and the deck panel's own artboard draws it at `margin-top: 12px` (`Main.dc.html:128`, the exact line coach.css already cites at :820 for a different property on the same element). 12px is also `--s-3`, aliased by `--d-stack-gap` and described in tokens.css:292 as "a control row -> the thing it controls". So the token exists, the canvas agrees with the token, and the sheet ships 10px twice and 8px once instead. This is the drift the tokens.css:291 comment ("the rhythm cannot drift off the 4px grid") was written to prevent, in the one place the token was designed for. Related: coach.css declares no page-head or section rhythm at all and never references `--d-head-gap` (20px) or `--d-section-gap` (32px), though `Main.dc.html:108` draws the page head to first block at exactly `margin-bottom: 32px`.
fix: Set all three to `var(--d-stack-gap)` (12px), matching both the artboard and the token. If the stat note is genuinely tighter, say so in a comment and use `var(--s-2)` rather than a bare 8px.

source: contrast
title: Primary CTA label drops to 4.28:1 on hover in dark, because dark's accent-hover lightens toward the label
why: consumer.css:719 sets color: var(--on-accent) on .consumer-primary-button and :753 swaps its background to var(--accent-hover) on hover. Measured: light on-accent on accent-hover = 7.30:1, and tokens.css:138 records exactly that number in a comment. Dark = 4.28:1, under AA, and tokens.css:472/:626 carry no ratio comment at all. The cause is a rule stated for one palette and silently inverted in the other: tokens.css:134 says "--accent-hover and --accent-active darken rather than lighten, because on a light ground pressing something has to feel like pushing it further in". In dark, --accent-active does darken (0.5306 -> 0.4515, on-accent 7.24) but --accent-hover LIGHTENS (0.5306 -> 0.5765), walking the ground toward the near-white label. The base state is 5.19:1, so hover is the only state that fails -- the worst possible place for it, since hover is when the reader is committing. The same token used as a foreground (consumer.css:329, .consumer-human-button:hover) measures 4.11 on --card and 4.41 on --row-hover over --canvas in dark, versus 6.40 in light. tokens-contrast.test.ts never measures --on-accent or --accent-hover in any palette.
fix: In tokens.css:472 and :626 take dark --accent-hover down rather than up -- oklch(0.49 0.115 264) restores on-accent to ~5.9:1 and still reads as a state change against the 0.5306 base. Then add an on-accent-over-accent/hover/active/fill-stops assertion to tokens-contrast.test.ts; it currently has none.
note: The core measurement is exactly right. I computed dark --on-accent oklch(0.99 0.003 267) on --accent-hover oklch(0.5765 0.12 265) = 4.28:1, versus base 5.19:1 and active 7.24:1; light hover = 7.30:1, which is precisely the number tokens.css:138 records. tokens.css:472 and :626 do declare dark --accent-hover with no ratio comment, and tokens.css:134/829 do state the darken-on-press rule for light only. The count of 3 --accent-hover call sites is exactly correct (consumer.css:329, :752, :753 -- the only three in src). .consumer-primary-button is 16px/600 (--consumer-body: 16px), so 4.5 is the right floor, and nothing forces the consumer surface to light, so dark is reachable. Two problems. First, the citation consumer.css:719 is wrong: line 719 is the closing brace of the .consumer-booking p rule; color: var(--on-accent) on the primary button is at line 734. Second, the secondary figure is wrong: dark --accent-hover as a foreground measures 4.27 on --card, not the claimed 4.11 (row-hover-over-canvas 4.41 is correct). Substantively this is a hover-only, 5% shortfall on one control, and lightening on hover is the ordinary dark-mode convention -- the inverse of the light rule rather than a silent contradiction of it. Real AA miss, but not high severity.

source: Date, number and locale formatting consistency — no scope owned it, no
title: Three functions named formatMetric; the money and duration branches disagree with the canonical one
why: metric.ts:40 exports `formatMetric(value, format)`. Two view-model files define a private function of the same name and role over the same metric registry, and the three disagree on output. Money: metric.ts:33-38 `money()` uses Intl currency defaults (2dp) → "$123.45"; admin-measurement-view-models.ts:96-100 sets `maximumFractionDigits: 0` → "$123". Duration: metric.ts:45-48 uses Intl `style: "unit"` with 1dp → "1.5 min", "2 hr"; both copies hand-roll `Math.round(value / 60)` + a literal " min" → "2 min". admin-overview.tsx imports the canonical `formatMetric` at :34 (used at :260, :292, :742, :939, :1200) while simultaneously consuming `PlatformMetricView.value` strings produced by the shadow copy imported at :53, so one page renders cents both ways. That the copies are aware of the original makes it worse, not better: admin-measurement-view-models.ts:88-89 cites it by name — "One decimal is what the shared formatter in `lib/format/metric.ts` uses" — and still reimplements the whole function beside it. Contrast kit/stat-strip.tsx:136-142, which faced the same pull and documented why it delegates instead.
fix: Collapse both view-model copies onto `formatMetric` from @/lib/format/metric, mapping `definition.unit` → MetricFormat once (admin-overview.tsx:115-119 already has that mapping written). Where a surface genuinely needs 0-decimal money, that belongs as a parameter on `money()`, not a fourth implementation.

source: public/site/ — the page that actually serves `/` in production — is 2,
title: Every guard that claims to police `/` is aimed at a file the flag rewrites away; the live page breaks both of its assertions
why: entry-surfaces.test.ts:26-27 declares `"/": ["app/page.tsx"]` and then asserts, at :68-72, that entry surfaces "name no colour of their own" by failing on any `#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}` match, and at :82-83 that they "load no stylesheet of their own". public-surfaces.test.ts:29 separately names `"/ (marketing, flagged)": "components/marketing/landing-page.tsx"` as the flagged `/`. next.config.ts:16-19 rewrites `/` to `/site/index.html` under exactly the flag public-surfaces names, so with the flag on neither file renders. The page that does render carries 63 distinct hex literals (140 occurrences) and loads its own stylesheet at index.html:12 — precisely the two things the guard for `/` exists to forbid. A repo-wide grep for `public/site` or `scrollcraft` across src/, tests/ and scripts/ returns nothing: 2,674 lines of the highest-stakes design surface have zero test coverage, while the 590-line dead React page has two dedicated guards. That gap is why every other pattern in this report survived.
fix: Add the served page to the guards rather than the source page. Either extend ENTRY_PAGES with `"/ (flagged)": ["../public/site/index.html"]` behind an HTML-aware reader that skips third-party device-mock blocks, or add a public-site.test.ts that pins the same three rules (no unexplained hex, no second token layer, the four-block theme model). Correct public-surfaces.test.ts:29 to name the file the flag actually serves.
note: Verified, and worse than stated. next.config.ts:16-19 puts the rewrite in `beforeFiles`, which pre-empts the filesystem, so when SETTERFI_PUBLIC_LANDING_LIVE=true the static page serves `/` and src/app/page.tsx never runs. But page.tsx:133 gates its own marketing surface on the SAME flag -- `if (publicLandingLive()) return <LandingPage plans={await landingPlans()} />` -- so src/components/marketing/landing-page.tsx (32KB) is unreachable in both flag states: flag on, the rewrite wins; flag off, page.tsx returns <RolePicker/>. Its generateMetadata branch (page.tsx:25-31) is dead for the same reason. Meanwhile entry-surfaces.test.ts:27 pins `/` to app/page.tsx and asserts no hex literal (:68-72) and no second stylesheet (:82-83), and public-surfaces.test.ts:29 labels landing-page.tsx as "/ (marketing, flagged)" -- while the page actually served carries 60+ raw hex literals and its own stylesheet. The guard's own docblock (entry-surfaces.test.ts:8-19) says the defect it exists to prevent is "the first page a visitor loaded was the only page in the product not made of tokens.css", which is true again. docs/SETUP.md:215 compounds it: "With the flag off, `/` still renders the React landing page in `src/app/page.tsx`" -- with the flag off page.tsx renders the role picker, not the landing page. Not high: the flag is blank by default in .env.example:162 and SETUP.md does document the rewrite, so the default configuration is coherent.

source: Responsive thresholds are the only design axis in the repo with no tok
tell: self-inconsistency — the same conceptual boundary given two numbers in different sheets, against a stated single-line principle
title: The phone boundary is 640px in coach.css and 620px in globals.css and consumer.css — three sheets, two answers
why: coach.css states the principle explicitly at lines 614-616: 'The breakpoint is 640px, the same line the pill bar uses to become the phone's tab strip, so the whole surface changes density once rather than at two different widths.' That is a decision, argued and worth keeping. The other two surfaces then answer the same question differently: globals.css:1729 bumps agent-dialog buttons to a 44px touch target at max-width 620, and consumer.css:1166 wraps the preview marker instead of slicing it at max-width 620 — both are 'this is a phone now' rules, set 20px inside the line coach.css argues for. A third spelling exists in JSX at admin-inbox.tsx:351 as @min-[620px]/attention. So the app carries a phone line at 620, at 639/640, and at Tailwind's stock sm=640 used 233 times, with only one of the three reasoned. The coach surface's own principle — change once, not at two widths — is exactly what the 620/640 split breaks at product scale.
fix: Move the two 620px media queries (globals.css:1729, consumer.css:1166) and the @min-[620px] at admin-inbox.tsx:351 onto the 639/640 line coach.css already argues for, so one number means 'phone' across all four surfaces; if 620 is deliberate for the agent and consumer shells, say why in a comment the way coach.css:610-617 does.

source: Disabled and inactive states are drawn by fading the element, at three
title: DESIGN.md's skeleton rule names --pulse-*, and the tokens are declared, reduced-motion-overridden, and consumed by nothing
why: docs/DESIGN.md:616-617 states the rule as a Do: 'render a skeleton at the exact proportions the loaded page arrives in, pulsing on --pulse-*'. tokens.css:352-354 declares --pulse-dur: 1000ms, --pulse-count: 1, --pulse-min: 0.5 under the comment 'Skeleton loader and reveal', and globals.css:1878 dutifully collapses --pulse-dur to 0.001ms under reduced motion. Grep for pulse-dur|pulse-count|pulse-min across all of src outside those two stylesheets returns nothing. Both skeletons ignore the rule in opposite directions: ui/skeleton.tsx:7 is stock shadcn (`animate-pulse rounded-md bg-muted`, Tailwind's own 2s cubic-bezier, not the token); kit/skeleton.tsx:14-16 explicitly sets animate-none and substitutes a hardcoded `skeleton-shimmer_1.6s` sweep with before:opacity-50. A named animation contract that survives a reduced-motion override but has no callers is generated scaffolding, not a system - and it means the one loading treatment DESIGN.md actually specifies is the one nothing implements.
fix: Either drive kit/skeleton.tsx's shimmer duration from var(--pulse-dur) and delete the 1.6s literal, or delete --pulse-dur/--pulse-count/--pulse-min and their globals.css:1878 override and amend the DESIGN.md line to describe the shimmer that actually ships. Do not leave a documented token with no consumer.

source: Disabled and inactive states are drawn by fading the element, at three
tell: self-inconsistency (the repo states the right answer in a comment and then ships the wrong one)
title: A decided, opacity-free refused state exists and is used twice; step-journey rejects the fade in its own comment and then inherits it
why: The house pattern is already written down twice. go-live-step.tsx:88-97 defines STEP_REFUSED_CLASS as a fully opaque face - border-[var(--line)], bg-[var(--control-fill)], text-[color:var(--muted)], cursor-not-allowed, no opacity anywhere - under a comment that rejects the alternative by name: 'It is deliberately not the accent face at reduced opacity... wearing it while the press is refused would say the work is finished'. kit/matrix-checkbox.tsx:61 does the same for a locked cell, and matrix-checkbox.test.tsx:28 pins it: 'marks a locked cell with a lock and a reason, not opacity alone'. Then kit/step-journey.tsx:288-289 writes the identical intent in its comment - 'Sequenced, not greyed-out primary: the action stays visible and named so the coach knows what is coming' - and on the very next lines (:291-292) renders <Button aria-disabled='true' disabled>, whose base class at ui/button.tsx:13 is disabled:opacity-50. The comment says not-greyed-out; the component greys out. That single site proves the 43 fades are drift rather than policy: the repo knows the right answer, wrote it down, tested it once, and then let the stock shadcn default overwrite it everywhere else.
fix: Promote go-live-step.tsx's STEP_REFUSED_CLASS into kit/atomics/button-class.ts as a named `refused` variant (opaque --control-fill face, --muted label, no multiplier, reason text alongside), point step-journey.tsx:292 at it instead of disabled, and make it the target the other 43 sites migrate to.

source: Every design guard in the repo roots its scan at src/ or narrower, so
title: Three guards spend their whole perimeter on a marketing module that `/` does not serve, and the repo's own two descriptions of `/` disagree
why: public-surfaces.test.ts:29 registers `"/ (marketing, flagged)": "components/marketing/landing-page.tsx"` as the public landing surface and holds it to CoachScale, the shadcn ban and the hex ban; palette-literals.test.ts:62 grants that same file an OVER_DRENCH exemption; ghl-branding-wall.test.ts:62 lists src/components/marketing as a client entry directory. src/app/page.tsx:133 renders it only when publicLandingLive(), and next.config.ts:16-19 rewrites `/` to `/site/index.html` on exactly the same env value (env-contract.ts:576 and next.config.ts:17 both test `=== "true"`), with the rewrite in `beforeFiles`. So on the flag-on path the static page answers `/` and on the flag-off path page.tsx returns the role picker -- LandingPage renders at `/` in neither.
