The repo says both things: env-contract.ts:565-566 states 'On, `/` renders the marketing page', while SETUP.md:209-212 states the flag 'makes next.config.ts rewrite `/` to `/site/index.html`' and then adds, incorrectly, 'With the flag off, `/` still renders the React landing page in src/app/page.tsx'. public-landing-flag.test.tsx:16-20 reasons from the first and concludes that entry-surfaces 'is deliberately untouched' and 'Nothing was relaxed to let the page through' -- a coverage claim about a file that is not the page. The two titles differ too: page.tsx:27's metadata versus index.html:6's 'SetterFi. The AI setter for funding coaches.' I could not read Next's rewrite docs to settle beforeFiles ordering (node_modules is partial here), so I am reporting the disagreement rather than the winner; either way one of the two landing surfaces is dead and the guards are pointed at whichever it is.
fix: Settle which page `/` serves, then make the three guards name it: if it is the static site, point public-surfaces' `/` row and ghl-branding-wall at public/site (see pattern 1) and delete the marketing module with its OVER_DRENCH row; if it is LandingPage, delete the next.config.ts:16-19 rewrite. Correct SETUP.md:212's flag-off sentence and env-contract.ts:565-566 either way, and re-check public-landing-flag.test.tsx:16-20's coverage claim against the answer.

source: admin-console
title: DataState's own technical disclosure is pasted into three pages instead of passed as a prop, and the third copy diverges
why: data-state.tsx:143-146 already renders exactly this disclosure, from the `code` prop, for `kind:"error"`. compliance:293-296 and brain:404-407 are character-identical clones of those three lines (only `max-w-full` becomes `max-w-[var(--measure-prose)]`), pasted after a `kind:"unavailable"` DataState that drops `code`. overview:64-70 is the same widget in different clothes: `text-body text-[var(--muted)]` and `text-body text-[var(--faint)]` instead of `t-faint`/`t-id`, plus `font-medium text-[var(--accent-text)]` on the summary and no `select-none`. tokens.css:1009/1015 put t-faint and t-id at 12px; `text-body` resolves to the 13.5px console body (console.css:469). So one disclosure is 12px monochrome on two pages and 13.5px with an accent-coloured summary on the third. All three sit outside the `<main>` DataState emits (data-state.tsx:115), so the code aligns to the card's outer edge rather than its text column — while error.tsx:28-34 does the same job correctly through `kind="error"` + `code`. A kit `TechnicalDetail` component with 10+ consumers exists and none of the three uses it.
fix: Extend DataState's `unavailable` variant to accept `code` (it already has the render path), delete all three inline `<details>` blocks, and let the shared component own the type ramp and the placement.
note: Every citation checks out and the visual claim holds. data-state.tsx:143-146 renders this exact disclosure from the code prop; compliance/page.tsx:293-296 and brain/page.tsx:404-407 are clones of it; overview/page.tsx:64-71 is the same widget rebuilt from different classes. I confirmed the size divergence by hand: globals.css:71 maps text-body to var(--t-body), console.css:469 sets --t-body to 13.5px inside [data-shell-role=admin], while tokens.css:1009 and :1015 hold t-faint and t-id at 12px. So the same failure state renders 12px monochrome with a select-none summary on two pages, and 13.5px with a font-medium --accent-text summary and no select-none on the third. All three sit outside the <main> that FailureState emits (data-state.tsx:115), which has p-[var(--s-4)], so 'Technical detail' hangs 16px left of the card's own text column - error.tsx:28-34 does the same job correctly through kind="error" + code. One correction to the framing: it could NOT have been 'passed as a prop' as written - data-state.tsx:34 types kind:"unavailable" without a code field, so making this a prop is a type change, not a call-site fix. And TechnicalDetail (technical-detail.tsx:34) takes items:{label,value}[] and renders a bordered card with CopyValue, so it is not a drop-in for a bare <code> either; its 12 consumers are real but it is not the substitute the finding implies. The duplication and the divergence stand.

source: tokens+globals
title: One vertical column, four different inline gutters at the same viewport - the left edges do not line up
why: The agent shell stacks topbar / chat-heading / chat-scroll / composer-shell / agent-embedded-actions in one column, so their inline padding is a single visual relationship - the column's left edge. It is authored four ways. Base: topbar 18px (349), chat-heading 20px (544), chat-scroll 20px (641), composer-shell 18px (849), embedded-actions 18px (955), trace regions 18px (976, 1166, 1173, 1272, 1285), dialog 22px (1325). Then @media (max-width:959px) moves the topbar alone to 12px (1632), and @media (max-width:620px) moves chat-heading and chat-scroll to 14px (1759-1760) and composer-shell to 12px (1764-1765) while .agent-embedded-actions - which renders inside the same column, directly under the composer - gets no override and stays at 18px. So on a 600px-wide phone the four stacked regions of one column indent at 12 / 14 / 12 / 18px. That is a visible misalignment a designer would catch in one screenshot, and none of the four numbers is on the 4px scale except by accident. The responsive overrides were clearly written per-rule as each region was touched, never checked against each other.
fix: Introduce one gutter variable on .agent-shell (`--agent-gutter`), set it once per breakpoint (var(--s-5) desktop, var(--s-3) at 620px), and have all five regions read `padding-inline: var(--agent-gutter)`. Delete the three per-rule responsive overrides at 1632, 1759-1760 and 1764-1765.
note: A misalignment exists, but not the one described, and three of the five citations are dead or misread code. (1) globals.css:1632 (.agent-topbar padding 8px 12px under max-width:959px) never applies to this component: meet-your-agent.css:127 sets `[data-shell-role="coach"].agent-shell .agent-topbar { min-height: 76px; padding: 0 var(--s-5) }` at specificity 0,2,0 against the media rule's 0,1,0, and media queries add no specificity. Same for globals.css:1759 (.chat-heading) -- meet-your-agent.css:188 sets `:where(.chat-heading, .trace-heading) { min-height: 78px; padding: 19px 22px }` at 0,2,0 and wins. Both mounts render <CoachScale> (meet-your-agent.tsx:583), so this always applies. (2) globals.css:955 is misread: the same rule carries `margin: 12px -18px calc(...)` and .agent-embedded-actions is a CHILD of .composer-shell (meet-your-agent.tsx:814 and :911). The -18px margin cancels the shell's 18px padding and the 18px padding restores it, so its content aligns with the composer exactly -- a full-bleed strip, not a fourth gutter. The real shipped numbers are 20/22/20/18 at base and 20/22/14/12 below 620px. The genuine defect is the inverse of the claim: because the coach layer outranks the responsive rules, the panel header band stays at 22px while the message column drops to 14px and the composer to 12px, so on a phone the heading sits 8px inboard of the messages under it. Also, below 620px the embedded-actions strip's -18px margin overshoots the shell's 12px padding by 6px per side. Two real mismatches, both mobile-only, both caused by a specificity fight the auditor did not see.

source: icons
title: The kit hand-copies lucide paths for glyphs it already exports, three lines below importing from itself
why: app-topbar.tsx:3 imports twelve Phosphor glyphs from `@/components/kit/icons`. Then app-topbar.tsx:260 defines `AgentMark()`, an inline svg on viewBox="0 0 24 24" at stroke-width 1.75 whose path `M21 11.5a8.38 8.38 0 0 1-.9 3.8 8.5 8.5 0 0 1-7.6 4.7...` is lucide's `message-circle` verbatim - while icons.tsx:144 exports `ChatIcon` (Phosphor ChatCircle) for exactly that meaning. deck-panel.tsx:227 does the same thing smaller: `DeckPanelChevron()` inline-draws `M9 6l6 6-6 6`, lucide's `chevron-right`, when icons.tsx:174 exports `ChevronRight`. Both sit inside the module boundary whose header (icons.tsx:5-13) says two families live here and nothing else does, so the kit is violating its own stated rule in its own files. The result is visible rather than academic: at app-topbar.tsx:530 the hand-drawn stroked AgentMark renders in the same topbar row as the filled Phosphor Bell (app-topbar.tsx:616) and Search (app-topbar.tsx:588) - one stroked outline beside two filled glyphs. This is distinct from the coach surfaces' inline SVGs, which VOCABULARY.md:71 explicitly sanctions, and from impersonation-banner.tsx:285 which justifies drawing inline in writing; these two are unjustified duplicates of exports already in scope.
fix: Replace `<AgentMark />` at app-topbar.tsx:530 with the exported `ChatIcon`, and `<DeckPanelChevron />` in deck-panel.tsx with the exported `ChevronRight`, then delete both local functions. If the topbar mark is intentionally not a chat bubble, name it and add it to icons.tsx as a seventh bespoke mark on the documented 16px/1.5-stroke grid rather than as a loose 24-grid copy.

source: The design system's own type-role utility layer is mostly dead, and on
title: The one class DESIGN.md names by explicit rule is hand-rolled at its only intended callsite, with tracking drifted 2x
why: DESIGN.md:351 states the rule: "One `.t-hero` (mono 500, 44px) is permitted, on Overview only." `.t-hero` has zero consumers. Overview draws that exact figure by hand at owner-overview.tsx:881 — `font-mono text-[44px] leading-none font-medium tabular-nums text-[var(--ink)]` — five utilities reproducing one class, and the hand-roll uses `tracking-[-0.05em]` where `--t-hero-tr` is `-0.024em`, a 2.1x drift on the one element the doc singles out. Same failure one line up in tokens.css: `.t-figure` (mono 22px/500/1.1/-0.01em) has one consumer, while owner-money.tsx:499 hand-rolls it as `font-mono text-[22px] leading-none tracking-[-0.05em]` — 5x tracking drift and lh 1.0 against the role's 1.1. This is the precise damage the class layer was built to prevent, occurring at the callsites the docs name.
fix: Replace owner-overview.tsx:881 with `className="t-hero"` and owner-money.tsx:499 with `t-figure` plus its tone class. If -0.05em is the intended look, move it into `--t-hero-tr`/`--t-figure-tr` so the doc and the pixels agree.
note: Every citation checks out and the drift is real and visible. DESIGN.md:351 reads 'One `.t-hero` (mono 500, 44px) is permitted, on Overview only.' tokens.css:1067 declares --t-hero: 44px / -w: 500 / -lh: 1.0 / -tr: -0.024em, and tokens.css:1109 builds .t-hero from them. owner-overview.tsx:881 -- the Overview surface, the single callsite the doc names -- spells the recipe by hand instead: 'font-mono text-[44px] leading-none font-medium tracking-[-0.05em] tabular-nums text-[var(--ink)]'. Family, size, weight, leading, numerics and color all match the class exactly; the one property that differs is tracking, -0.05em against the token's -0.024em, i.e. 2.08x. .t-hero has zero consumers repo-wide, so the class DESIGN.md wrote a named rule for is never used at the one place the rule permits it. The same pattern repeats one rung down: tokens.css:1110 defines .t-figure (22px / 1.1 / -0.01em) and it is live via stat-strip.tsx:117, yet owner-money.tsx:499 hand-rolls 'font-mono text-[22px] leading-none tracking-[-0.05em]', drifting tracking 5x and line-height from 1.1 to 1.0. This is visible: at 44px, -0.05em versus -0.024em is ~1.1px tighter per glyph, roughly 7-9px across the largest figure on the Overview page.

source: Orphaned dead CSS — named in the audit brief as a tell-adjacent axis,
title: svg.i.i-sm / svg.i.i-lg: a parallel icon-sizing recipe with zero occurrences anywhere in the repo
why: `i-sm` and `i-lg` appear in exactly two places in the entire repository, and both are their own declarations at tokens.css:995-996. Not a single call site in src/**/*.tsx, in any of the 22 design/coach/*.dc.html artboards, or in public/site. They are a size-variant API invented for a base rule the application itself never uses either: `svg.i` at tokens.css:994 has zero occurrences in src/** (`className="i"` count: 0) and is live only inside the design canvas, where `class="i"` appears 226 times across the artboards. The shipped app draws icons through lucide-react and @phosphor-icons/react via `@/components/kit/icons`. So the sheet the product loads carries a three-rule icon system for markup the product does not write, two thirds of which nothing anywhere writes. A small/large pair generated alongside a base rule 'because a size scale should have variants' is the shape of a recipe that was produced rather than needed.
fix: Delete tokens.css:995-996. Keep `svg.i` at :994 only if the design canvas is meant to keep reading the same tokens file, and if so add a one-line comment saying it exists for design/coach/*.dc.html rather than for the app, so the next reader does not assume it is product CSS.

source: Date, time and number formatting has no audit scope and is systematica
title: Display zone is split roughly in half — 14 UTC against 18 America/New_York — and one clone of the canonical timestamp differs from it only by zone
why: datetime.ts:63-72 permits UTC in exactly one circumstance — a metric's methodology line, where metric-definitions.ts already declares clock: "UTC." — and insists the marker be part of the string, "because 'Aug 17, 2026, 4:35 PM' with no zone is the same ambiguity written more confidently"; utcTimestampLabel (line 86) duly appends " UTC". Of the 14 UTC display formatters outside src/lib/format, none appends a zone marker. Several are legitimate and documented (see clean list), but the rest print a plain instant in the wrong clock with nothing to warn the reader. coach-leads-model.ts:184 is the sharpest: its option set — month short, day numeric, hour numeric, minute 2-digit — is field-for-field identical to workspaceDateTimeFormat (datetime.ts:37), differing only in `timeZone: "UTC"`, so the leads board prints "Sep 4, 4:35 PM" for the same instant the inbox two clicks away prints as "Sep 4, 12:35 pm" — a four-hour and sometimes one-calendar-day disagreement between two coach surfaces. Its own docstring one line above reads "One format for every date this screen prints, so two cards cannot spell a day two ways." admin-help.tsx:68, owner-overview.tsx:77 and :91, and admin-overview.tsx:103 format arbitrary server instants (not civil dates) in UTC with no marker.
fix: Repoint coach-leads-model.ts:184 at workspaceDateTimeFormat and delete the clone. For the remaining unmarked UTC display formatters, decide per site: an instant a coach reads goes through the WORKSPACE_DISPLAY_TIMEZONE formatters; a genuine UTC methodology reading goes through utcTimestampLabel so it carries its " UTC" suffix. Leave the documented civil-date UTC formatters alone.
note: The counts mix scopes. `timeZone: "UTC"` is 15 total, 14 outside datetime.ts; `timeZone: WORKSPACE_DISPLAY_TIMEZONE` is 18 total but 4 of those ARE datetime.ts's own formatters, leaving 14 outside. So the real outside-module split is 14 vs 14, and the quoted "18" silently counts the owning module against itself. More importantly, most of the UTC half is documented, not drift: datetime.ts:66-73 explains at length why UTC is correct for measurement surfaces because metric-definitions.ts declares `clock: "UTC."` beside each window, and admin-overview.tsx, admin-measurement-tables.tsx, owner-overview.tsx, owner-money.tsx, affiliate-money.tsx and trend-panel.tsx are exactly those surfaces. The clone sub-claim, however, is CONFIRMED and is the real finding: coach-leads-model.ts:184 `boardDateFormat` is en-US {month:"short", day, hour, minute} — option-for-option identical to the canonical workspaceDateTimeFormat at datetime.ts:37 — differing ONLY in `timeZone: "UTC"`. It sits under a docstring at :183 reading "One format for every date this screen prints, so two cards cannot spell a day two ways," while in fact spelling the coach's day four hours off every other coach surface (coach-inbox, coach-billing, coach-setup all pin WORKSPACE_DISPLAY_TIMEZONE). admin-help.tsx:68 is the second defensible one — a help/guide generated-at stamp, not a measurement window, so the UTC rationale does not cover it.

source: src/lib was in no scope, yet it is a presentation layer: it holds the
tell: duplicated logic behind a one-substring guard
title: theme.ts keeps two hand-written copies of the theme resolution and a test that only checks a shared string
why: theme.ts:63-67 `applyTheme` stamps three markers (data-theme, data-workspace-theme, and the `dark` class). theme.ts:69 THEME_BOOT_SCRIPT is a 380-character minified string literal that re-implements readStoredTheme + systemTheme + applyTheme from scratch so the stamp lands before first paint. The two agree today, but nothing executes the string: theme.test.ts:12-13 asserts only that the storage key appears in both, and :17-32 exercises applyTheme against a stub root. A fourth marker added to applyTheme, or a change to how 'system' resolves, silently forks the pre-hydration paint from every render after it, and the only test would still pass. The three markers also have unequal footing: `data-theme` has a real no-JS fallback in tokens.css (bare :root plus the prefers-color-scheme block), `data-workspace-theme` is a JS-to-JS channel read at app-topbar.tsx:246, and the `dark` class is what globals.css:5 binds Tailwind's dark variant to (`&:where(.dark, .dark *)`) -- so on a dark-preferring load with JS off, the whole token palette flips while the 25 `dark:` utilities in the tree stay in their light branch. Those utilities are almost all in vendored src/components/ui/, which is why this is medium rather than high, but the fork is real and undocumented.
fix: Derive THEME_BOOT_SCRIPT from the same functions instead of retyping them, or add a test that evals the boot script against a jsdom document and asserts it produces byte-identical dataset and classList state to applyTheme for all three inputs (stored 'light', stored 'dark', absent + matchMedia dark). Separately, note in tokens.css or DESIGN.md that Tailwind's dark: variant is class-bound and therefore JS-only, so nobody reaches for it expecting the media-query fallback the tokens have.

source: public/site/ — the page actually served at `/` in production — was in
title: Two glows on a page whose two governing stylesheets each independently forbid them, in the one syntax and directory src/app/glow-budget.test.ts cannot see
why: docs/DESIGN.md:399-400 states the No-Glow Rule: 'One glow on the page, and it belongs to the attention dot. A glow anywhere else -- on a status dot, a card edge, a button at rest -- is a defect.' DESIGN.md:699 lists it among the things the 2026-09-01 palette change explicitly did NOT touch. scrollcraft.css:70-72, the other stylesheet this page loads, reaches the same rule independently: 'Every shadow has an offset AND a soft blur... A zero-offset coloured halo is decoration, not depth, so there isn't one here.' The page then paints two. index.html:158 gives the booked Friday slot `box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #1b1b1b, 0 0 36px 4px rgba(138,180,248,0.45)` -- a 36px zero-offset blue halo, inside a Google Calendar mock, on an element whose whole job is fidelity to a product that does not glow. index.html:358 gives the provenance line a `.line__glow` stroke at width 14 and opacity 0.18 in var(--sc-accent). Both land on the page's two climax beats, and neither carries a comment claiming an exception, on a page that comments almost everything else. src/app/glow-budget.test.ts:56 tests for /shadow-\[0_0_[1-9]\d*px/ -- Tailwind arbitrary-value syntax -- over a tree rooted at src/ (line 26), so a raw-CSS halo in public/site is invisible to the guard that exists for exactly this defect.

source: gradients
title: Two hand-rolled drench gradients on the owner console, off-token and invisible to both drench guards
why: coach.css:84 states the rule in its own words: "The two drenches, and there are only two." console.css:83/605 and consumer.css:80 restate those same two gradients verbatim, and consumer.css:77 says the surface "spends one of the two allowed." Both shipped drenches are `158deg, oklch(0.28 0.08 262) -> oklch(0.17 0.04 265)` and `158deg, oklch(0.5 0.15 264) -> oklch(0.385 0.128 261)`, each with measured white-on-drench ratios in the comment beside it. owner-overview.tsx:533 and owner-money.tsx:263 then paint two MORE dark-navy panel gradients inline, at 160deg instead of 158deg, at flat hue 262 rather than the system's 262->265 / 264->261 walk, with stops (0.30/0.19 with a stray 70% position; 0.2905/0.2325) that appear nowhere in tokens.css. Around them sits a whole shadow palette of raw hue-262 oklch literals: 12 in owner-money.tsx, 8 in owner-overview.tsx, 8 in context-eye.tsx, including a hardcoded border `oklch(0.22 0.04 262)` and a hardcoded `0 18px 40px -22px rgba(28,42,82,0.6)` shadow. context-eye.tsx:268 reuses owner-money's off-token bottom stop `oklch(0.2325 0.023 262)` as a flat fill, which is how you can tell it is a second palette being copied around and not a decision. Neither panel carries `data-drench`, so drench-decision.test.ts's corpus (which scans `data-drench` subtrees) never sees them; and their literals are oklch rather than rgba, so palette-literals.test.ts's DARK_ERA regex never sees them either. Meanwhile palette-literals.test.ts's own OVER_DRENCH comment still describes coach-dashboard.tsx as carrying an inline `oklch(0.30 0.07 262) -> oklch(0.19 0.045 262)` gradient "the drench tokens carry" -- that file now uses `drench="live"` and has no gradient at all, and the drench tokens never carried those values. Three surfaces, three near-identical dark blues, none of them the token.
fix: Replace both inline gradients with the existing drench token plus a literal fallback, exactly as app-shell.tsx:373 already does for the portalled fleet card, and put `data-drench` on the two elements so drench-decision.test.ts starts scanning them. Re-solve the surrounding hue-262 oklch literals in owner-money.tsx, owner-overview.tsx and context-eye.tsx onto the `[data-shell-role="admin"] .coach-panel[data-drench]` role overrides that console.css:608-612 already declares (--ink/--body/--muted/--faint with measured ratios). Then delete the stale coach-dashboard.tsx row from palette-literals.test.ts's OVER_DRENCH set, which the file no longer needs.
note:
CORE IS REAL. owner-overview.tsx:533 and owner-money.tsx:263 do paint dark navy panel gradients inline at 160deg with stops that are not the drench tokens (158deg, 0.28/0.17 and 0.5/0.385). Neither carries data-drench. owner-money's NetMrrCard has no comment at all justifying it (verified 225-263). That is a genuine off-token second dark surface on the same admin console.

BUT THE SUPPORTING ARGUMENT IS SUBSTANTIALLY WRONG:
(1) 'stops that appear nowhere in tokens.css' is FALSE. oklch(0.2325 0.023 262) is EXACTLY --ink (tokens.css:104 and :799). 0.2905 is --body's lightness (tokens.css:105). So context-eye.tsx:268 is not 'reusing owner-money's off-token bottom stop' -- it is the --ink literal used as a popover ground (dark in both themes, which is why it is a literal and not var(--ink)). The 'second palette being copied around' provenance claim collapses.
(2) 'invisible to both guards' is only half true. palette-literals.test.ts's OVER_DRENCH set explicitly names workspace/rehaul/owner-overview.tsx with the note 'The `overview-pulse` section is the one drenched surface that screen is allowed' -- the repo documents this exact panel as a deliberate drench, and owner-overview.tsx:525 says the same in its own words. Deliberate is not slop.
(3) Literal counts are wrong: claimed 12 hue-262 oklch in owner-money, 8 in owner-overview, 8 in context-eye. True: 9, 9, 8 (14/9/9 oklch total).
(4) No product-wide rule exists. 'The two drenches, and there are only two' is a coach.css-local token-family comment (coach.css:84). docs/DESIGN.md contains the string 'drench' ZERO times; the playbook contains it zero times. The rule the auditor invokes is not the repo's stated authority.

VISUAL CONSEQUENCE: 158deg vs 160deg and 0.28 vs 0.30 is imperceptible. The one a designer would actually catch is owner-money's panel bottoming out at 0.2325 where the drench bottoms at 0.17 -- a visibly flatter, lighter dark panel on Billing than the one on Overview. One real cross-screen inconsistency, not three.

source: admin-console
title: Three horizontal gutters for one alignment contract, against the file's own written rule
why: console.css:569-573 states the rule in its own words: the queue row takes the same 18px gutter as the table `so a screen carrying a queue above a table does not read as two grids that failed to agree`. The rule is then applied to five shapes across eight declarations (:227, :267, :392, :528, :560, :565, :566, :576) and silently broken by two more: the KPI tile stays at 16px (:498) and the drenched panel takes 24px (:316, :321). Three gutters on one shell. The concrete pair: the Inbox screen renders MetricCard at src/components/workspace/live/admin-inbox.tsx:352, :366, :378 directly above QueueItem at :268, :419, :493 — tiles whose text column sits 2px inboard of the rows beneath them, which is precisely the failure the comment forbids. admin-overview.tsx pairs the same two slots. A rule stated in prose and violated twice in the same file, with no note at either violation, is the signature of text generated around a principle rather than applied to one.
fix: Move [data-slot="metric-card"] to the 18px gutter (or state in the comment at :490 why a KPI tile is the one shape allowed to break the console's column). Give the drenched panel the same 18px sides and keep only its vertical departure, which is the part the comment at :305-314 actually argues for.
note: Count is accurate (8 declarations at 18px: :227, :267, :392, :528, :560, :565, :566, :576; 2 at 24px; 1 at 16px = 11). The 18px side is not a deviation at all - it is documented twice as the owner console's table row padding: COACH-REDESIGN-PLAYBOOK.md:140 and REDESIGN-CANVAS.md:64 both carry the row 'table row padding | 19px 26px | 12px 18px'. So the question is only who fails to join it. The MetricCard half of the finding - the 'concrete pair' it leads with - does not hold: the rule at :569-573 is scoped to 'a queue above a table', two full-width list shapes; admin-inbox.tsx:351 puts the three MetricCards in 'grid-cols-1 ... @min-[620px]:grid-cols-3', so only the first tile even shares a left edge with the queue below, each tile carries its own visible border the eye anchors to, and the delta is 2px. That is grep-visible, not eye-visible. The drenched-panel half IS real and IS visible, and is the stronger case the finding buries: ConsoleStatDeck renders ONE drenched tile inside a strip of otherwise-plain tiles (shipped at admin-compliance.tsx:879, admin-money-affiliates.tsx:1197 and :1405, admin-money-corrections.tsx:458, admin-testing.tsx:365, admin-support-team.tsx:425), so in one row of identical tiles the drenched one's eyebrow sits 22px/24px inboard against its neighbours' 15px/18px - a 7px vertical and 6px horizontal offset, with no note, in a file whose own comment at :107-110 argues that a strip of four figures must not read as four unrelated boxes. The finding also missed the cleanest instance in its own subject: admin-inbox.tsx:439 draws LaneHeader at px-[14px] directly on top of QueueItems that console.css:576 moves to 18px, inside the same Surface panel - 4px, one container, header over its own rows.

title: One chat bubble, three paddings and three radii, all on the same route
why: /meet-agent renders one of two components depending on actor (src/app/meet-agent/page.tsx:70 vs :102). Both draw a chat bubble. globals.css:657-661 has the console base: padding 10px 13px, radius 13px 13px 13px 4px. meet-your-agent.css:232-233 overrides it for the coach density: padding 13px 17px, radius 14px 14px 14px 5px. rehaul/meet-agent.tsx:554-556 draws the third: px-[15px] py-[11px], rounded-[18px_18px_18px_6px]. The booking card compounds it: meet-your-agent.css:252 is 20px 20px 14px 14px while the same card on the consumer side takes var(--consumer-panel-radius) (24px 24px 17px 17px, consumer.css:70). consumer.css:88-90 declares a token for the bubble's measure specifically so 'the four places that need it cannot drift apart'; the radius, which drifted three ways, got no such token.

note: Every file:line resolves, but the load-bearing claim - three implementations on one URL - is false. meet-your-agent.tsx:583 renders CoachScale unconditionally as the component root ('Both mounts of this component are coach-facing... so there is no third reader'), which stamps data-shell-role=coach, so the globals.css:657-661 base radius/padding (13px 13px 13px 4px, 10px 13px) is ALWAYS overridden on this surface and never renders here. Two bubbles exist on the route, not three, and they are on mutually exclusive actor paths (page.tsx:70 platform vs :101 coach) under a ruling documented three times: page.tsx:54-63, REDESIGN-CANVAS.md:111-116, and the playbook's 'Shared components have three consumers... build the coach playback additively as a new component.' No one person sees both. The booking-card half is worse: .consumer-booking does not take --consumer-panel-radius, it takes --consumer-panel-radius-hero at consumer.css:681, and it is a hero deck panel on a phone screen while meet-your-agent.css:252's .booking-card is a card inside a chat stream - different objects. A coach really does see 14px/5px on Inbox and 18px/6px on /meet-agent. Different finding, same neighbourhood.

source: unlayered-cascade.test.ts attributes classes per-file, so a collision
title: globals.css names two callers whose hover border never drew, ships the fix, and applies it to one of them - and the fix cannot serve the other
why: globals.css:176-183 states the problem and the remedy in the sheet: '`.surface-card`'s own `border-color` beats any `hover:border-*` utility... Two callers wrote that utility with a `transition-[border-color]` beside it and neither has ever drawn an edge. Callers keep the transition and the `motion-reduce` opt-out; this owns only the colour', then defines `.surface-card.is-actionable:hover { border-color: var(--accent-edge) }`. `is-actionable` appears at exactly one call site in the whole repo, setting-row.tsx:229. The second caller the comment counts is src/app/page.tsx:177, which still carries `group-hover:border-[var(--accent-edge)] group-focus-visible:border-[var(--accent-edge)]` beside a live `transition-[border-color,transform]` and a live `group-hover:-translate-y-[2px]`, with no `is-actionable`. So the marketing entry cards lift 2px on hover and never change edge colour, while the comment at page.tsx:171-175 asserts 'The hover is the secondary button's hover, an --accent-edge border, which is the same signal every other ownable surface in the product gives.' Worse, `is-actionable` could not fix this one: page.tsx wraps the Surface in a `<Link className="group">` and needs the hover on the ancestor, which `.surface-card.is-actionable:hover` does not express, and nothing in the sheet covers `group-focus-visible` at all - so the keyboard affordance has no route to draw either.

source: kit-content
title: Row/card interior padding takes 6 distinct off-grid value-pairs; --d-card-p (16px) has 2 consumers repo-wide
why: tokens.css:286 declares `--d-card-p: 16px; /* card padding */`. Six card/row surfaces in atomics/ ignore it and each writes its own pair: SettingRow 17x14 (setting-row.tsx:68), SettingSection 18x15 (setting-row.tsx:311), QueueItem 14x12 (queue-item.tsx:47), NoteStrip 15x11 (queue-item.tsx:114), MetricCard 15x16 (metric-card.tsx:62), kanban column 14px (kanban-board.tsx:604). The killer is setting-row.tsx itself: two row recipes in ONE file, 243 lines apart, that differ by exactly 1px on BOTH axes (17x14 vs 18x15). An off-by-one in both dimensions is a copy-and-nudge, not a ruling — and this is a repo that writes a 12-line comment justifying why --d-row-quiet is 54px. Every one of these six pairs is uncommented. Only callout.tsx:48 and data-state.tsx:181 actually reference --d-card-p; every other card surface in scope re-rolls the number.
fix: Give the row family two named rungs and use them: keep --d-card-p:16px for card interiors and add --d-row-p (e.g. 12px 16px) for list rows. Replace the six literal pairs with p-[var(--d-card-p)] / px-[var(--d-row-p-x)] py-[var(--d-row-p-y)]. If a surface genuinely needs a different pair, it needs a comment saying which drawing sets it, the way button-class.ts:9-14 and logged-button.tsx:52-65 already do.
note: Every cited line is real and quoted correctly (17x14 at :68, 18x15 at :311, 14x12 at queue-item:47, 15x11 at queue-item:114, 15x16 at metric-card:62), and --d-card-p really does have exactly 2 consumers (data-state.tsx:181, callout.tsx:48). But the premise is wrong. The card-padding contract in this repo is NOT --d-card-p: it is `.surface-card { padding: 16px 17px }` at globals.css:149-155, which DESIGN.md's front-matter `components.card` specifies verbatim as `16px 17px` and which globals.css documents as unlayered and therefore winning over utilities. Five of the six flagged surfaces are not cards taking card padding at all -- they are a row inside a flush card, a section-header button, a queue row, a note strip, and a kanban column well -- and DESIGN.md:604 states the rule outright: 'Do give each card an interior shaped like its job. If two cards on a page look alike, one of them is wrong.' Two specific sub-claims are false: kanban-board.tsx:604 is NOT uncommented (lines 600-601 say '...and 14px of padding so the cards inside never touch its edge'), and metric-card.tsx:62's pair never renders at all (see pattern 2), so it cannot be one of six drawn recipes. What survives is one genuine defect, and it is the one the auditor called the killer: SettingSection's header button (px-18 py-15, :311) sits directly above SettingRow (px-17 py-14, :68) inside a single card -- verified at setting-row.tsx:346, where SettingRows is rendered as the button's sibling in the same `surface-card is-flush` div -- so the section title's left edge and the rows' left edges are 1px apart down one stack, with no reason given. That is one uncommented inconsistency in one file, not a six-surface systemic pattern.

source: kit-content
tell: 15 — inconsistent spacing (as a live rendering defect) / self-inconsistency
title: MetricCard's padding utility is dead: it collides with the unlayered .surface-card rule the repo already documented
why: metric-card.tsx:62 renders `<Surface className={cn("relative overflow-hidden p-[15px_16px]", className)}>`. Surface with the default variant="card" emits the `surface-card` class (surface.tsx:58). globals.css:149-155 sets `.surface-card { padding: 16px 17px; }` at brace depth 0 — outside every @layer, verified — so it beats the Tailwind utilities layer. globals.css:159-161 says this in the repo's own words: "`p-0` beside `surface-card` cannot say so: this sheet is unlayered, so it beats the utility layer and every one of those elements drew 16px 17px it was written not to have." So MetricCard renders at 16px 17px and the 15x16 an author drew never applies. The repo shipped utility-collision.test.ts specifically to catch this class of bug after it produced a 1:1-contrast button — but property() at utility-collision.test.ts:63-67 recognises only `color`, `background-color` and `font-size`. Padding is unguarded, and here is a live instance.
fix: Either drop `p-[15px_16px]` from metric-card.tsx:62 (accepting the card's 16x17) or add `is-flush` and own the padding, matching what setting-row.tsx:304 already does. Then extend utility-collision.test.ts's property() to map `p-[`/`px-[`/`py-[` to padding so the next one is caught, and consider a companion guard for a padding utility written on any element carrying `surface-card` without `is-flush`.
note: Verified end to end. metric-card.tsx:62 renders `p-[15px_16px]`; surface.tsx:58 emits `surface-card` for the default variant='card'; globals.css:149-155 sets `.surface-card { padding: 16px 17px }` at brace depth 0 -- I confirmed the `@layer base` block closes at line 139, so the rule is genuinely unlayered and beats Tailwind's utilities layer -- and globals.css:157-162 states the consequence in the repo's own words. MetricCard is shipped, not demo-only (admin-overview.tsx:616 and :1481, admin-inbox.tsx:352/366/378). Count of 1 is exact: it is the only Surface callsite inside kit that adds a padding utility. Two corrections. First, the utility-collision.test.ts framing is wrong: that suite (per its own header comment, lines 8-43) guards two arbitrary Tailwind utilities for one property inside ONE class list, a different mechanism entirely from a utility losing to an unlayered stylesheet; property() at :63-67 not covering padding is therefore irrelevant, and no guard was ever meant to catch this. Second, severity: the rendered delta is 1px on each axis, so no designer would see it in the shipped UI. It is real dead code that lies about what it draws -- worth fixing by adding `is-flush` or deleting the utility -- but not high.

source: Focus indicators were not in any of the 20 scopes, and there are at le
title: .share-field draws focus as a 3px box-shadow at 22% — 1.24:1, the exact figure the playbook names as unacceptable
why: globals.css:1358 puts `outline: 0` on the resting `.share-field > input`, then :1367-1369 replaces the product's indicator with `border-color: var(--agent-focus-ring)` plus `box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in srgb, var(--agent-focus-ring) 22%, transparent)`. --agent-focus-ring aliases --focus-ring at globals.css:258, so the 22% multiplies the token's own 0.65/0.6 down to 0.143/0.132. Composited: 1.24:1 on --canvas and 1.24:1 on --card in light, 1.24:1 and 1.29:1 in dark. COACH-REDESIGN-PLAYBOOK.md:101-104 is a section titled "Move the accessibility, never delete it" whose whole argument is that the FieldShell tint "measures about 1.2 to 1 against the card, far under the 3 to 1 a focus indicator needs" — I measure that tint at 1.18/1.15 with the same method, confirming the arithmetic. So this field ships, as its focus indicator, the same 1.2:1 wash the playbook uses as its worked example of what must never be the only cue. It survives in practice only because `outline: 0` at :1358 is unlayered and sits in the same sheet, and the unlayered tokens.css:976 rule is imported first (layout.tsx:4 before :5) at equal (0,1,0) specificity — so a later-source rule at :1358 has already stripped the resting outline while :1367 never restores one. The 22% is a number with no relative in tokens.css; every alpha in that file carries a measured comment.
fix: Delete globals.css:1358's `outline: 0` and the box-shadow at :1369, and let the global outline paint. If the border-colour change is wanted as an additional cue, keep :1368 and drop only the shadow.
note: The substance holds and the finding actually understates its own authority. globals.css:1358 sets `outline: 0` on `.share-field > input` — unlayered, specificity (0,1,1), which beats the unlayered `:focus-visible` at (0,1,0), so the global 2px outline is genuinely killed here, the only outline-killer in any of the six unlayered sheets outside the shell-scoped one at tokens.css:987. What is left on focus (globals.css:1367-1369) is a border-colour change to --agent-focus-ring plus `0 0 0 3px color-mix(in srgb, var(--agent-focus-ring) 22%, transparent)`, and since --agent-focus-ring aliases --focus-ring (globals.css:258, already 0.65 alpha) the shadow composites to roughly 0.14 alpha. The finding missed the citation that settles it: DESIGN.md:466 says focus is the global outline "— never a border-colour change alone." This ships: src/app/meet-agent/page.tsx renders MeetYourAgent, whose share field is at meet-your-agent.tsx:1085. Corrected severity to medium: it is one control on one route, not a systemic failure. The playbook citation is misused — its 1.2:1 is the FieldShell tint measured against the card, not this shadow, and the "1.24:1" figure is not derivable from it.

source: Orphaned dead CSS — named in the audit brief as a tell-adjacent axis,
title: --t-hero and .t-hero: a token pinned by the test suite and documented for a named page, rendered by nothing, while the real hero figure is a hardcoded 34px literal

source: Date, time and number formatting has no audit scope and is systematica
title: Ambient-zone reads reach first paint in client components — the exact React 19 #418 shape datetime.ts:4-8 describes, in one case 20 lines below a comment refusing it
why: impersonation-banner.tsx is the clearest case: at lines 109-114 it carries a six-line comment explaining that the elapsed clock is deferred to after mount because "would differ between the server pass and the first client pass, which is a hydration mismatch on a banner whose whole job is to be trusted", and it correctly gates that value at line 218 with `now === null ? "counting"`. Twenty lines above, `expiryLabel` (line 95) calls `expires.toLocaleTimeString("en-US", { hour, minute })` with no timeZone, and line 242 renders it unconditionally in the first paint. The file argues the rule and breaks it in the same render. onboarding-calendar.tsx:48 and calendar-step.tsx:81 are the same defect by a different route: `const EMPTY: Form = { ... timezone: Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone || "UTC" ... }` is evaluated at module scope in a "use client" file, seeded into `useState<Form>(EMPTY)` (onboarding-calendar.tsx:93, calendar-step.tsx:145) and painted as `value={form.timezone}` (onboarding-calendar.tsx:411, calendar-step.tsx:500) — SSR emits "UTC", the browser emits the visitor's zone, on the very first render. This is not the exempted shape: consumer-experience.tsx:216-228 confines its resolvedOptions read to an event handler and says so in twelve lines of comment, and signup-form.tsx:293-297 wraps it in a function called from a handler; these two put it in module-scope initial state. agent-simulator.ts:129-141 compounds it, using ambient `getDay()`/`setDate()` plus a timeZone-less formatter and then hardcoding ", 2:30 PM", reached from src/components/agent-flow.tsx and src/components/meet-your-agent.tsx, both "use client".
fix: impersonation-banner.tsx:95 → `workspaceTimestampFormat` or a pinned time formatter from src/lib/format/datetime. onboarding-calendar.tsx:48 and calendar-step.tsx:81 → seed `timezone: ""` in EMPTY and fill the visitor's zone in a `useEffect` after mount, the pattern the same repo already uses for the impersonation clock. agent-simulator.ts:134 → pass `timeZone: WORKSPACE_DISPLAY_TIMEZONE` and derive the day with a zoned key rather than `getDay()`. connect-channel-flow.ts:131 → as in pattern 1.
note: One citation is excellent and four do not survive. CONFIRMED: impersonation-banner.tsx:95. `expiryLabel` uses toLocaleTimeString with no timeZone, and it is called UNGATED at line 242, while the sibling `elapsedLabel` at line 217 is gated behind `now === null` under a comment at 109-114 that names hydration mismatch explicitly. Same component, same concern, one half handled and one half missed — the strongest item in the whole set. REFUTED, documented-deliberate: onboarding-calendar.tsx:48 and calendar-step.tsx:81 use `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`, and datetime.test.ts:67-68 explicitly sanctions that shape in prose — "deliberately reads the visitor's own zone to prefill the field, which is resolvedOptions() rather than formatting, so it is exempt by shape not by name." Deliberate is not slop. REFUTED, does not reach first paint: agent-simulator.ts:134 runs only inside the `qualification?.outcome === "BOOK"` branch at :301, i.e. after a user types into the demo, and connect-channel-flow.ts:131 is reached via connect-channel-sheet.tsx:603 only on the post-202 "connected" step. Neither is in the initial SSR pass, so neither can produce #418. connect-channel-flow.ts:131 is real evidence, but it belongs to finding 1 (red guard test), not to a first-paint claim.

why: The repo treats the canvas as pixel authority and cites it 317 times across src/ and docs/, usually with a line number, as the reason a value is what it is. 143 of those (45%, spanning 33 distinct filenames) name a file that is not in design/coach/. Some are renames whose line numbers no longer resolve: CoachError (20 citations) is now ErrorState.dc.html, CoachHomeMobile (15) is HomeMobile.dc.html, CoachTips (9) is Tips.dc.html, CoachAccountMenu (6) is AccountMenu.dc.html, CoachSupportBubble (5) is SupportBubble.dc.html, CoachSetup (5) is Setup.dc.html. A citation nobody can open is indistinguishable from one that was never true, which is exactly how the COACH_SURFACE_TITLE_CLASS argument above survived being read.
fix: Sweep the 33 names: rewrite the eight renamed ones to current filenames with re-resolved line numbers, and for the ~20 with no in-repo counterpart either export those artboards into design/ or replace the citation with a plain statement of the rule so it stops claiming evidence it cannot produce. Then add a cheap test that extracts every `*.dc.html` reference from src/ and docs/ and asserts the file exists in design/coach/.
note: The count is essentially right: my own walk of src/ and docs/ finds 320 named .dc.html citations (plus 3 glob patterns), of which 146 across exactly 33 distinct filenames name a file absent from design/coach/ — 45.6%, versus the claimed 143 of 317 across 33. The per-name figures also match (CoachError 20, MeetYourAgent 17, CoachHomeMobile 15, CoachTips 9, AdminClients 8, CoachAccountMenu 6, CoachSupportBubble 5, CoachSetup 5, AdminOverview 5, ConsumerBooked 5). Downgraded because the framing "unverifiable / indistinguishable from never true" is undercut by the repo's own documentation: REDESIGN-CANVAS.md:1-13 records the 2026-09-01 canvas as a live published Artifact with its URL, states "Treat the published artifact as current and this document as an index," and its Coverage section lists exactly the Admin/Consumer/Affiliate/Landing boards those citations name. Those names come from a documented authority that was deliberately never checked in, not from thin air — the defect is the missing name-mapping and the unresolvable line numbers, not fabrication. source: canvas
title: The canvas imports the color half of tokens.css verbatim and re-types every spacing value as a literal: 2,385 px literals, 0 var(--s-*)/var(--d-*)
why: VOCABULARY.md:11-14 says the :root block is "src/app/tokens.css bare :root (the light palette), lifted verbatim" -- and it is: 50+ color tokens copied exactly into all 22 helmets. But --s-1..--s-12 and --d-stack-gap/--d-head-gap/--d-section-gap/--d-card-p were not lifted at all. Measured across design/coach/*.dc.html: 1,979 padding/margin/gap declarations containing 2,385 px values, and exactly 0 occurrences of var(--s-N) or var(--d-*). Those 2,385 values resolve to 26 distinct numbers where tokens.css names 9 and VOCABULARY.md:69 names 8 ("Spacing steps: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40"). 1,016 of them (43%) are off the 4px grid; 1,080 (45%) are off the declared scale. tokens.css:291 states the rhythm "cannot drift off the 4px grid" -- in the canvas it drifts in 43% of cases. Someone made a deliberate decision about color and then typed spacing from memory. The 18 undocumented values are 1px, 2px, 3px, 5px, 6px, 10px, 11px, 14px, 18px, 19px, 22px, 26px, 28px, 36px, 72px, 80px, 96px, 340px.
fix: Add the --s-* and --d-* declarations to the shared helmet block (they are already the second half of the tokens.css :root the canvas claims to lift verbatim), then rewrite the eight sanctioned values as var(--s-N). Add a line to VOCABULARY.md's Tokens section naming the exceptions the drawing genuinely needs (19px band, 26px cell, 96px bubble inset) so the next artboard inherits the exception list instead of re-inventing it.
note: The arithmetic is exact — I reproduce 2,385 px values in padding/margin/gap across design/coach/*.dc.html, 26 distinct positive values, 1,016 (42.6%) off the 4px grid, 0 var(--s-*) and 0 var(--d-*). But the framing collapses under three checks. (1) The premise is impossible by construction: the canvas helmet defines no --s-*/--d-* names at all (Main.dc.html:12-78 lifts only the colour palette, exactly as VOCABULARY.md:10-11 states — 'the bare :root ... plus four canvas-only names'). var(--s-4) in a .dc.html would resolve to nothing. Nobody 'declined' to use the tokens; they were never in the file. (2) The '18 undocumented values' claim is mostly false. 11 of the 18 are documented in VOCABULARY.md itself: 19px and 20px as band padding (:70), 26px as table cells (:71) and nav-pill padding (:78), 36px and 96px as page padding (:69), 18px as segmented-control padding (:85) and thread-row padding (:94), 22px as secondary-button padding (:80) and panel-body top inset (:133), and 5px / 10px / 11px / 14px / 2px inside the canonical chrome and button snippets (:107, :108, :109, :115, :148, :149, :92). Genuinely undocumented values total 108 of 2,385 = 4.5%, not 45%: 6px x69, 28px x18, 3px x14, 1px x4, plus 72/80/340 one-offs. (3) tokens.css:291's 'cannot drift off the 4px grid' is a sentence about the --d-* aliases aliasing --s-* rungs inside tokens.css. Those --d-* tokens sit under the heading 'Density, pass-2 admin scale' (tokens.css:267-268) — owner-console tokens — and COACH-REDESIGN-PLAYBOOK.md:129-131 states that coach and the owner console are two densities on purpose and that mixing them 'is a regression rather than consistency'. Real residue: ~108 values on no scale and in no doc, mostly 6px and 3px optical nudges. Invisible without a ruler.

source: tokens+globals
title: @theme inline maps every design axis except the one with 1,382 arbitrary values
why: The @theme inline block at globals.css:7-86 carries 75 entries: 32 --color-*, 35 --text-*, 5 --radius-* (globals.css:39-43 wire --r-card/--r-control/--r-input/--r-panel straight into Tailwind), 3 --font-*. It carries zero --spacing-* entries, even though tokens.css declares 9 spacing rungs, 3 named rhythm steps and 8 layout metrics 150 lines away. This is the mechanical root cause of the 1,382 arbitrary-px spacing classes measured repo-wide: because no token reached Tailwind's spacing namespace, there is no `p-card` or `gap-stack` to write, so authors either fall back to the stock numeric scale or bracket a raw pixel - which is exactly why px-[16px] (x46) and px-4 (x16) coexist as two spellings of one value. Every other axis got wired; the axis that got skipped is the axis that drifted. That asymmetry is the tell: whoever built the theme block worked down a checklist of colour, radius, font and type and never asked what spacing needed.
fix: Add the spacing axis to @theme inline: `--spacing-1: var(--s-1)` through `--spacing-12: var(--s-12)`, plus named semantic rungs `--spacing-stack: var(--d-stack-gap)`, `--spacing-head: var(--d-head-gap)`, `--spacing-section: var(--d-section-gap)`, `--spacing-card: var(--d-card-p)`. Then `p-card` and `gap-section` become writable and a lint rule against bracketed px spacing becomes enforceable.
note: The measurements are exact -- I reproduced all of them. The @theme inline block (globals.css:7-86) has 75 entries: 32 --color-*, 35 --text-*, 5 --radius-*, 3 --font-*, 0 --spacing-*. Repo-wide raw-px spacing utilities: 1,382 exactly. px-[16px] appears 46 times and px-4 16 times. All four citations point at real shipped code. What fails is the causal claim, and it fails on Tailwind mechanics. Tailwind v4's default --spacing base is 0.25rem = 4px, so the stock numeric scale ALREADY is this repo's 4px grid: p-1/2/3/4/5/6/8/10/12 map exactly onto --s-1..--s-12. There was no gap to wire. Colour, radius and type had no stock equivalents, which is why those three axes needed a bridge and spacing did not -- that asymmetry is mechanical, not a checklist. The repo also has a third sanctioned spelling used 1,207 times, p-[var(--s-4)], guarded by token-references.test.ts. And most of the 1,382 raw values are off-grid on purpose because the design artifact is off-grid: px-[26px] (x26) is DESIGN.md:436's `0 26px 22px` page padding, py-[19px] is the deck panel band. What remains is a genuine but cosmetic inconsistency: three spellings for one value coexisting with no lint rule choosing between them. Invisible in the rendered UI.

source: workspace
title: The same spacing value is spelled up to three ways: 71 utility+value pairs collide, 30 of them across all three vocabularies, covering 1,565 class instances
why: The tree carries 2,001 spacing declarations in three parallel vocabularies with no rule separating them: 951 literal `-[Npx]` (47.5%), 602 `-[var(--s-N)]` (30.1%), 448 numeric Tailwind (22.4%). 71 utility+value pairs are spelled at least two ways and 30 all three. Worst offenders: gap=8px is written gap-[8px] x49 / gap-2 x37 / gap-[var(--s-2)] x105 (191 instances of one value, three spellings); gap=12px is 52/41/89; gap=16px is 29/23/50; px=20px is 28/24/5; mt=4px is 10/5/31. This is not a cross-file drift - owner-brain.tsx does it to itself: line 634 `flex min-w-0 flex-col gap-[16px]` and line 868 `relative flex min-w-0 flex-col gap-[var(--s-4)]` are the same column stack 234 lines apart; line 1366 `flex flex-wrap items-end gap-[12px]` and line 885 `flex flex-wrap items-end gap-[var(--s-3)]` are byte-identical except the gap spelling. Four sibling owner page roots spell the same 16px three ways: owner-overview.tsx:479 gap-[var(--s-4)], owner-inbox.tsx:180 gap-[16px], owner-money.tsx:913 gap-4, owner-system.tsx:767 gap-4. Nine files mix two spellings of gap-8px internally (owner-brain, owner-compliance, owner-overview, owner-money, affiliate-home, coach-settings-notifications, escalation-panel, coach-tips, coach-support). Heights repeat the pattern: h-[48px] x39 vs h-12 x9, h-[44px] x12 vs h-11 x3, h-[32px] x4 vs h-8 x9, h-[40px] x1 vs h-10 x2. Radius too: --r-card is 14px (tokens.css:245) yet rounded-[14px] appears 25 times against rounded-[var(--r-card)] 10 times. No design authority explains spelling one value three ways; a person picks a house spelling and holds it.
fix: Pick one spelling per value class and enforce it with an ESLint no-restricted-syntax rule on className: `-[var(--s-N)]` for every value the scale carries, bare `-[Npx]` only for values it does not. Ban the numeric Tailwind scale in this tree outright (448 instances, zero of them load-bearing) since it silently aliases the same rungs. Highest-yield first pass: gap 8/12/16px, which is 475 of the 1,565 instances.
note: The counting is honest and I reproduce it almost exactly: 951 literal -[Npx] (exact match), 600 -[var(--s-N)] (claimed 602), 352 numeric Tailwind excluding -0 (claimed 448), 72 utility+value pairs spelled two or more ways (claimed 71), 30 spelled all three (exact match), 1,574 instances covered (claimed 1,565). The internal-contradiction citations are exact: owner-brain.tsx:634 gap-[16px] vs :868 gap-[var(--s-4)], and :1366 'flex flex-wrap items-end gap-[12px]' vs :885 'flex flex-wrap items-end gap-[var(--s-3)]' are byte-identical but for the gap spelling. Height and radius counts check out (h-[48px] 39 / h-12 8; h-[44px] 12 / h-11 3; rounded-[14px] 24 / rounded-[var(--r-card)] 10). What kills it as a design finding is criterion (d): there is no --spacing override in the @theme block of globals.css, so gap-2, gap-[8px] and gap-[var(--s-2)] compile to the identical 8px. Not one pixel of the shipped UI differs. No authority is violated either: token-references.test.ts only asserts that a referenced --s-N exists, and no doc or test names a house spelling. This is a maintainability tell visible only by grepping, not a deviation a designer could see.

source: crossvector
tell: magic numbers against an unused token scale
title: The five-rung z-index scale is reached 13 times; 54 other sites use magic numbers, flattening drawer, popover, dialog and toast onto one layer
why: tokens.css:251 declares an ordered layering scale — --z-sticky:10, --z-rail:20, --z-drawer:30, --z-popover:40, --z-toast:50 — and DESIGN.md never mentions it, so the one scale that would make overlay order legible is documented nowhere. It is reached by 13 utilities, all inside src/components/kit/. Everything else is a magic number: 48 bare `z-N` utilities plus 6 raw `z-index:` declarations in CSS. The ordering the scale encodes is then lost: ui/sheet.tsx:66 (the drawer, rung 30), ui/popover.tsx:40, ui/dropdown-menu.tsx:64, ui/select.tsx:401, ui/tooltip.tsx:53 (rung 40), ui/dialog.tsx:57, ui/alert-dialog.tsx:55 and coach-support-bubble.tsx:297 all sit at a flat z-50, so a drawer, a popover, a dialog and the support bubble stack by DOM order rather than by role — while toast-preset.ts:24, the thing meant to sit on top, is at the same 50. coach.css:1460 puts the kanban drag preview at z-index: 100, above the entire scale. The two tooltips disagree with each other: kit/tooltip.tsx:41 takes var(--z-popover) (40) and ui/tooltip.tsx:53 takes 50. 38 files import the ui/ overlay primitives, so this is the shipped layering, not a corner case.
fix: Point the eight ui/ overlay primitives at the rungs they belong to (sheet -> --z-drawer, popover/dropdown/select/tooltip -> --z-popover, dialog/alert-dialog -> --z-drawer or a new --z-modal), give the kanban drag preview a rung instead of 100, and collapse the two tooltips onto one value. Document the five rungs in DESIGN.md §4 beside the shadow vocabulary, since the two encode the same layering story.
note: The counts are accurate and every file:line resolves. 48 bare `z-N` utilities (z-0 x1, z-10 x20, z-20 x4, z-30 x2, z-40 x2, z-50 x19) plus 6 raw `z-index:` declarations in CSS = 54 exactly as claimed. tokens.css:251 declares the scale on one line with no commentary; DESIGN.md mentions z-index and --z-* zero times. source: gradients
title: The card face is the only gradient in the system with no token, and it is retyped 27 times
why: tokens.css gives a named token to every gradient that appears once or twice -- `--rail` (one consumer, app-shell.tsx:162), `--pane-bloom` (nine consumers), `--accent-fill` (nineteen) -- each declared in all four theme blocks. The single most-repeated gradient in the product gets none. `linear-gradient(180deg, var(--card-top), var(--card))` is the canvas's card-face lift, named `.surface-card` in DESIGN.md:421 and drawn 80 times across the 22 artboards, and in the code it is hand-copied 27 times: 9 CSS declarations across globals.css, coach.css (x3), console.css and consumer.css (x4), plus 18 Tailwind arbitrary values across 16 component files. It is spelled three different ways -- `bg-[linear-gradient(...)]`, `[background:linear-gradient(...)]` (account-security-settings.tsx:128, setting-row.tsx:163) and a `background:` shorthand with `!important` (coach.css:1465) -- which is what a copied string looks like versus a referenced one. surface.tsx:32 exists specifically to prevent this and says so in its docstring ("The surface ladder, as one component rather than four inline gradient strings"), and 16 files route around it. The drift is already visible: _primitives.tsx:307 copies the face but substitutes a hand-written three-part shadow for `var(--shadow-card)`, so its cards sit at a different elevation than every other card carrying the same face. This is also the exact failure mode accent-fill-spelling.test.ts was written for -- a gradient with no single spelling -- one token short of being fixable by the same mechanism.
fix: Add `--card-face: linear-gradient(180deg, var(--card-top), var(--card))` to all four theme blocks in tokens.css beside `--rail` and `--pane-bloom`, and rewrite the 27 sites as `[background:var(--card-face)]` / `background: var(--card-face)` -- the spelling accent-fill-spelling.test.ts already blesses for a gradient token. Restore `var(--shadow-card)` in _primitives.tsx:307 in the same pass, then extend that test's regex to forbid `bg-[var(--card-face)]` too.
note:
COUNT VERIFIED EXACTLY, AND THE RULE IS REAL. 9 CSS declarations + 18 Tailwind arbitrary values = 27. The canvas claim also checks out: `grep -oh` across design/coach/*.dc.html returns exactly four distinct gradient strings, the card face appearing 80 times. And DESIGN.md:600-601 states the rule in the strongest possible terms: 'Do build every card from `.surface-card`... Add layout classes on top; never restate the face inline.' So this is a genuine violation of an explicitly documented rule.

BUT IT IS NOT SLOP, AND IT HAS NO VISUAL CONSEQUENCE:
(1) All 27 spellings resolve to var(--card-top) and var(--card). A token move reaches every one of them. There is ZERO drift in the face itself -- a designer looking at shipped UI sees identical card faces everywhere. This is grep-visible only.
(2) globals.css:150 is a BAD CITATION: it is the `.surface-card` recipe itself, the authority the rule points at, not one of the hand-copies. True duplicate count is 26, not 27.
(3) 'surface.tsx exists to prevent this and 16 files route around it' misreads the mechanism twice. Surface (src/components/kit/atomics/surface.tsx, not kit/surface.tsx) applies the `.surface-card` CLASS, not an inline gradient. And unlayered-cascade.test.ts documents at length that globals.css is unlayered, so a Tailwind utility CANNOT override `.surface-card`'s `border-radius` or `padding` -- 'class="surface-card p-0" renders the card's padding: 16px 17px and the p-0 is simply not there.' Nearly every inline restatement uses a non-default radius (15px on kanban-card, 13px on setting-row, 16px_16px_13px_13px and 24px_24px_17px_17px on coach-leads, var(--coach-panel-radius) on landing-page/account-security-settings). Those callers are structurally forced to restate the face; that is the cascade, not a copy-paste habit. File count is 14, not 16.
(4) The one real drift is described backwards. _primitives.tsx:307's hand-written shadow is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the light --shadow-card (tokens.css:231), so it does NOT 'sit at a different elevation than every other card' in light. The actual defect is worse and different: it is a light-theme literal, so on the dark palette (tokens.css:553/:707) the admin brain page's CARD_TABLE cards lose their elevation. One instance, not a pattern.

title: 19 hand-rolled focus utilities are inert against the unlayered global, and two of them silently render a different offset than written
why: Every `focus-visible:outline-*` utility outside ui/ is a Tailwind utility in `@layer utilities` naming a longhand of the `outline` shorthand that tokens.css:976 already declares unlayered. Most are harmless because they happen to restate the right numbers, but two are not: kanban-card.tsx:148 and kanban-board.tsx:577 both write `focus-visible:outline-offset-1`, and both render at the global's 2px. A card whose author deliberately tightened its ring by a pixel has been drawing the untightened ring since the line was written. This is precisely the trap unlayered-cascade.test.ts:4-13 exists to catch, and it cannot see any of it: its `keyClasses()` at :110-118 attributes unlayered declarations only to *classes* in a rule's rightmost compound, and the global's selector is the bare pseudo-class `:focus-visible`, which yields an empty class list. Every focus utility in the repo therefore falls outside the guard's model — a structural blind spot, not an oversight of coverage.

For the two kanban sites, decide whether the 1px offset was actually wanted and, if so, express it in tokens.css beside the global rule (unlayered) the way the FieldShell exception is expressed at :983-987. Separately, teach unlayered-cascade.test.ts about non-class unlayered selectors, or add a narrower guard in focus-ring.test.ts that scans src/**/*.tsx for `focus-visible:(outline|ring|border)-` and fails on anything outside a named allowlist.

All 14 are dead: the unlayered `outline` shorthand at tokens.css:976 beats every layered longhand regardless of specificity. And four, not two, render something other than what is written — `focus-visible:outline-offset-1` at kanban-card.tsx:148 and kanban-board.tsx:577 renders at 2px, and `focus-visible:outline-1` at scroll-area.tsx:21 and tabs.tsx:102 renders at 2px width. This is a real self-inconsistency because the repo built a guard for precisely this trap: unlayered-cascade.test.ts's docstring says the dead declaration "reads exactly like a live one" and cost a whole audit round, but its keyClasses() at line 110 only keys rules by class name, so a pseudo-class-keyed rule like `:focus-visible` is invisible to it.
