title: Two opposite authoring dialects split sibling files inside src/components/onboarding/ with zero overlap
why: The directory splits cleanly in two and the split is total, not gradual. Token-first files: get-started-checklist.tsx (56 var(--s-N) usages, 3 px literals), optin-artifact.tsx (26/2), messaging-install-panel.tsx (24/0), coach-onboarding.tsx (20/2), install-attempts.tsx (13/0), admin-provisioning.tsx (8/0). Literal-only files: calendar-step.tsx (0 tokens, 44 literals), sms-step.tsx (0/30), go-live-step.tsx (0/29), connect-step.tsx (0/13), offer-step.tsx (0/13), profile-step.tsx (0/5). Six files use the token scale exclusively and six use px literals exclusively, in one directory, on one surface, with not a single file mixing at a ratio in between. That is not a system evolving — it is two passes that never met, and it is why the same 16px gap is `gap-[var(--s-4)]` on the checklist and `gap-[16px]` two files over. step-shell.tsx (4 tokens / 33 literals) sits on the seam and is the only file that genuinely mixes.
fix: Convert the six literal-only step files to the token spelling for every value that lands on an --s-* rung — mechanical, roughly 90 substitutions, and it makes the two halves of the directory greppable as one system. Values the artboards pin off-rung (19, 22, 78) stay literal and get the artboard citation comment.
note: The bimodal split is real and the per-file numbers are close to right (my rg: get-started-checklist 53 token/3 literal not 56/3; optin-artifact 26/2; messaging-install-panel 24/0; coach-onboarding 20/2; install-attempts 12/0; admin-provisioning 8/0; calendar-step 0/44; sms-step 0/30; go-live-step 0/29; connect-step 0/13; offer-step 0/13; profile-step 0/5; step-shell 4/33). But 'two passes that never met' is not supported. The split tracks a real property of the surfaces: the six literal-only files are exactly the six artboard-traced step components, and their literals are dominated by values with no --s-* token at all — calendar carries 6px, 10px, 14px, 19px; sms carries 10px×6, 14px, 19px; connect carries 14px, 18px, 19px, 22px — the artboards' own band and row paddings. The six token-first files contain almost no off-scale values across all six combined (3px, 6px, 7px, 2px, 28px). Once a class string is carrying `py-[19px]`, writing every neighbour in px is the consistent choice, not the careless one. And the harm is nil: `gap-[16px]` and `gap-[var(--s-4)]` emit the same declaration. One citation is not evidence of anything.

source: kit-shell
title: 16 of 24 literal spacing values are off the 4px grid, 11 of them in the two files whose only cited authority is fabricated
why: tokens.css:291 states the rhythm 'cannot drift off the 4px grid'. Full histogram of literal-px spacing in this scope: 4px x4, 2px x3, 6px x3, 12px x2, 7px x2, 3px, 5px, 8px, 10px, 11px, 14px, 18px, 32px = 24 total, of which 16 are not multiples of 4. Two of the 16 are legitimate: app-topbar.tsx:386's `gap-[11px] pr-[14px]` is byte-exact against AccountMenu.dc.html:96, so it is decided. The remaining 14 have no verifiable basis, and 11 sit in coach-pillbar.tsx (px-[6px]:88, pt-[6px]:88, gap-[2px]:92, gap-[3px]:109, px-[6px]:203) and impersonation-banner.tsx (py-[18px]:172, mt-[5px]:206, gap-[7px]:209, gap-[7px]:222, mt-[6px]:239, mt-[6px]:247) — the two files whose only cited canvases (CoachHomeMobile, AdminImpersonation) do not exist. impersonation-banner.tsx:172 is the clearest instance: `gap-[var(--s-6)] ... px-[var(--s-10)] py-[18px]` puts tokens and a raw off-grid literal in one class string, and 18px sits between --s-4 (16) and --s-5 (20) for no stated reason. The 7px icon-to-label gaps at :209 and :222 are the same visual relationship that gap-[var(--s-2)] (8px) expresses at 15 other sites across 6 files in this scope.
fix: Snap the 14 unbacked values to the nearest --s-* rung (18->--s-5, 7->--s-2, 5/6->--s-1 or --s-2, 3/2->--s-1) and re-measure. Where a value genuinely must be off-grid, state the measurement in a comment the way app-topbar.tsx:386's canvas-exact set effectively is. The 15-vs-2 split on the icon-gap alone makes the 7px indefensible.
note: My independent scan of the ten shell files reproduces the totals exactly — 24 literal-px spacing utilities, 16 off the 4px grid — though the auditor's histogram is off (6px appears 5 times, not 3). What fails is the 'no verifiable basis' half. HomeMobile.dc.html:242 draws the phone tab bar `padding: 6px 8px 10px`, which is the source of coach-pillbar.tsx:88's px-[6px] pt-[6px] and the 10px inside its pb-calc; HomeMobile.dc.html:244 draws the tab count `padding: 0 6px`, which is coach-pillbar.tsx:203's px-[6px]. So three of the eleven the auditor calls baseless are canvas-exact, in the very file it says has no real canvas — plus the two it already conceded (11px, 14px at app-topbar.tsx:386). That leaves 11 off-grid literals without a local referent, six of them in impersonation-banner.tsx, whose artboard is on the published canvas rather than in design/coach/ and so is neither verifiable nor disprovable. The grid rule is also misapplied: tokens.css:288-291 constrains the three --d-* rhythm STEPS ('Each step aliases a --s-* rung'), and neither DESIGN.md nor the playbook states any repo-wide 4px spacing rule — DESIGN.md:646's literal prohibition is explicitly about hex/token colour values, and palette-literals.test.ts:19-31 confines its doctrine to colour. What genuinely survives is impersonation-banner.tsx:172 and :206 mixing tokens and off-grid literals in one class string (py-[18px], mt-[5px], gap-[7px] x2, mt-[6px] x2). Real, but 1-3px deltas on a banner: grep-visible, not eye-visible.

source: shadcn
title: 2,261 lines of never-imported shadcn primitives, over half in one file
why: Nine primitives have zero references anywhere in src/ outside components/ui/ itself, verified by grepping both the @/components/ui/<name> path and the barrel (which is never imported at all): file-upload.tsx (1407 lines), field.tsx (238), form.tsx (164), table.tsx (116), card.tsx (103), progress.tsx (83), accordion.tsx (73), scroll-area.tsx (55), aspect-ratio.tsx (22) — 2,261 lines total, 62% of it file-upload.tsx. Each duplicates a role the shipped kit already owns: kit/atomics has field.tsx, progress.tsx, grid-table.tsx, metric-card.tsx and surface.tsx, and kit/ has data-table.tsx with its own toolbar/pagination/column-header/row-actions. A registry install that pulled the catalog rather than the components the product needs is the classic generated-not-decided signature, and it costs real surface area: these files are the largest single source of stock shadcn class strings a future contributor will copy from.
fix: Delete the nine unreferenced files and their entries in src/components/ui/index.ts. If any is a planned dependency, note which surface will use it; otherwise re-add via shadcn add at the moment of need, so the port cost is paid once for components that actually ship.
note: The most accurate pattern in the set; if anything it undercounts. I verified every file has zero references anywhere in src/, e2e/, evals/ or scripts/ outside components/ui/ itself, and confirmed the barrel src/components/ui/index.ts is imported zero times. Line counts are exact: file-upload 1407, field 238, form 164, table 116, card 103, progress 83, accordion 73, scroll-area 55, aspect-ratio 22 = 2,261, and 1407/2261 = 62.2%. UNDERCOUNT: badge.tsx (52) and switch.tsx (32) are also dead -- their only importer anywhere is src/components/ui/kit.test.tsx, which is itself inside components/ui/, so by the finding's own stated criterion the true count is 11 files / 2,345 lines. (separator.tsx and toggle.tsx are genuinely live, reached through sidebar/field and toggle-group.) The duplication claim holds: kit/atomics ships field.tsx, progress.tsx, grid-table.tsx, metric-card.tsx and surface.tsx, and kit/ ships data-table.tsx plus data-table-toolbar/-pagination/-column-header/-row-actions/-faceted-filter. MINOR OVERREACH: 'the largest single source of stock shadcn class strings' is false -- sidebar.tsx (46 shadcn-vocabulary refs) and button.tsx (35) are both shipped and both larger sources than any dead file (file-upload 13, field 11, table 6, card 5). Severity correctly filed as low: dead code renders nothing, so this is a provenance and surface-area finding, not a visual one.

source: shadcn
title: Motion was themed across 8 primitives; color and radius in the same files were not
why: Eight primitives had their transitions rewritten onto repo motion tokens: button (13 motion-token refs), dropdown-menu (10), sidebar (10), select (9), popover (5), tabs (3), dialog (2), alert-dialog (2), sheet (2), using var(--duration-quick), var(--ease-out), var(--press-dur), var(--press-scale), var(--dropdown-pre-scale). button.tsx:7-12 even carries a thoughtful six-line comment explaining the two-clock transition. Yet the same class string at button.tsx:13 keeps rounded-lg focus-visible:border-ring focus-visible:ring-3 focus-visible:ring-ring/50 aria-invalid:border-destructive, and :17-26 keeps every stock variant (bg-primary; border-border bg-background hover:bg-muted; bg-secondary; text-primary). A designer themes color first and motion last. Theming motion while leaving all 35 color references stock is the signature of a mechanical find-and-replace pass over transition properties only. Same shape at tabs.tsx:27, which pairs a repo-token duration with text-muted-foreground and rounded-lg.
fix: Finish the pass these files started. In each of the 8, apply the same substitution discipline already used on the transitions to the color and radius utilities, using kit/atomics/button-class.ts as the reference for what the button variants actually are (primary/secondary/ghost/destructive/soft, not default/outline/secondary/ghost/destructive/link).
note: The premise is half false and the residue duplicates pattern 2. VERIFIED counts are actually HIGHER than claimed and the auditor undercounted the very evidence it relies on: my census of repo-token references gives select 27, button 14 (13 motion + --critical-text), sidebar 10, dropdown-menu 10, dialog 8 (claimed 2), alert-dialog 8 (claimed 2), sheet 6 (claimed 2), popover 5, checkbox 5 (not listed at all), tabs 4 (claimed 3). True population is 10 primitives carrying repo motion tokens, not 8. button.tsx:7-12 is indeed a six-line motion rationale, and :13 does keep rounded-lg / focus-visible:ring-3 / aria-invalid:border-destructive. WHY IT IS OVERSTATED: 'color... was not [themed]' is false -- globals.css's @theme inline routes bg-primary to --accent, text-muted-foreground to --muted, border-input to --line-strong, so these components render in repo color. The only untreated axes are radius and focus, both already counted as patterns 2 and 6, so this is a re-framing of the same defect with a provenance story ('mechanical find-and-replace', 'a designer themes color first') that is inference, not evidence -- and checkbox.tsx:15's hand-written 'the box fills first, then the mark draws itself into it -- two beats, not one snap' is the opposite of a mechanical pass. No visual consequence of its own: on screen the motion looks right.

source: unlayered-cascade.test.ts attributes classes per-file, so a collision
title: A recipe class reaching an element through a shared class constant is invisible to the guard even inside one file, and the docstring frames that indirection only as a false-positive risk
why: Ten class constants in src/ embed an unlayered recipe class in their text: BASE (kit-button), CHART_AXIS_LABEL_CLASS (chart-axis-label), FIGURE_CLASS (t-figure), three `mono` constants in account-security-settings.tsx, LEADS_PANEL_CLASS (coach-panel), ESCALATION_HANDOFF_BASIS, H1_CLASS and STAT_LABEL_CLASS. `classSets` only reads literals inside a `className=` expression, so `className={`${LEADS_PANEL_CLASS} flex min-w-0 ...`}` at leads-surface.tsx:1223 presents the guard with the utilities and no recipe class - `styled` is empty and the site is dropped, in the same file, with no component boundary crossed at all. The docstring anticipates the indirection at :276-281 but only as a source of phantom rows ('a lookup unions every value in the table onto one imaginary element... the fix there is to skip the expression, not to split it'), and concludes the safe move is to skip. That reasoning is one-directional: skipping is safe against false positives and is exactly what makes the missed collisions permanent. Currently only 2 collisions come through this path (leads-surface.tsx:1223 `flex` against `display:flex` and `min-w-0` against `min-width:0`, both duplicates of the sheet's own value, so benign today), but nine of the ten constants sit one edit away from a real one.
fix: Resolve single-file `const NAME = "..."` class constants before tokenizing - utility-collision.test.ts:82-89 already has a `classConstants(source)` extractor doing exactly this, so reuse it - and inline each constant's tokens into the class set at every `${NAME}` interpolation site. Keep the existing skip for genuine lookup tables (`TONE[tone]`), which is a different shape and is correctly out of reach.

source: There is no breakpoint scale, and no scope audited responsive behaviou
tell: Two competing conventions for the same boundary, split by accident of authorship
title: The repo disagrees with itself about where desktop begins (959 vs 1023/1024) and where phone begins (620 vs 639/640)
why: The ten viewport widths resolve into two boundaries, each answered twice with different numbers. "Where desktop begins": globals.css:1623 uses `max-width: 959px`, which is the complement of a 960 grid; consumer.css:1119 uses `max-width: 1023px`, the complement of Tailwind's lg=1024, which 62 JSX sites also use. Both are correctly formed `N-1` complements — they just complement different scales, so the product holds two incompatible ideas of the desktop line 64px apart. "Where phone begins": globals.css:1729 and consumer.css:1166 both use `max-width: 620px` (implying 621), while coach.css:617/:1654 use `max-width: 639px` against :561's `min-width: 640px` (Tailwind sm, which 302 JSX sites use). console.css:355's `max-width: 1180px` implies 1181 and matches nothing else in the repo, and globals.css:1486's 1600 is a content-max rule for a 2000px cap. The tell is not that intermediate widths exist; it is that the same boundary has two answers, and which one you get depends on which stylesheet the surface happens to load.
fix: Collapse each boundary to one number in the --bp-* family: pick 1024 for the desktop line (already the majority at 62 JSX sites plus consumer.css) and retire 959 and 1180; pick 640 for the phone line (302 JSX sites plus coach.css) and retire 620. Express every max-width as the exact N-1 complement of its min-width partner, which coach.css:561/:617 already does correctly and is the pattern worth generalising.
note: All five citations verified and the counts hold. `grep -rn '@media (m..-width' --include=*.css src/` returns exactly 10 sites: consumer.css:1119 (max 1023), consumer.css:1166 (max 620), globals.css:1486 (min 1600), globals.css:1623 (max 959), globals.css:1729 (max 620), console.css:355 (max 1180), coach.css:561 (min 640), coach.css:590 (min 1280), coach.css:617 and :1654 (max 639). Three different tablet/desktop lines do the same collapse job on three surfaces — 959 on `.agent-shell`, 1023 on `.consumer-stage`, 1180 on `[data-shell-role='admin'] .console-deck--lead` — alongside `lg:` (1024) used 67 times elsewhere. The split is real rather than cosmetic: 1023 and 639 are the exact complements of Tailwind's `lg:` and `sm:` and pair cleanly with the utility classes on the same surfaces, while 959 (complement of a 960 that exists nowhere in the scale) and 620 are complements of nothing. I read the lines above each: 620, 959, 1023, 1180 and 1600 all sit under an unrelated preceding rule with no comment of their own, so none of the five odd widths carries reasoning, against a stylesheet convention where coach.css writes a paragraph for 640 and a sentence for 1280. Severity downgraded because the surfaces are genuinely independent and the visible consequence is confined to narrow bands.

source: tokens+globals
title: globals.css reaches for a literal where a token exists on every axis except colour
why: Colour in globals.css is perfect discipline: 208 colour-bearing declarations, 100% through var(--...), zero hex and zero raw rgba()/oklch() in any colour position. Every other axis is the opposite. border-radius: 19 literals against 11 token references, and most of the literals duplicate a token's value rather than needing a new one - `999px` four times (396, 550, 619, 743) where --r-full is 999px; `8px` twice (692, 1254) where --r-chip is 8px; `12px` twice (735, 767) where --r-panel is 12px; `11px` (1067) where --r-well is 11px; `6px` (447) where --r-input is 6px. Alongside those sit values no token carries at all: 13px (219), 9px three times (439, 602, 1179), 7px twice (389, 1682), 5px (1089), 2px (1007). font-size: 27 literals against 8 token references, and `12.5px` appears 6 times (451, 486, 583, 795, 1339, 1399) - a size DESIGN.md names in prose but tokens.css, the stated source of truth, declares no --t-* role for, so the shipped value has no token to drift from. The point is not that literals are forbidden; it is that the same file proves the author can be exhaustive when they choose to be. Colour got the pass, spacing, radius and type did not, which is what a checklist looks like from the outside.
fix: Mechanical sweep: replace every border-radius literal that equals a token's value with the token, and give the four genuinely new radii (13px, 9px, 7px, 5px) either a --r-* token or the nearest existing one. Add a --t-* role for 12.5px in tokens.css (or move the six call sites to --t-badge/--t-body) so the type scale covers what the product actually ships. token-references.test.ts already enforces this shape for --r-*/--s-* references; extend it to reject literals that duplicate a declared token value.
note: The colour half is exactly right and I confirmed it independently: globals.css contains one hex/rgba/oklch match in the whole file and it is inside a comment at line 212 -- zero colour literals in any declaration. The other counts are close but off: border-radius is 30 declarations, 10 through var(), 20 literal (claimed 19/11); font-size is 36 declarations, 8 through var(), 28 literal (claimed 27/8). 12.5px x6 and 999px x4 verified. Two problems. First, the flagged values are documented, so criterion (c) fails on the main examples: DESIGN.md:436 specifies 'buttons 9px' and 'chips and secondary buttons 8px' (covering 439/602/1179 and the chip radii), section 5 specifies the strip's 13px, and 12.5px is a named role in two places -- DESIGN.md Hierarchy 'Card subtitle / secondary (12-12.5px, --faint)' and Buttons 'Secondary / Edit ... 12.5px --body'. The 11px Floor Rule also pins the type-token count at 16 in tokens.test.ts, so a --t- role for 12.5px cannot be added quietly by design. Second, the 'checklist' inference has a mechanical answer: colour must be a var because it forks across four palette blocks, and src/app/agent-surface.test.ts enforces exactly that ('carries no second hardcoded palette'). Radius and font-size do not fork and have no such guard. That is the repo's own rule 9 ('Every rule gets a guard, and the guard is the authority'), not an axis someone forgot. The real residue is nine radius literals that duplicate an existing token's value byte for byte -- 999px x4 (--r-full), 8px x2 (--r-chip), 12px (--r-panel), 11px (--r-well), 6px (--r-input) -- plus undocumented 2px, 5px and 7px x2. Genuine sloppiness with zero rendered difference.

source: canvas
title: The same channel row is spaced three ways on three consecutive onboarding artboards, with two different badge shapes
why: OnboardingConnect.dc.html:124 ("Your channels") and OnboardingGoLive.dc.html:125 ("Ready now") draw the identical row -- 44px leading badge, `font-size: 20px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: -0.015em` "Instagram" heading, `border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line-soft)`. Connect pads it `22px 20px`; GoLive pads it `20px`. Connect's badge is `border-radius: 10px`, GoLive's is `border-radius: 999px`. OnboardingOverview.dc.html:124 draws the third sibling at `padding: 20px 20px 20px 20px; gap: 20px` against the other two at gap 18px. Three adjacent artboards on canvas page-2, one component, three spacings and two badge geometries. The same drift runs through every bordered list row on the canvas: Notifications.dc.html:114 uses `min-height: 96px; padding: 20px 22px; gap: 18px; border-radius: 17px` -- 17px is the panel's bottom-corner radius, not the 11px VOCABULARY.md:68 assigns to "well and stepper row"; Agent.dc.html:128 uses `min-height: 64px; padding: 10px 16px; gap: 16px; radius 11px` while Agent.dc.html:256 uses `min-height: 64px; padding: 8px 8px 8px 16px; gap: 14px; radius 11px` two panels below; Billing.dc.html:177 uses `padding: 16px 20px; gap: 24px`. And on the 390px phone, HomeMobile.dc.html's gutter is 16px in 16 places but 18px in 7 (:191,:195,:203,:211,:219,:223,:231) -- one whole panel indented 2px deeper than its neighbours on a 390px artboard, plus a third value at :183 (`16px 12px 14px`).
fix: Define one list-row shape in VOCABULARY.md's Controls table (padding 20px, gap 16px, radius 11px when it is a well and none when it is a hairline row) and rewrite the seven variants onto it. Fix the phone gutter to a single 16px.
note: The core comparison holds and is the best-evidenced part of this audit. OnboardingConnect.dc.html:124 and OnboardingGoLive.dc.html:125 draw the same row to the byte in every respect except padding: both 'display: flex; align-items: flex-start; gap: 18px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line-soft)', both a 44px leading badge, both an <h3> at 'font-size: 20px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: -0.015em; line-height: 1.2', both a 16px/1.55 --muted line under it. Connect pads '22px 20px', GoLive pads '20px'. That 2px is real and unexplained. The badge half is weaker: GoLive's 999px badge is --good-line/--good-wash/--good-text (a confirmation token) while Connect's r10 badge is --line/--well/--body (the documented icon-button radius, VOCABULARY.md:68), so the geometry follows the tone family rather than drifting. The HomeMobile claim is also real and I confirmed it: lines 191, 195, 203, 211, 219, 223 and 231 use an 18px inner gutter while every other panel on the 390px artboard uses 16px (81, 92, 99-105, 111-165, 174) — one panel indented 2px deeper than its neighbours on a phone board. Everything else in the count is a different component: OnboardingOverview:124 is a numbered stepper row with a 2px connector rail, not a channel row; Notifications:114 is a 96px selectable option card with a 48px icon tile on --accent-edge/--accent-wash, which the doc's 11px 'well and stepper row' radius does not govern; Agent:128 vs :256 are a keyword row and a numbered question row with a drag affordance. The claimed count of 52 bundles at least four unrelated components.

source: tokens+globals
title: Container inner padding takes eight vertical values for one relationship, including two chat bubbles 1px apart
why: Nine rules in globals.css describe the identical relationship - a small bordered box wrapping a line or two of text - and give it eight different vertical paddings: .system-message 7px (693), .decision-badge 8px (1180), .sandbox-banner 9px (603), .message-bubble 10px (661), .receipt-content dl 10px (1215), .go-live-checks 10px (1389), .thinking-bubble 11px (736), .trace-node 11px (1068), .booking-card 14px (768). Horizontal runs 12/12/12/12/13/13/14. Only 8px and 12px are on the scale. The sharpest pair is .message-bubble `padding: 10px 13px; border-radius: 13px 13px 13px 4px` (660-661) against .thinking-bubble `padding: 11px 13px; border-radius: 12px 12px 12px 4px` (735-736): the thinking bubble is the placeholder that is replaced in place by the message bubble, so the two render at the same spot one after the other, and they differ by 1px of padding in one direction and 1px of radius in the other. Nothing in either file explains it. Content swapping into a box should not make the box breathe.
fix: Define two box recipes - a compact one at var(--s-2)/var(--s-3) and a roomy one at var(--s-3)/var(--s-4) - and route all nine rules through them. Make .thinking-bubble share .message-bubble's padding and radius outright, since it is the same box in a different state.
note: The nine literal paddings all exist as cited and I read each one: .system-message 7px 12px (693), .decision-badge 8px 12px (1180), .sandbox-banner 9px 12px (603), .message-bubble 10px 13px (661), .receipt-content dl 10px 12px (1215), .go-live-checks 10px 12px (1389), .thinking-bubble 11px 13px (736), .trace-node 11px 12px (1068), .booking-card 14px (768). Nothing documents them. But the headline example -- the one that carries the argument -- is stale. meet-your-agent.css:231-235 overrides .message-bubble at coach scale to `padding: 13px 17px; border-radius: 14px 14px 14px 5px`, with a comment explaining the jump ('The bubble is the whole point of the screen, so it gets the largest jump on the page: 13px to 16px'). That applies on every mount, so the shipped pair is 13/17 against 11/13, not 1px apart. The 'content swapping into a box should not make the box breathe' framing also does not hold: globals.css:740-749 shows .thinking-bubble contains three animated dots on staggered delays, i.e. a typing indicator, not a text container -- a smaller pill for a dot row is a normal choice, not drift. What survives is eight bordered boxes carrying eight vertical paddings between 7 and 14px, with only 8px and 12px on the scale. Real, undocumented, and imperceptible at 1-2px steps between boxes that mostly never appear adjacent.

source: copy
title: The no-em-dash guard scans only src/components, so 8 em dashes ship to screen from src/app and src/lib
why: This is the repo violating its own documented rule, not a taste call. docs/DESIGN.md:643 says "Don't write an em dash in UI copy", and src/app/em-dash.test.ts enforces it in two forms (U+2014 with escapes/entities decoded, and the ASCII ' -- '). That test's docstring argues at length about closing holes: "Scanning for the literal alone would have left a hole wide enough to reintroduce the whole sweep one file at a time." But both describe blocks pass join(SRC, "components") and nothing else (em-dash.test.ts:88 and :167), so the entire src/app and src/lib trees are unguarded. The gap is provably an oversight rather than a decision, because the sibling typography guard sitting in the same directory already knows the right scope: quote-entities.test.ts:56 reads [...sourceFiles(join(SRC, "components")), ...sourceFiles(join(SRC, "app"))]. Two guards, same file-scanning shape, same author, different scope, and only one of them is right. The result reads as generated because the surviving sentences are exactly the ones a model writes: "SetterFi — your funding DMs answered, qualified and booked" is the public marketing <title>, the single most externally visible string in the product, read by the browser tab and the search snippet. Confirmed rendered: page.tsx:27 is returned from generateMetadata(); account/page.tsx:22-23 are EYE_COPY, passed at line 93 as <ContextEye copy={EYE_COPY} /> and printed at context-eye.tsx:294; reset-password:166 is a JSX text node inside <AuthNotice tone="failure">, an error a locked-out coach reads; admin-help-guides.ts:361 is a guide step caption rendered on /admin/help; atomics-sheet.tsx:195/294/485 are <Section title> strings on the gated /design route. Breakdown: 4 U+2014 (page.tsx:27, atomics-sheet.tsx:195/294/485) and 4 ASCII ' -- ' (account/page.tsx:22 and :23, reset-password:166, admin-help-guides.ts:361).
fix: Widen both scans in src/app/em-dash.test.ts to match its sibling: at line 88 and line 167 replace sourceFiles(join(SRC, "components")) with [...sourceFiles(join(SRC, "components")), ...sourceFiles(join(SRC, "app")), ...sourceFiles(join(SRC, "lib"))], keeping the existing .test.tsx exclusion on the ASCII half. source: There is no breakpoint scale, and no scope audited responsive behaviou
tell: A design system with a token family for every axis except the one being audited (missing scale / ad-hoc values)
title: Zero breakpoint tokens: the one axis of the design system with no scale, no doc, and no test
why: tokens.css spends 1129 commented lines pinning colour, type, spacing, radius, elevation, z-index and motion, and declares the layout tokens that breakpoints actually move (--topbar-h at :257, --sidebar-w). It declares no breakpoint token at all — its only @media is prefers-color-scheme (:411). The @theme inline block (globals.css:7-86) maps colour, radius, font and the nine --t-* type roles into Tailwind's namespaces and never touches --breakpoint-*, so Tailwind's stock 640/768/1024/1280 ship unexamined. docs/DESIGN.md and docs/COACH-REDESIGN-PLAYBOOK.md contain zero occurrences of "breakpoint", "responsive", "viewport", "mobile" or "media query" — I grepped both. The result is 23 distinct hand-picked widths (10 viewport, 13 container) governed by nothing. A system that pins a five-rung z-index scale and a seven-rung duration scale but leaves the axis that decides whether a layout is one column or three entirely ungoverned has an obvious hole, and the omission reads as an axis nobody thought to name rather than one deliberately left free.
fix: Add a --bp-* family to tokens.css with the same commenting discipline as the --s-* rungs, seeded from what the canvas actually supplies (390 phone, 1440 desktop) plus the small number of intermediate widths the product genuinely needs. Map them into Tailwind via `--breakpoint-*` in the @theme inline block so `sm:`/`lg:` and the stylesheets read the same numbers. Add a section to DESIGN.md stating the rule, and a token test in the shape of tokens.test.ts that fails on any @media width or arbitrary container width not drawn from the family.
note: The literal premise is true — `grep -rn -- '--breakpoint' src/` returns nothing, tokens.css has no breakpoint/min-width/max-width text anywhere, the `@theme inline` block (globals.css:7-86) never touches `--breakpoint-*`, DESIGN.md's only width mention is the Line Length Rule at line 371, and COACH-REDESIGN-PLAYBOOK.md is silent. But 'no scale' is false and 'no test' is false. Not overriding `--breakpoint-*` in Tailwind v4 *keeps* the default scale, which is what ships: sm/md/lg/xl are used ~370 times. The component axis is deliberately container-queried, and that choice is written down in at least three places (surface.tsx:132-135 'Admin drops these panels into a 266px list column and a full-width content pane on the same screen, so viewport breakpoints would be measuring the wrong box'; setting-row.tsx:47-51; grid-table.tsx:49) and guarded by a 468-line `src/app/container-queries.test.ts`; `coach-pillbar.test.ts:245` pins behaviour above and below the 640 phone line. The genuine residue is narrower than claimed: 10 width media queries across 4 stylesheets at 8 distinct widths (620x2, 639x2, 640, 959, 1023, 1180, 1280, 1600), of which only the 640/639 pair and the 1280 pill-padding rule carry any written reasoning. n=23 could not be reproduced. The three cited lines are pointers at an absence (tokens.css:257 is `--page-x`, globals.css:7 and 86 are the open and close of `@theme inline`), not evidence of a defect.

source: auth+entry
title: Two thirds of the literal spacing on /design is off the 4px grid tokens.css says it cannot drift off
why: Every literal-px spacing utility in the whole auth+entry surface (12 of them) sits in one file: src/app/design/atomics-sheet.tsx, the page whose own docblock (src/app/design/page.tsx:22-28) says it 'exists so the design system has one place it can be audited.' Of those 12, eight land off the 4px grid: mb-[6px] (:146), gap-[10px] (:126), p-[10px] (:159), p-[10px] (:177), gap-[11px] (:395), gap-[13px] (:317), gap-[13px] (:368), mb-[10px] (:648). A ninth, gap-[28px] (:295), is on the 4px math but is not a rung -- the scale at tokens.css:239-240 runs 4/8/12/16/20/24/32/40/48 and has no 28. tokens.css:291 states the rhythm 'cannot drift off the 4px grid'; DESIGN.md:86-93 repeats the rungs. 6, 10, 11 and 13 are the signature of values typed to look right in a browser rather than picked off a scale, and they appear only here -- the four hand-written auth pages (access, forgot-password, reset-password, the forgot-password form) contain zero literals and spend var(--s-3)/var(--s-4) exclusively. The reference sheet is the least systematic file on the surface it is the reference for.
fix: Snap the eight off-grid values onto the nearest rung and spell them as tokens: 6->var(--s-2), 10->var(--s-3) (or var(--s-2) for the swatch padding), 11->var(--s-3), 13->var(--s-3), 28->var(--s-6) or var(--s-8). Then add the four literal-px spacing offenders to a lint rule or a register test in the shape of entry-surfaces.test.ts's FLOOR_DEBT so the next one is written down rather than argued about.
note: All five file:line citations are real and say what is claimed, and the in-file arithmetic checks out: atomics-sheet.tsx carries exactly 12 literal-px spacing utilities, 8 off the 4px grid (mb-[6px]:146, gap-[10px]:126, p-[10px]:159, p-[10px]:177, gap-[13px]:317, gap-[13px]:368, gap-[11px]:395, mb-[10px]:648) plus gap-[28px]:295 which is on the math but is not a rung. tokens.css:239-240 and DESIGN.md:86-93 are quoted correctly. Three things collapse the finding. (1) THE RULE DOES NOT EXIST AS QUOTED. tokens.css:291 reads 'Each step aliases a --s-* rung so the rhythm cannot drift off the 4px grid' -- the subject is the --d-* rhythm steps aliasing --s-* rungs, not a global law over every spacing value in the app. tokens.css:238's '(4px grid)' header scopes the --s-* family only. Nothing in tokens.css, DESIGN.md or COACH-REDESIGN-PLAYBOOK.md forbids an off-grid spacing literal, and no test guards it (I enumerated src/app/*.test.ts). (2) THE SYSTEM ITSELF IS DELIBERATELY OFF THE 4PX GRID. globals.css:154 .surface-card padding 16px 17px, :193 .surface-well 12px 13px, DESIGN.md:428-429 .surface-strip 15px 17px, radii 14/11/9/8/6, --t-mono-crumb 11.5px, --t-nav 13.5px, --d-row 36px, --d-row-quiet 54px. DESIGN.md's stated philosophy is the artifact's own value, unrounded. Odd values are the house style, not the tell. (3) THE EXCLUSIVITY CLAIM IS FLATLY FALSE, and in the direction that kills the 'reference sheet is the least systematic file' rhetoric. Literal-px spacing outside atomics-sheet, inside the same auth+entry scope: auth-shell.tsx:61 gap-[28px] and :285 mt-[7px]; login-form.tsx:148 gap-[18px]; signup-form.tsx:165 gap-[18px], :166 gap-[14px], :175 gap-[14px], :188 gap-[10px], :195 gap-[9px]+px-[10px]; auth-card.tsx:48 gap-[22px], :59 gap-[18px] and inline padding '28px 30px 30px', :110 px-[14px]; optin-artifact.tsx:117 mt-[6px], :307 mt-[3px]. That is 15 more, most off-grid (7, 18, 9, 3, 6, 22, 14, 30). The four page.tsx files are clean, but the stage components they mount -- which ARE the entry surface -- are more literal-heavy than the sheet being indicted. One more correction: p-[10px] at :177 is itself dead (see pattern 4), so only 7 of the 8 off-grid literals render at all. source: canvas
title: Segmented control ships in three shapes and contradicts the doc's own parenthetical about page-header height
why: VOCABULARY.md:85 says "segmented control | 44px (48 in a page header) | segments padding 0 18px in a 12px well with 4px padding". Main.dc.html:113 puts one in the page header (same flex head, `margin-bottom: 32px`, same flex-end slot as Leads) at 44px. Leads.dc.html:114 and LeadsBoard.dc.html:114 put one in the identical page-header slot at 48px. Six artboards choose 44px in a page header (Main:113, Loading:111, ErrorState:110, SupportBubble:109, AccountMenu:109, Vocabulary:133) against two that choose 48px -- so either the parenthetical is wrong or three-quarters of the canvas violates it, and the outer well ends up 52px on some pages and 56px on others in the same optical position on the same 1440px grid. Inbox.dc.html:110 then draws a third shape entirely: 44px segments at `padding: 0 20px; border-radius: 999px` inside a `padding: 4px; border-radius: 999px` well, where the doc specifies a 12px well and 0 18px segments. One control, three geometries, and the spec sheet cannot be satisfied by any of them simultaneously.
fix: Pick 44px everywhere (it is what six of eight artboards already draw and it matches the 44px icon-button rung), delete the "(48 in a page header)" parenthetical from VOCABULARY.md:85, and bring Leads/LeadsBoard down to 44 and Inbox's pill variant onto the documented `0 18px` in a 12px well.
note: All five citations check out and the contradiction is real. I extracted every segmented well: 11 across the canvas, and all 11 match VOCABULARY.md:85 exactly on well radius (12px), well padding (4px), segment padding ('0 18px') and segment radius (9px). Only the height varies: 44px x9, 48px x2. Main.dc.html:113 and Leads.dc.html:114 sit in byte-identical page headers — both files run 'padding: 36px 40px 96px' then 'display: flex; align-items: flex-end; justify-content: space-between; gap: 40px; margin-bottom: 32px' holding an h1 at 46px/600/-0.026em and a 17px status line, with the control in the flex-end slot. Main draws 44px, Leads and LeadsBoard draw 48px, and the doc says '44px (48 in a page header)'. Six page headers take 44 (Main:113, Loading:111, ErrorState:110, SupportBubble:109, AccountMenu:109, Vocabulary:133) against two that take 48, and the canvas's own spec sheet takes the 44 side — Vocabulary.dc.html:275 is captioned 'Segmented: 44px in a 12px well'. So the markdown and the drawing disagree, which is exactly the internal inconsistency worth reporting. Two corrections. The 'cannot be satisfied by any of them simultaneously' claim is wrong — Leads and LeadsBoard satisfy the parenthetical precisely, and their 48px matches the 48px Export button beside them in the same slot. And Inbox.dc.html:110's third geometry is arguable rather than drift: it sits in a filter toolbar ('padding: 18px 40px', --pane, border-bottom), not a page header, and its 999px well over 999px segments carrying mono count badges is the documented navigation-pill family (chrome snippet, VOCABULARY.md:107-109), not a segmented control. Visually this is a 4px control height on boards that never appear in one view, so medium is a rung too high.

title: The agent surface writes spacing as raw off-grid px while its sibling consumer sheet is 100% tokenized
why: tokens.css:291 states the rhythm 'cannot drift off the 4px grid'. Full histogram for my scope. consumer.css: 83 spacing declarations, 71 use var(--s-*), 0 contain a px literal, 120 var(--s-N) references total (s-4 x26, s-2 x26, s-3 x25, s-1 x15, s-5 x14, s-8 x4, s-10 x4, s-12 x4, s-6 x2). meet-your-agent.css: 12 spacing declarations, 3 tokenized, 10 carry a px literal. rehaul/meet-agent.tsx: 39 arbitrary-px spacing classes, 0 var(--s-*) uses of any kind. Off the 4px grid, by instance: gap-[10px] x4, px-[18px] x2, pt-[18px], py-[19px], py-[14px], py-[11px], px-[15px], gap-[11px], gap-[7px], gap-[6px], mt-[10px] (15 in the tsx); padding:19px 22px, padding:13px 17px, padding:0 14px, padding:2px 10px, gap:2px (5 in meet-your-agent.css); gap:6px (1 in meet-your-agent.module.css). A further 22 of the tsx's 39 classes spell an exact --s-* rung as a literal (px-[20px] x5 = --s-5, gap-[12px] x4 = --s-3, gap-[8px] x3 = --s-2, py-[12px] x2, px-[24px] x2 = --s-6, gap-[16px] x2 = --s-4, px-[16px], pb-[8px], gap-[24px], gap-[20px]) - the token exists and is simply not reached for. Two more are on the 4px grid but off the --s-* scale entirely: mt-[28px] and gap-[44px] (meet-agent.tsx:511), which is also the page-head to first-block gap and the section gap, so the vertical rhythm answers to neither --d-head-gap (20px) nor --d-section-gap (32px). Those three --d-* rhythm tokens are used 0 times in my scope and only 8 times repo-wide - declared, commented at length in tokens.css:288-294, then ignored. The tell is not that literals exist; it is that the same feature area contains a sheet that never uses one and a sheet that almost never uses a token, with no rule anywhere explaining the split.
fix: Replace the 22 rung-valued literals with var(--s-N) mechanically. For the 15 off-grid values, snap to the nearest rung unless a canvas line can be cited (see the fabricated-citation pattern - for this screen none can). Bind mt-[28px] to var(--d-head-gap) and gap-[44px] to var(--d-section-gap) or state in the file why this screen's rhythm is its own.
note: The arithmetic is almost perfect but the rule it is measured against does not exist. title: One spacing value, three spellings: bare literal, a MOTION travel token, and fractional calc() on the 4px rung
why: 6px is written three different ways inside one folder. (1) As a literal: `gap-[6px]`/`px-[6px]`/`mt-[6px]` x11 (status.tsx:91, field.tsx:183, segmented.tsx:113, coach-pillbar.tsx:88, impersonation-banner.tsx:239, deck-panel.tsx:408, ...). (2) As `gap-[var(--distance-small)]` x4 (currency-input.tsx:100, field.tsx:203, persona-switcher.tsx:44, step-journey.tsx:229) — but tokens.css:311-316 is the block headed "Motion tokens, copied from .agents/skills/transitions-dev/_root.css", and --distance-small is how far a thing TRAVELS, not how far two things sit apart. Borrowing the motion scale for layout means a future motion tune silently reflows four components. (3) As `calc(var(--s-1)+var(--s-1)/2)` x6 (filter-bar.tsx:417/446/475, toast-preset.ts, segmented-control.tsx). The same laundering produces the other off-grid numbers: `calc(var(--s-1)/4)` x11 is a 1px BORDER WIDTH expressed as a quarter of the 4px spacing rung (filter-bar.tsx:278, 322, 335, 417, 438, 446, 475, 476, 480, 505; segmented-control.tsx:64), `calc(var(--s-1)/2)` x7 = 2px, `calc(var(--s-2)+var(--s-1)/2)` x4 = 10px, plus 26px, 30px, 22px and 14px each built the same way. Wrapping an off-grid number in arithmetic on a grid token does not put it on the grid; it only makes the drift unsearchable. The sharpest single line: step-journey.tsx:229-230 sets the same element's gap from TWO DIFFERENT SCALES on adjacent lines — resting `gap-[var(--distance-small)]` (6px, motion) and emphasised `gap-[var(--s-2)]` (8px, spacing).
fix: Pick one spelling per value. If 6px is a real rung the design needs, declare --s-1-5: 6px in tokens.css with the reasoning and point all three spellings at it; otherwise snap them to --s-1 or --s-2. Replace all 11 `[border-width:calc(var(--s-1)/4)]` with a --line-w (or plain 1px) token — a border width has no business reading from the spacing scale. Ban --distance-* outside transition/transform properties with a source-scanning test.
note: Counts hold up. I measured exactly 11 literal 6px spacing utilities in kit (4 gap, 3 mt, 2 px, 1 mb, 1 pt), exactly 4 `gap-[var(--distance-small)]` (currency-input:100, field.tsx:203, persona-switcher:44, step-journey:229), 7 `calc(var(--s-1)+var(--s-1)/2)`, 11 `calc(var(--s-1)/4)`, 7 `calc(var(--s-1)/2)`, 4 `calc(var(--s-2)+var(--s-1)/2)`. tokens.css:296 does head the block 'Motion tokens, copied from .agents/skills/transitions-dev/_root.css' and --distance-small is at :314. The one defensible kernel is those 4 gap uses: borrowing a travel distance for a layout gap is an undocumented category error that couples layout to a motion tune. Everything around it weakens. atomics/tone.ts:125 shows the repo reasoning explicitly about sizing off the motion scale ('Sized off --distance-base so it tracks the motion scale, not a literal'), so the practice is at least partly a considered convention, not an accident. The calc family is not scattered drift: it is a consistent local dialect confined to filter-bar.tsx, segmented-control.tsx, view-switch.tsx and toast-preset.ts, where every dimension is derived from --s-1. And the 'sharpest single line' is a misread: step-journey.tsx:229-230 sets 6px on the resting state and 8px on the `emphasised` state -- two different states of the element deliberately given different air, not one relationship answered twice. Nothing here is visible without grep; 6px renders as 6px however it is spelled.

title: Five one-off gradient geometries invented outside the four the canvas ships and the three DESIGN.md names
why: The approved vocabulary is small and closed. All 22 artboards between them contain exactly four gradient strings: the card face, `--accent-fill` at 180deg, `--pane-bloom` at `85% 50% at 78% -8%`, and the drench at 158deg. DESIGN.md adds one more by name, the tone frame at `radial-gradient(120% 140% at 12% 0%, ..., transparent 62%)` (DESIGN.md:579), which surface.tsx:73 implements faithfully. Everything else in the tree is invented, and each one answers "add depth here" a different way: a 150deg accent->accent-active fill on the Monogram avatar (icon-tile.tsx:118) at an angle used nowhere else in the product; a 90deg progress fill that mixes each tone 62% with pure `black` (progress.tsx:9), a lightening ramp with no counterpart in tokens.css, where `--accent-fill` walks only 0.08 of lightness; a fifth radial geometry `circle at 50% 50%, ..., transparent 42%` on the trace canvas (globals.css:1020) sitting beside `--pane-bloom`'s and the tone frame's two; and a 180deg `--accent-wash -> transparent` row tint on the client drawer (success-client-book.tsx:986) where the token is already a flat 7%/14% alpha and the fade adds nothing the wash does not. None carries a comment justifying its geometry, which is conspicuous in a repo where the four token gradients each carry a paragraph and a measured ratio. The angles alone -- 150, 158, 160, 180, 90, 270 -- read as five authors rather than one system.
fix: Pick one bloom geometry (`--pane-bloom`) and one frame geometry (the tone frame) and route globals.css:1020 through them. Drop the 150deg monogram fill to flat `--accent` or to `--accent-fill` at the system's 180deg. Drop the progress fill to flat `TONE_MARK[tone]`, or if a ramp is genuinely wanted, define it as a token with the same lightness delta `--accent-fill` uses instead of mixing to black. Replace success-client-book.tsx:986 with flat `var(--accent-wash)`.
note:
ALL FIVE CITATIONS ARE EXACT AND REAL -- icon-tile.tsx:118 (150deg accent to accent-active), progress.tsx:9 (90deg color-mix 62% with black), globals.css:1020 (radial circle at 50% 50%, transparent 42%), success-client-book.tsx:986 (180deg accent-wash to transparent), metric-card.tsx:72 (radial closest-side). The canvas premise also verifies exactly: the 22 .dc.html artboards contain precisely four gradient strings and nothing else.

BUT THE FRAMING AND THE COUNT BOTH FAIL:
(1) 'The approved vocabulary is small and closed' is the auditor's inference, not a repo rule. Nothing in tokens.css, DESIGN.md or the playbook closes the gradient set. And design/coach/*.dc.html is the COACH subset -- docs/REDESIGN-CANVAS.md says the canvas is 55 artboards. Three of the five flagged surfaces (MetricCard, the agent trace canvas, the admin client book) are console/agent surfaces the 22 coach artboards were never drawn to cover. Judging them against a canvas that does not include them is the wrong authority.
(2) 'Five' is arbitrary. A full enumeration of gradients under src/ finds ~11 geometries outside the canvas four and the tone frame -- including two 90deg/270deg canvas edge-fade masks, a `to bottom, transparent, var(--card) var(--s-4)` overflow fade, the kit skeleton's shimmer sweep, and a `linear-gradient(TONE_ROW_TINT, TONE_ROW_TINT)` flat-colour-as-image tint. Most of those are functional masks, not answers to 'add depth here.' The finding neither counted them nor excluded them on a stated principle.
(3) 'None carries a comment justifying its geometry' is FALSE. progress.tsx:7 carries one directly above the function: 'The fill gradient for a tone: the tone's own mark lightening left to right.'
(4) One of the five (metric-card.tsx:72) renders on no shipped page -- the finding's own pattern 5 concedes this. So four ship, not five.

VISUAL CONSEQUENCE: mostly nil. 150deg vs 180deg on a ~28px Monogram avatar is imperceptible. The 180deg accent-wash fade on an expanding drawer row reads as a deliberate 'this row is open' top-light. Only the progress fill's steep mix-to-black walk (~0.21 of lightness against --accent-fill's 0.08-0.105) is a treatment a designer would notice as off-system.

why: consumer.css:120-122 declares `.consumer-shell :where(a, button, textarea, [tabindex]):focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring); outline-offset: 2px }` — the same width, the same token, the same offset as tokens.css:976, for a subset of the elements the global already covers. title: The four tail roles have zero base-palette coverage and each carries one unqualified best-case number

Separately --dim is declared four times (tokens.css:125/459/613/820) and consumed nowhere under src/ -- a role whose measured ratio has been maintained across four blocks and has no consumer.

But two of the four roles are explicitly documented at the floor they meet, so the finding collapses to two. console.css:634 and tokens-contrast.test.ts:735-740 both state in the repo's own words that "--dim and --glyph are the two roles the base palette already holds to 1.4.11's 3:1 rather than 4.5 -- weekend letters and icon strokes". Dark --glyph measures 3.63 on canvas, 3.41 on card, 3.14 on card-top and 3.14 on raised: it CLEARS 3:1 on every real ground, so the claim that 3.14 is "under 1.4.11's 3:1" is simply wrong. Only the band composite (2.70) dips, and --glyph on a table group band is speculative -- field.tsx:83 paints it inside an input, app-shell.tsx:261 on the rail, tone.ts:38 as a dot. Same for --meta: 4.34 on band-over-card-top is a 3.5% shortfall, but app-shell.tsx:304 is a rail group label and owner-clients.tsx:1263 is a table footnote row, neither of which sits on --band. --dim really is declared four times (tokens.css:125/459/613/820) and consumed zero times in src -- I confirmed that with ripgrep -- but a dead token has no contrast consequence at all. source: Date, number and locale formatting consistency — no scope owned it, no
title: Currency assembled by hand with a literal dollar sign, bypassing money()'s currency argument
why: metric.ts:33-38 exports `money(cents, currency)` and its test at metric.test.ts:12 proves the currency argument works (`money(12_345, "GBP")` → "£123.45"). Two sites instead prefix a literal `$` onto a plain NumberFormat: owner-clients.tsx:688 `` `$${Math.round(mrr / 100).toLocaleString("en-US")}` `` — in a file that already imports from @/lib/format/datetime at :61 — and render-placeholders.ts:24 `` `$${new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", { maximumFractionDigits: 0 }).format(cents / 100)}` ``, which composes lead-facing agent copy. Hardcoding the glyph makes the currency unreachable and puts the symbol outside the number's formatting, so a non-USD tenant renders a dollar sign over a euro amount. It also produces a third money shape ("$1,234") beside the canonical "$1,234.00" and the shadow view-model's "$1,234".
fix: Call `money(mrr, currency)` at owner-clients.tsx:688 and `money(cents, currency)` at render-placeholders.ts:24. If 0-decimal display is wanted, add it as an option to `money()` so all callers inherit it.

source: Date, number and locale formatting consistency — no scope owned it, no
title: A `locale` knob on the shared column factories that no caller anywhere overrides
why: `moneyColumn` and `numberColumn` each declare `locale?: string` on their options type and default it to "en-US" (:148, :196), then build a fresh `Intl.NumberFormat(locale, ...)` per column (:153, :200). Searching every call site in src/components and src/app turns up no caller passing `locale:` to either factory — the only `locale:` hits in the surface tree are unrelated message-template and export fields. So it is a per-column locale override in a product whose canonical module pins exactly one locale at datetime.ts:18 and whose contrast-and-token discipline is otherwise built on single sources of truth. Speculative generality of this shape is the standard generated-code tell: an axis of variation invented because the API looked more complete with it, not because a screen asked. Low severity — the default is correct, nothing renders wrong today — but it is one more place a fifth locale can enter without the guard noticing.
fix: Drop the `locale` field from MoneyColumnOptions and NumberColumnOptions and hoist the two formatters to module-level constants built from the canonical locale (or reuse `workspaceCountFormat` / `money()`), which also stops re-allocating a formatter per column definition.

source: Date, time and number formatting has no audit scope and is systematica
title: A percentage has eleven spellings, and the docstring that names the exact bug sits above one of them
why: stat-strip.tsx:134-138 states the rule and names the failure: "a second copy of this function is how '6%' here and '6.0%' there gets into the product. One definition, two renderers." Both spellings it warns about are live simultaneously. admin-overview.tsx:1198 renders `${ONE_DECIMAL.format(value)}%` with minimumFractionDigits forced to 1 — that is the "6.0%" — while measurement-view-models.ts:148 renders a raw `${value}%` with no formatter at all, which is the "6%" and will happily print an unrounded float. Counting distinct constructions of a percentage: formatMetric's Intl style:"percent" (metric.ts:7); stat-strip.tsx:148's Intl percent with forced precision; admin-overview.tsx:1198's ONE_DECIMAL plus a literal %; admin-measurement-view-models.ts:94's PERCENT_FORMATTER plus a literal %; measurement-view-models.ts:148's bare interpolation; measurement-view-models.ts:388's `${Math.round(rate * 100)}%`; coach-analytics.ts:77's `.toFixed(1)}%`; admin-overview.tsx:735, admin-money-billing.tsx:686, coach-agent.tsx:1804 and escalation-panel.tsx:139's Math.round-plus-literal-%. Eleven. The same fragmentation shows in the helper names — measurement-view-models.ts:146 and admin-measurement-view-models.ts:92 both declare a local `function formatMetric` shadowing the exported formatMetric from metric.ts:40, and admin-overview.tsx imports the real one at line 34 while hand-rolling the percent branch at line 1198 rather than using it. Numbers show a third locale spelling too: four constructors pass "en" instead of "en-US" (measurement-view-models.ts:155 and :386, admin-measurement-view-models.ts:108, eval-comparison-view-models.ts:69), which is harmless in output but is a third way of writing the pinned locale that datetime.ts:89 specifically comments on.
fix: Extend metric.ts's formatMetric with an optional precision argument so it covers every percent case, then replace all eleven constructions with calls to it — the literal-% branches especially, which bypass Intl entirely. Rename the two shadowing local formatMetric functions. Normalise the four "en" locale literals to "en-US".
note: This inverts what the docstrings say. All three headline citations carry comments that JUSTIFY their shape — the exact 'deliberate is not slop' exclusion. admin-overview.tsx:1184-1194: the docstring names the drift ('6%', '6.3%', '8.3%', '77.8%') as the bug it FIXES with one decimal. admin-measurement-view-models.ts:85-90 explains the 4.166666666666667 overflow and states 'One decimal is what the shared formatter in lib/format/metric.ts uses' — and it cannot simply reuse metric.ts's PERCENT_FORMATTER because that one is style:"percent" and divides by 100 while these values already carry percent units. stat-strip.tsx:136-142 justifies the exported precision helper outright: 'a second copy of this function is how "6%" here and "6.0%" there gets into the product. One definition, two renderers.' The probe read three justifications as three indictments. What IS real is a case the probe never cited: measurement-view-models.ts:148 returns `` `${value}%` `` with NO rounding at all — the unfixed twin of the seventeen-digit overflow docs/COACH-REDESIGN-PLAYBOOK.md:203-205 records as a lesson learned. Severity is capped low because I traced it: that value flows only through coachMeasurementView/coachPipelineView into src/app/api/exports/[resource]/handler.ts, a CSV export, with no UI card consumer — so it cannot overflow a card the way the playbook describes. coach-analytics.ts:77's toFixed(1) is a second real variant, in src/lib and outside the guard's scan roots.

source: auth+entry
title: The same visual relationship takes 2-3 different values within one file, on four separate relationships
why: Four distinct relationships each get more than one value, all inside src/app/design/atomics-sheet.tsx. (1) RESPONSIVE CARD-GRID GAP: three `grid grid-cols-[repeat(auto-fit,...)]` containers doing the identical job -- :158 gap-[12px] (surface swatches), :317 gap-[13px] (KPI tiles), :368 gap-[13px] (chart cards). DESIGN.md:436 fixes the card grid at '12px gap'; two of the three are 1px off it and off the --s-3 rung. (2) LABEL-ABOVE-ITS-BLOCK bottom margin takes three values: :146 mb-[6px] (h1 -> subline), :648 mb-[10px] (Overline -> KeyValueList), :680 mb-[var(--s-4)] = 16px (prose -> StepJourney). (3) HORIZONTAL SPECIMEN ROW: :126 gap-[10px] is the gap inside every Specimen (30+ renders), but the type card's specimen row at :295 is gap-[28px] -- a 2.8x difference for the same 'row of things being compared' relationship. (4) VERTICAL STACK INSIDE A CARD: :386 gap-[8px], :395 gap-[11px], and :196/:369/:384/:661 gap-[var(--s-4)] = 16px, three values for one relationship 9 lines apart at the 8/11 pair. A designer picking these would not land on 12 and 13 for two adjacent card grids, or 10 and 28 for two specimen rows; a generator emitting each block independently would.
fix: Pick one value per relationship and name it. Card grids -> var(--s-3) (12px, what DESIGN.md:436 already says). Specimen row -> var(--s-3) at :126 and :295. Card interior stack -> var(--s-4) at :386 and :395. Label-above-block -> var(--s-2) at :146 and :648 to match :680's tokenized sibling, or lift all three to the --d-stack-gap step.
note: Citations are all real, but three of the four sub-claims mischaracterize the relationship being compared. (1) RESPONSIVE CARD-GRID GAP -- REAL. :158 gap-[12px], :317 gap-[13px], :368 gap-[13px] are three auto-fit card grids with three min-widths and two gap values; 12 vs 13 in one file is a genuine drift. DESIGN.md:436 does say 'Grid: 1fr 1fr, 12px gap', but read in context that is the coach artifact's two-column card grid ('The attention card and the managed strip take grid-column: 1 / -1'), not a generic auto-fit specimen grid, so the doc is not being violated. (2) LABEL-ABOVE-ITS-BLOCK -- NOT ONE RELATIONSHIP. :146 mb-[6px] is h1 to its own subline; :648 mb-[10px] is an Overline to a KeyValueList; :680 mb-[var(--s-4)] is a paragraph to a StepJourney. A title-to-subline pair being tighter than a paragraph-to-component break is exactly the graded rhythm the repo documents in kit/templates/rhythm.ts (BREAK.crumb 8px vs BREAK.head 20px). Collapsing three tiers into 'one relationship' is the auditor's move, not the code's. (3) SPECIMEN ROW 10 vs 28 -- WRONG LEVEL. gap-[10px] at :126 is inside a Specimen, between the atoms being compared (Figure, Figure, Figure). gap-[28px] at :295 is on the Surface, between whole labelled Specimens (three of them, :296/:302/:307). Those are different nesting levels; there is no 2.8x on one relationship. The real inconsistency here is one the auditor missed and inverted: specimen-to-specimen gap is 28px at :295 but gap-[var(--s-4)]=16px at :196/:369/:384/:661. (4) VERTICAL STACK IN A CARD -- WRONG LEVEL AGAIN. gap-[var(--s-4)] at :196/:369/:384/:661 is the Surface's gap between Specimens; gap-[8px] at :386 and gap-[11px] at :395 are inside two different Specimens' demo stacks. Only 8 vs 11 is a same-level pair. Net: 2 real relationships (grid gap 12/13; specimen-set gap 28 vs 16), not 4. All of it is 1-3px on a staff-only page; nothing here is visible.

Five are `pb-[64px]` (:257, :320, :359, :386, :434) and the sixth is `pb-[60px]` (:545) — a lone 4px difference on the final CTA with no comment, which is what a value looks like when it was typed rather than derived. The head-to-body gap inside a section is `mb-[26px]` at :360, :387 and :435 — consistent among themselves, off the 4px grid, and equal to no token (--d-head-gap is 20px). The card grid gap is `gap-[18px]` at :364, :393 and :457 but `gap-[40px]` at :343 and :546 and `gap-[56px]` at :257, so "the space between sibling cards" is three values with no rule distinguishing them. The drench panel at :343 is `pt-[30px] pb-[32px]` — asymmetric by 2px, both values unexplained, 30 off-grid. --d-section-gap (32px) exists for precisely this stack and is used nowhere.
fix: Wrap the six sections in one `flex flex-col gap-[var(--d-section-gap)]` container and delete the six per-section `pb-` values, keeping only the deliberate hero `pt-[56px] lg:pt-[76px]`. Normalise `mb-[26px]` to `var(--d-head-gap)` unless a reason for 26 gets written down, and make the drench body padding symmetric or say why it is not.
note: The 60-vs-64 outlier is real and I confirmed it: five sections carry the byte-identical string `px-[var(--s-5)] pb-[64px] sm:px-[48px]` (:257 via a longer variant, :320, :359, :386, :434) and :545 carries pb-[60px]. But that is the opposite of 'hand-set per section': five of six are one repeated literal, which is a rule, and the drift is exactly one value on the terminal section, sitting directly above a `border-t` footer (:560) with no sibling beside it to compare against. Invisible in the shipped page. The card-gap claim is a conflation of three different relationships, not three values for one: gap-[18px] at :364/:393/:457 is the 3-up and 2-up card grid; :343's gap-[40px] is a three-figure stat row inside the drench panel; :546's gap-[40px] is a flex row between a heading block and a button; :257's lg:gap-[56px] is the hero's two-column split. mb-[26px] is 3/3 consistent. --d-section-gap is the admin console's token, not a coach one (see pattern 2), so its absence here proves nothing. Residual: the pb-60 outlier plus :343's 2px-asymmetric pt-[30px] pb-[32px].

source: consumer+agent
title: Comments assert a canonical value, then the declaration on the next line writes a different one
why: Three verified cases where the prose cites an authority and the value beside it contradicts that authority. (1) meet-your-agent.css:184 says 'The header band, at the deck panel's own anatomy: 19px/22px padding'; line 190 sets padding: 19px 22px. The deck panel's anatomy is 19px 20px - stated in coach.css:256 and set at coach.css:264, restated at coach.css:315, :358 and :653, drawn 7 times unanimously in design/coach/Agent.dc.html (lines 120, 134, 171, 188, 205, 244, 300, all 'min-height: 78px; padding: 19px 20px'), and pinned by deck-panel.test.tsx:156 ('pads the band at the artboards 19px 20px'). The agent sheet copies the 78px floor correctly and invents the 22. The guard did not catch it because it tests .coach-panel__header, not .chat-heading/.trace-heading. (2) meet-your-agent.css:200-201 says 'Sentence case at 12px, which is coach.css's eyebrow. The canvas draws this particular label at 14px; the 12px role is used instead...' - a full paragraph of reasoning for declining the canvas. --coach-eyebrow is 14px (coach.css:36). The rule renders at exactly the value the comment claims it rejected, and the argument is backwards. coach.css:267-272 documents this precise stale comment as a known defect and repaired it there ('The comment here said 12px for a while after the token moved, which is the same mistake in miniature'); meet-your-agent.css:107 and :200 still carry it. (3) consumer.css:74 says the drench is 'at coach.css's exact value' - the gradient on :80 is byte-identical, but --consumer-on-drench-sub on :81 is rgba(255,255,255,0.85) against --coach-on-drench-sub's 0.8 (coach.css:95), and it is the one value in that 1,355-line file with no comment. A designer reads reasoning that does not describe the code as a sign the reasoning was generated after the fact.
fix: Set meet-your-agent.css:190 to 19px 20px (or lift the band into the deck-panel rule and delete the override); rewrite the :107 and :200 comments to say 14px; either justify 0.85 or set it to 0.8. Extend deck-panel.test.tsx's band assertion to cover .chat-heading/.trace-heading so the next copy cannot drift.
note: Two of three cases are real, one is not, and all three are prose defects with zero rendered consequence. Case 1 verified but mis-titled: meet-your-agent.css:184 says '19px/22px' and :190 sets 19px 22px, so the comment and the declaration AGREE - the falsehood is the claim that this is 'the deck panel's own anatomy' when the deck's anatomy is 19px 20px (coach.css:264, seven unanimous draws in design/coach/Agent.dc.html, pinned at deck-panel.test.tsx:156). A 2px deviation from a cited source, invisible on screen because .chat-heading and .trace-heading both take 22 and so align with each other. Case 2 verified: --coach-eyebrow is 14px (coach.css:36) and meet-your-agent.css:200-201 argues for 12px while :206 renders the 14px token. But this is a known, repo-wide, already-diagnosed staleness, not a local tell: the same 12px prose survives at meet-your-agent.css:107, consumer.css:14, leads-surface.tsx:393, coach-pipeline.tsx:525, landing-page.tsx:84 and in docs/DESIGN.md:343 itself, and coach.css:270-274, coach-type-floor.test.ts:16 and coach-data-panel.test.ts:129 all name it explicitly as the mistake being tracked. Case 3 fails: consumer.css:74's sentence governs the drench, and the drench on :80 IS byte-identical to coach.css:92. --consumer-on-drench-sub on :81 is a different token, and 0.85 vs 0.8 white is MORE contrast on a surface whose own header (consumer.css:1-11) argues for legibility for a stranger reading one-handed outdoors. The 'one value in that file with no comment' claim is false - the sheet comments in blocks, and :81 sits inside one.

source: There is no breakpoint scale, and no scope audited responsive behaviou
tell: Self-inconsistency: one surface stepping at three widths, putting sibling elements into contradictory layout modes
title: Meet Your Agent steps at 620, 639 and 959; between 621px and 639px its type is in phone mode while its chrome is still in desktop mode
why: This is the band the gap brief predicted, and it is real — though it is 621-639px, not the 620-641 guessed, and it is one surface contradicting itself rather than two components on a page. The chain is verified end to end: meet-your-agent.tsx:583 renders `<CoachScale as="main" className={cn("agent-shell", ...)}>`; coach-scale.tsx:47 stamps `data-shell-role="coach"` on that same element and coach-scale.tsx:36 imports coach.css; meet-your-agent.css:193-194 selects `[data-shell-role="coach"].agent-shell` and reads `--coach-panel-name`, so the file knows it is coach-stamped. So one element tree is governed by three viewport steps owned by two stylesheets that never coordinated. At <=639px coach.css:640 drops --coach-panel-name to 19px and :632 drops --topbar-h to 60px — phone density. At <=620px globals.css:1729 hides `.brand-name`, `.topbar-slash` and `.context-label` (rendered at meet-your-agent.tsx:588, :597, :600, :606) and raises buttons to the 44px touch floor. At <=959px globals.css:1623 reflows `.agent-topbar` to 58px with wrapping. Between 621px and 639px inclusive the headings have already gone to phone size while the topbar still shows the wordmark, the slash and the "Preview as" label, and buttons are still below the 44px floor the coach density mandates. A second defect sits underneath: `.agent-topbar` hard-codes `min-height: 50px` (globals.css:344) and 58px at <=959px, ignoring --topbar-h entirely — the very token coach.css:73-81 overrides to 76px specifically so "the four surfaces that compute against it" stay correct.
fix: Move the globals.css 620 block to 639 so the agent chrome steps on the same line as the coach density, and delete the 959 block or re-express it at 1023 (see pattern 7). Make `.agent-topbar` read `min-height: var(--topbar-h)` instead of hard-coding 50px/58px, which is the mechanism coach.css:73-81 already documents.
note: The mechanism is real and I verified the whole chain: meet-your-agent.tsx:583 mounts `<CoachScale as='main' className='agent-shell'>`, so the surface carries `data-shell-role='coach'`; meet-your-agent.css:194 reads `font-size: var(--coach-panel-name)` under `[data-shell-role='coach'].agent-shell`; coach.css:617's `@media (max-width: 639px)` block re-declares `--coach-page-title: 30px`, `--topbar-h: 60px` and `--coach-panel-name: 19px` (line 640); globals.css:1729's `@media (max-width: 620px)` hides `.brand-name`/`.topbar-slash`/`.context-label` and raises dialog targets to 44px on the same shell. So a 19px band at 621-639px does exist in which the coach type tokens have stepped to phone while that chrome has not. What is wrong is the characterisation. The chrome in that band is not 'desktop' — globals.css:1623's `@media (max-width: 959px)` block is already active, having wrapped `.agent-topbar`, hidden `.topbar-spacer`, reordered `.context-switcher` and switched `.agent-workspace` to mobile panel tabs. So the surface is in tablet chrome with phone type, and the delta inside the 19px band is one step (brand name still shown, dialog buttons not yet 44px), not a phone/desktop contradiction. The 959 step is also a separate concern — collapsing a two-pane workspace — rather than a third leg of a type/chrome disagreement. What survives is worth one line: the coach-role agent shell changes density at both 620 and 639, which is the thing coach.css:613 says it wrote 640 to avoid.

source: layout-cliche
title: Accent-washed pill sitting directly above the hero h1, restating the footer verbatim
why:
Line 259 is a rounded-[var(--r-full)] span with an --accent-edge border, --accent-wash fill, mono face and 0.03em tracking, reading "For credit and business-funding coaches", placed with mb-[22px] immediately above the h1 at line 268. It also carries zero information the page does not already state -- the footer at line 562 reads "SetterFi · Built for credit and business-funding coaches", near-verbatim, and the h1 plus subhead name funding DMs, Instagram and Facebook outright. A file whose docblock argues at length for restraint ("it keeps declining to overclaim", "exactly one accent fill face") opens by spending a third accent element in the hero on a decorative label. Compounding it: the artboard cited as authority for this page, Landing.dc.html (line 10), does not exist in design/ -- so the badge has no pixel authority behind it either.
