note:
The element is real and the count of 1 is right. landing-page.tsx:259 is a `rounded-[var(--r-full)]` span with `border-[var(--accent-edge)] bg-[var(--accent-wash)] text-[color:var(--accent-text)]`, mono, 0.03em tracking, mb-[22px], reading "For credit and business-funding coaches", immediately above the h1 at :268. I grepped the whole repo for `inline-block rounded-[var(--r-full)]` and for accent-wash pills: line 259 is the only accent-washed pill anywhere, and the only chip above an h1 outside ProvenanceChip (kit/page-header.tsx:191-198, a required seeded-data disclosure). auth-shell.tsx:149 is a bare `

` eyebrow as claimed. The footer at :562 reads "SetterFi · Built for credit and business-funding coaches", near-verbatim. The copy string appears nowhere else in the repo — no canvas, no doc, no test — so nothing justifies it, and the artboard cited as its authority does not exist. There is even a stronger charge the auditor did not make: DESIGN.md:459-462 reserves accent-wash on accent-edge with accent-text for the **Selected** chip, "and selected means *the coach chose it*", and the Ownership Rule at DESIGN.md:263-267 says accent marks what the coach set or can act on. A stranger who has chosen nothing is neither. Two things force a downgrade. First, the fill accounting is wrong: the docblock's boast is "exactly one accent fill face" and the One Fill Rule (DESIGN.md:259-262) governs *solid fills*. A wash-and-edge chip is not a fill, and the page's single fill ("Start your setup", pinned at landing-page.test.tsx:239-245) is intact. "Spends a third accent element" is rhetoric, not a rule breach. Second, and decisive under the shipped-UI test: by this audit's own pattern 1 this component never renders in either flag branch, so no designer looking at the product ever sees the badge. Real tell, correct count, but low severity on unreachable code.

source: kit-content
title: Form-control heights drift 1px between three controls designed to sit on one row
why: Inside one file: FieldShell is `h-[34px] ... px-[11px]` (field.tsx:40), SelectShell is `h-[33px] ... px-[11px]` (field.tsx:147), ValueReadout is `h-[33px]` (field.tsx:270). These three are the input, the select and the numeric readout that appear side by side in a settings row, and two of them are a pixel shorter than the third. Nothing in the file mentions it. The contrast inside the same folder is what makes this a tell rather than a nit: atomics/button-class.ts:9-15 sets exactly three heights (26/30/34) and spends a comment saying they "are places rather than preferences: `sm` (26px) is an action inside a queue row, `md` (30px) an action on a toolbar, `lg` (34px) the page's own header action. The artifact draws exactly these three and nothing between them." The button ladder is decided; 33-vs-34 is residue. It also breaks the button ladder's own claim — a 33px control is a fourth height between 30 and 34.
fix: Set all three shells to h-[34px] to match FieldShell and the button `lg` rung, or better, declare a --control-h token (34px) beside --d-row in tokens.css and have field.tsx:40, 147 and 270 plus button-class.ts:14 read it, so the input row and the header action are provably the same height.
note: The citations are exact: field.tsx:40 FieldShell h-[34px] px-[11px], field.tsx:147 SelectShell h-[33px] px-[11px], field.tsx:270 ValueReadout h-[33px], and button-class.ts:11 is the sm rung of the documented 26/30/34 ladder. The controls do co-occur -- atomics-sheet.tsx:279-288 puts KitInput, two SelectShells and a ValueReadout in one flex specimen, and :497/:505 place ValueReadout and SelectShell as SettingRow controls -- so a 1px height difference is real and undocumented. But two things shrink it. The button-ladder argument is a category error: button-class.ts:7-9 says 'the artifact draws exactly these three' about buttons, and DESIGN.md's own component spec already lists a fourth control height in between (button-secondary at 29px), so a 33px input violates nothing. And the visual consequence is 1px of height on a bordered control -- invisible in the shipped UI unless the two are baseline-checked side by side. This is one residual inconsistency in one file, not a three-way drift; ValueReadout and SelectShell agree with each other, so only FieldShell is the odd one out.

source: copy
title: Both runtime copy sanitisers strip U+2014 but not the ASCII ' -- ', enforcing the encoding instead of the rule
why: Two functions scrub em dashes out of operator-facing text at render time, and both do it with the identical one-liner value.replaceAll("—", ",") — operatorCopy at admin-help.tsx:54 and displayCopy at admin-provisioning.tsx:110. Neither touches the doubled hyphen. This is precisely the failure src/app/em-dash.test.ts calls out in its own second describe block, in its own words: "a guard that reads only the Unicode codepoint is enforcing the encoding rather than the rule." The repo diagnosed the bug, wrote a whole test to close it in src/components, and left the same bug live in the two runtime sanitisers that exist for the same purpose. It is not hypothetical: admin-help-guides.ts:361 contains "...on older instructions -- that is a conversation with the coach, not an incident", and that string is fed through operatorCopy at admin-help.tsx:324 as operatorCopy(step.caption) and reaches /admin/help unchanged. The second consumer is worse: account-sheet.tsx:40 imports ADMIN_GUIDES and renders guides at :1065 with no sanitiser at all, so both spellings pass through there. A sanitiser that catches one of two spellings of the same mark is the signature of a fix applied to the symptom that was visible rather than to the rule that was written.
fix: Give both sanitisers the whole rule rather than half of it. Extract one shared helper (next to the guide data, or in src/lib/copy/) that does value.replaceAll("—", ",").replace(/ -- /gu, ", "), and have admin-help.tsx:54 and admin-provisioning.tsx:110 both call it. Better still, fix the source string at admin-help-guides.ts:361 so nothing has to be scrubbed at render time, and cover src/lib/admin-help-guides.ts with the widened guard from the previous pattern — then the sanitisers become a belt-and-braces layer over already-clean input rather than the only thing standing between the guide text and the screen. Also decide whether account-sheet.tsx:1065 should route guide copy through the same helper, since today it renders ADMIN_GUIDES with no sanitising at all.
note:
CITATIONS: the three evidence lines are correct. src/components/workspace/admin-help.tsx:54 is `value.replaceAll("—", ",")` as the reduce seed inside operatorCopy (declared :51). src/components/onboarding/admin-provisioning.tsx:110 is `return value.replaceAll("—", ",");` inside displayCopy (declared :109). src/lib/admin-help-guides.ts:361 does contain "...working correctly on older instructions -- that is a conversation with the coach, not an incident" and it does reach admin-help.tsx:324 as operatorCopy(step.caption). The em-dash.test.ts:130-131 quote is verbatim. So the mechanical claim — two sanitisers, both catching only the codepoint — is true.

BAD CITATION: the "second consumer is worse" argument is false. src/components/workspace/rehaul/account-sheet.tsx:40 does import ADMIN_GUIDES, but :1065 renders `ADMIN_GUIDES.slice(0, 5).map(...)` printing only `{guide.title}` (:1069) — never caption, heading, outcome, or steps. I extracted all 23 guide titles from src/lib/admin-help-guides.ts; not one contains U+2014 or ' -- '. Nothing passes through that consumer in either spelling, so the claim that it is "worse" is unsupported.

COUNT: claimed 2. Two sanitisers with the asymmetry is literally true, but the count that matters — strings actually affected on screen — is 1: admin-help-guides.ts:361 on /admin/help. displayCopy's only call site is admin-provisioning.tsx:734, `displayCopy(selected.detail)`, whose input is runtime tracker data with no evidence any value contains ' -- ' (every ' -- ' in that file is in a comment or an eslint-disable pragma). And that single affected string is the same one already counted in pattern 1, so this is largely a re-count of one line dressed as a second systemic pattern.

DELIBERATENESS: em-dash.test.ts:25-28 explicitly names these sanitisers as legitimate reasons the glyph survives in the tree — "two copy-sanitisers strip it out of generated operator text" — and their sibling replacements in OPERATOR_COPY_REPLACEMENTS (admin-help.tsx:33-40: persisted→saved, tombstones→deletion protection records, Unavailable→Could not read just now) show these functions are vocabulary translators for authored/generated operator text, not the enforcement point for the copy rule. Stripping U+2014 there is defensive normalisation of a character a data source might carry; ' -- ' is a keyboard typo whose correct fix is the source string, not a runtime rewriter. Nothing in tokens.css, DESIGN.md's Corrections, or COACH-REDESIGN-PLAYBOOK.md asks these functions to enforce the ban.

WOULD A DESIGNER NOTICE: only on /admin/help, an operator-only page, in one sentence, and only if reading closely. Everywhere else this is grep-visible with zero rendered consequence.

source: public/site/ — the page that actually serves `/` in production — is 2,
title: The day half of the copy palette is a byte-exact token copy; the night half is invented, and one invented accent sits in a rule that can never match
why: index.html:39-41 declares --ink-now #181e28, --soft-now #333d50, --over-now #5e6b83. Converting tokens.css's light roles to sRGB gives --ink (tokens.css:104) = #181e28, --muted (:106) = #333d50, --overline (:124) = #5e6b83 — three exact matches, and the file states a real reason for the sRGB form (the verification harness cannot parse oklch). Three lines later, index.html:44-46 gives the night triple as #f4f5f8, #c0c4cc, #9aa5b8, and none of the three matches any role in either dark block: dark --ink converts to #e8edf6, dark --faint to #9dadcb, dark --overline to #6d7d99. #c0c4cc in particular is r192 g196 b204, effectively a flat grey, in a system whose entire neutral ramp is tinted at hue 262 and whose own vendored stylesheet warns "Tinted, never flat gray" (scrollcraft.css:25). index.html:416 adds `oklch(0.78 0.12 264)` as a night accent, matching neither dark --accent-bright (0.8148 0.085 264) nor dark --accent-text (0.8586 0.062 265) — a higher chroma than any accent role in the palette — and the rule is unreachable: its only target, `.named` at index.html:639, lives in copy--hero, whose data-sc-window closes at pr 0.0691 (t≈1.11) while data-phase does not go night until t≈1.74. Two of the six copied literals are also dead on arrival: `var(--well)` (index.html:25) and `var(--faint)` (:26) have zero references in the file. Half faithfully extracted, half freehand, is the signature of a palette that was copied once and then improvised on.
fix: Replace index.html:44-46 with the sRGB conversions of tokens.css's dark --ink / --muted / --overline (#e8edf6 / the dark --muted value / #6d7d99), delete the unreachable rule at index.html:416 or point it at dark --accent-bright, and delete the two unused copies at index.html:25-26.
note: Both halves of the factual claim check out; the framing does not. I converted the OKLCH: index.html:39-41's #181e28/#333d50/#5e6b83 are exactly tokens.css:104 --ink, :106 --muted and :124 --overline. That is compliance, not a defect, and the hex form is justified in-file two lines above (index.html:37-38: "the verification harness reads computed text colour as r,g,b and cannot parse an oklch() value"). The night triple (#f4f5f8/#c0c4cc/#9aa5b8) is indeed not the dark tokens (#e8edf6/#b5c1d8/#6d7d99) -- but the page's night ground is oklch(0.16 0.025 262) while the product's dark --canvas is oklch(0.1342 0.0172 262.2) (tokens.css:415), so the dark tokens' measured contrast ratios would not transfer anyway; there is no rule requiring the match. The one defensible residue is the dead rule: `html[data-phase="night"] .copy .named` at index.html:416 can never be seen. The page's only `.named` is at index.html:639 inside `.copy--hero`, whose data-sc-window is "0.0 0.0691 0 0.45" -- gone by t≈1.18 of a 17-unit track -- while night begins where the G track crosses 0.55, at t≈1.74 (interpolating index.html:777-778). One dead declaration, zero pixels.

source: public/site/ — the page that actually serves `/` in production — is 2,
title: A hardcoded follow-up schedule the platform does not run, contradicted by this page's own alt text three elements away
why: The "Smart follow-ups" card (index.html:610-620) renders a concrete schedule: `+3 h` at :615, `+1 d` at :616. src/lib/followups/touch-lists.ts:26-31 fixes DURABLE_TOUCHES at 2h, 1d, 3d, 7d, 14d, and its docstring says the timing lives in code precisely "because changing consumer-message frequency requires the review and test trail of a deploy" — so the first touch shipped is +2h, not +3h. The +3h/+1d pair is the retired cadence from docs/APPOINTWISE-LEARNINGS.md:45 ("five touches at 3h, 1d, 1d, 2d, 2d"), which src/components/workspace/rehaul/coach-agent.test.tsx:279-281 records as superseded by DURABLE_TOUCHES. The page then contradicts itself: index.html:562's alt text says the agent "follows up five times over fourteen days", which matches the shipped list and not the timeline drawn 53 lines below it. DESIGN.md:632-634 bans exactly this — "Don't hardcode a count, a date, or a statistic the code cannot derive", with "replies in about 12 minutes" as the named example. This is the one finding here with a direct commercial cost: a prospect who signs up on the strength of the drawn schedule gets a different one.
fix: Change index.html:615 to `+2 h` and add the remaining shipped touches (+3 d, +7 d) or trim the card to the two touches that fire before the reply, so the drawing and touch-lists.ts agree. Longer term, generate this card's rows from DURABLE_TOUCHES at build time the way coach-agent.tsx:49 does, so the marketing page cannot drift from the cadence again.
note: One real discrepancy, one hour wide, and the contradiction claim is backwards. index.html:615 shows "+3 h" where src/lib/followups/touch-lists.ts:27 sets touch 1 at 2 * HOUR_MS -- that part holds. But index.html:616's "+1 d" matches touch-lists.ts:28 (DAY_MS) exactly, so it is not evidence. And the alt text at index.html:562, "follows up five times over fourteen days", matches DURABLE_TOUCHES exactly -- five touches, last at 14 * DAY_MS (touch-lists.ts:26-32) -- so it corroborates the code rather than contradicting the card; a ladder cancelled on reply at index.html:617-618 is entirely consistent with a five-touch schedule. The section is also aria-labelled "sample data" at index.html:612, and docs/DESIGN.md:632 is aimed at product surfaces fabricating advisory statistics, not at a marketing illustration of a cancelled cadence. What survives is a single number that should read "+2 h".

source: gradients
title: A dead full-page shimmer gradient in globals.css, duplicating the live one with different colour, timing and no reduced-motion guard
why: globals.css:1451-1503 declares a whole loading surface -- `.agent-loading`, `.skeleton`, `.skeleton::after`, `.loading-topbar`, `.loading-panels`, `.loading-heading`, `.loading-message`, `.loading-composer`, `.loading-trace`, `.loading-receipt` -- whose sweep is `linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, var(--agent-loading-sheen), transparent)`. Nothing in the tree renders any of those class names; the 13 route-level `loading.tsx` files re-export `kit/skeleton`'s default instead. So this gradient never paints. The live shimmer, kit/skeleton.tsx:11, is a different gradient for the same effect: `--line-strong` at 50% opacity instead of `--muted` mixed to 8%, `to right` instead of `90deg`, on `::before` instead of `::after`, 1.6s with `var(--ease-out)` instead of 1.3s linear -- and it carries `motion-reduce:before:hidden` while the dead copy carries nothing. Both drive the same `@keyframes skeleton-shimmer` at globals.css:1511. The dead one's 1.3s is hardcoded, so the `--duration-*` collapse in the reduced-motion block at globals.css:1855 cannot reach it -- precisely the trap globals.css:751 identifies for `.thinking-bubble` and handles by naming that rule in its own `prefers-reduced-motion` block. page-skeleton.tsx:31 meanwhile asserts the product has one shimmer ("the only [animation] the skeleton itself carries is the kit Skeleton's single shimmer sweep, which `motion-reduce` drops"), which is true only because the second one is dead. Two implementations of one effect that disagree on colour, direction, duration, easing and accessibility is the signature of a treatment that was regenerated rather than reused; css-budget.test.ts is currently paying 53 lines of its 3,100-line cap for the half that never renders.
fix: Delete globals.css:1451-1503 (`.agent-loading` through `.loading-receipt`) and the now-unused `--agent-loading-*` aliases, keeping `@keyframes skeleton-shimmer` at 1511 since kit/skeleton.tsx reads it. If any of those routes actually wanted a full-page loading surface, the fix is to point their `loading.tsx` at `kit/page-skeleton` rather than at `kit/skeleton`'s single-bone default -- but that is a separate change and should not revive the dead CSS.
note:
THE DEAD CODE IS REAL. `.agent-loading`, `.skeleton`, `.skeleton::after` and the eight `.loading-*` rules are referenced nowhere in the tree (verified by grepping every classname across the whole repo excluding node_modules and .git -- zero hits outside globals.css and one test comment). The gradient at globals.css:1470 never paints. Citations at globals.css:1470/:1473 and skeleton.tsx:11/:14 are all exact.

BUT THE LOAD-BEARING CLAIM IS FLATLY REFUTED, AND THE NUMBERS ARE WRONG:
(1) 'The dead one's 1.3s is hardcoded, so the --duration-* collapse cannot reach it' is FALSE. globals.css:1939-1946, inside the same prefers-reduced-motion block, is a universal rule: `*, *::before, *::after { animation-duration: 0.001ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important; ... }`. It reaches `.skeleton::after` directly. The block's own comment at globals.css:1852 says this is exactly why it exists: 'the universal rule catches hardcoded durations like the sheet primitive's duration-200.' The .thinking-bubble opt-out at :751 is needed for a different reason -- it has to settle at a resting opacity, not merely stop -- so the 'precisely the trap' parallel does not hold. There is no accessibility gap here.
(2) '13 route-level loading.tsx files' -- true count is 43, and they route to two different components (kit/skeleton and kit/page-skeleton), not one.
(3) 'globals.css:1451-1503... 53 lines' -- the block runs 1451 to 1484, 34 lines. css-budget.test.ts (cap 3,100, counting only top-level src/app/*.css) is paying 34, not 53.
(4) 'Two implementations that disagree on colour, direction, duration, easing and accessibility' -- they disagree on the first four; on accessibility they do not, per (1).

VISUAL CONSEQUENCE: none whatsoever. It never renders. By the stated test -- grep-only with no visual consequence -- this is a dead-code cleanup, not a design finding.

source: admin-console
title: The console gutter is `--s-4 + 2`, shimmed per slot, and one slot was missed
why: The kit atomics draw on the grid: grid-table.tsx:103, :152 and :240 all use `px-[var(--s-4)]` (16px). console.css:560 and :565-566 override each to a flat 18px — a 2px shim over a token rung, with no reasoning given. queue-item.tsx:47 draws `px-[14px] py-[12px]`; console.css:576 rewrites it to `13px 18px`. metric-card.tsx:62 draws `p-[15px_16px]`; console.css:498 rewrites it to `14px 16px` — moving the vertical by exactly 1px and leaving the horizontal at 16px, so the tile is the one slot the shim forgot. Five overridden slots, five different destination numbers, none derived from a token, and a 1px vertical delta that no reader can perceive and no comment explains. The comment above :498 justifies the border-radius in four sentences and never mentions the padding it changes on the same line.
fix: Pick one console gutter (18px, snapped to a rung, or 16px = --s-4 and drop the shim entirely), apply it to all five slots including metric-card, and delete the 1px vertical nudge at :498 unless a measurement justifies it.
note: The pattern's thesis is falsified on four of its five slots. 'console.css:560 and :565-566 override each to a flat 18px ... with no reasoning given' is simply untrue: the comment seven lines above, at :553-558, reads 'Table rows at 12px 18px, which is the console column of the density table. The head and footer take the same 18px gutter so the columns line up through all three bands; only the horizontal padding moves there, because the head's 9px and the footer's 11px are already right and a row height set in two places drifts.' And 'the console column of the density table' is a real, findable document: COACH-REDESIGN-PLAYBOOK.md:140 and REDESIGN-CANVAS.md:64 both publish '12px 18px' as the owner console's table row padding. The queue row at :576 is likewise reasoned at :569-574 with a canvas citation. 'Five different destination numbers' is wrong - four of five slots land on one horizontal (18px) by explicit design; the console gutter is a single decided value, not a per-slot shim. What survives is exactly one item, and it is the one the finding gets right: metric-card.tsx:62 draws p-[15px_16px] and console.css:498 rewrites it to 14px 16px, moving the vertical by 1px while the four-sentence comment above it (:490-496) discusses only the border-radius and never mentions the padding on the same line. That is a real unexplained edit, and it is a 1px change on a 90px tile - no designer sees it.

source: admin-console
title: --d-head-gap is declared with a paragraph of reasoning and used zero times; the admin pages invent a sixth vertical step
why: tokens.css:292-294 names three rhythm steps and explains at :291 that `each step aliases a --s-* rung so the rhythm cannot drift off the 4px grid`. Repo-wide, --d-section-gap has 7 consumers, --d-stack-gap has 1, and --d-head-gap has **zero** — the head break is spelled `mt-[var(--s-5)]` at rhythm.ts:24 while the section break two lines later at :29 correctly reads `var(--d-section-gap)`. Two of four steps go through the semantic token, two bypass it, in the same 40-line file. console.css contributes no rhythm at all: its only block margins are `margin-top: auto` (:300) and `margin-top: 8px` (:292). And the three admin pages that stack a block after a card hand-roll `mt-[var(--s-2)]` — a top-margin step that is not one of rhythm.ts's five sanctioned BREAK values (its 8px step, `crumb`, is a *bottom* margin for a different relationship). Three pages, one unsanctioned step, on the surface the --d-* block was written for.
fix: Point rhythm.ts:24 at var(--d-head-gap) and rhythm.ts's control step at var(--d-stack-gap), then replace the three hand-rolled `mt-[var(--s-2)]` with the BREAK step that names the relationship — or delete --d-head-gap and --d-page-x from tokens.css if the console is never going to read them.
note: The dead-token half is true and I confirmed it: --d-head-gap appears only at tokens.css:293 and in tokens.test.ts:210, zero shipped consumers. Everything built on top of it is wrong or inconsequential. 'Two of four steps go through the semantic token, two bypass it, in the same 40-line file' is false - rhythm.ts declares FIVE steps (crumb, head, section, control, bareControl at :22, :24, :29, :34, :39) and exactly ONE of them reads a --d-* token. '--d-section-gap has 7 consumers' is inflated: 3 in shipped code (rhythm.ts:29, settings-layout.tsx:71, page-skeleton.tsx:326); the remainder are four test assertions, a README row and a comment line. And the visual consequence is precisely zero: --d-head-gap is literally defined as var(--s-5), so rhythm.ts:24's mt-[var(--s-5)] renders the identical 20px - this is a naming preference visible only to grep. The 'unsanctioned sixth step' is 8px, which is an --s-* rung squarely on the 4px grid, attached to a disclosure hanging off an error card - not a page-template block that BREAK is the contract for. Per the rule that grep-only findings with no visual consequence are downgraded, this is one dead token and nothing else.

source: ui+marketing+onboarding
title: landing-page.tsx re-types its own PANEL_HEAD constant verbatim instead of using it, and gives the same header band a third value
why: Line 83 declares `const PANEL_HEAD = "border-b border-[var(--line)] px-[22px] py-[15px]"` under a comment reading "The deck panel's anatomy, written once." It is used at :286 and :367. At :484 the identical string is hand-expanded inline — `flex items-start justify-between gap-[var(--s-3)] border-b border-[var(--line)] px-[22px] py-[15px]` — which is not just PANEL_HEAD retyped but PANEL_HEAD plus the exact wrapper classes from its own usage at :286, retyped as one literal. The constant is 400 lines above and the file imports nothing to reach it. At :325 the same role, a panel header band closed by a hairline, is `px-[26px] py-[19px]` — a third value, off-grid, with no comment. The comment claiming the anatomy is "written once" is falsified two ways in the same file. Marketing has no artboard (design/ contains only coach/), so no pixel authority defends the 26px. Change PANEL_HEAD and the pricing cards silently drift out of alignment with the hero and how-it-works panels.
fix: Replace the literal at :484 with `${PANEL_HEAD} flex items-start justify-between gap-[var(--s-3)]`, matching :286 exactly. Then decide whether the drench band at :325 is a distinct role: if it is, give it its own named constant beside PANEL_HEAD saying so; if it is not, set it to PANEL_HEAD's 22/15. Same treatment for the panel body, which is `p-[22px]` at :296/379/400/417/532 but `px-[22px] py-[var(--s-6)]` at :450/497, `px-[22px] py-[var(--s-4)]` at :310, `px-[26px] pt-[30px] pb-[32px]` at :343 and `px-[44px] py-[40px]` at :546 — six paddings, one role, no constant.
note: The core defect is real and I confirmed it: line 484 is `flex items-start justify-between gap-[var(--s-3)] border-b border-[var(--line)] px-[22px] py-[15px]`, byte-for-byte PANEL_HEAD (:83) plus the wrapper classes from its own use at :286, hand-expanded. Change PANEL_HEAD and the pricing cards drift. But it is ONE site, not four, and the audit undercounted the constant's real uses: PANEL_HEAD is applied at :286, :367, :396 and :413 — four times, not two — so 'retypes instead of using it' is backwards. The `px-[26px] py-[19px]` at :325 is not a third PANEL_HEAD value: it is the drenched proof band, a distinct surface (`--coach-drench-live` ground, `--coach-on-drench-line` hairline), and 19px/26px is precisely the coach row padding docs/COACH-REDESIGN-PLAYBOOK.md §11 tables as coach density ('table row padding | 19px 26px'). The 'no pixel authority defends the 26px' claim also cuts the other way: landing-page.tsx:10 states `Landing.dc.html` on the redesign canvas 'is the authority for every word and every measurement here', and that file is simply not checked in — the measurements are unverifiable from this repo, not disproven. Visually nothing is wrong today because the duplicated string is identical.

source: ui+marketing+onboarding
title: src/components/ui/ is a second control scale that was never reconciled with the design system, and select.tsx forks itself inside one file
why: The 40 primitives in ui/ carry 165 Tailwind-numeric spacing utilities against 1 arbitrary-px — a clean island that shares no notation with the rest of the scope — and they size controls at h-6/h-7/h-8/h-9 (24/28/32/36px) while the artboard-traced controls in step-shell.tsx:39/63/70 are 48px and coach.css enforces a 44px pressable floor. input.tsx:12 is `h-8 px-2.5 py-1`; the field it is meant to be is `h-[48px] px-[16px]`. Only 3 of the 40 are imported anywhere in this scope. select.tsx is the sharpest case: it ships two live trigger implementations in one file, dispatched by overload at :261 — line 32 is token-native (`rounded-[var(--r-control)]` = 4px, `min-h-9`, `text-xs`, `border-[var(--line)]`) and line 359 is stock shadcn (`rounded-lg` = 14px, `data-[size=default]:h-8`, `text-sm`, `border-input bg-transparent`). Same role, same file, 4px versus 14px corners and 36px versus 32px height. profile-step.tsx:203 and calendar-step.tsx import the stock one and then override height, radius, padding and type size with STEP_FIELD_CLASS at every call site, which is the tell that the primitive is fighting the design system rather than expressing it. Relatedly, tokens.css:243-249 defines seven radius rungs (4/6/8/11/12/14/999) and the scope writes `rounded-[9px]` 6 times and `rounded-[10px]` 7 times — neither is a rung, and both are consistent enough among themselves to be real decisions that simply never got a token. (Checked and cleared: the primitives' 353 semantic colour classes are legitimate — globals.css:8-26 maps them onto the design tokens via @theme inline.)
fix: Decide whether ui/ is vendor surface or product surface. If product: collapse select.tsx to one trigger — keep the token-native one at :32, delete the stock string at :359, and raise it to the 48px/9px face the step files override it to anyway, which removes the per-call-site overrides. Then add `--r-control-lg: 9px` and `--r-tile: 10px` to tokens.css so the 13 hand-written radii have a rung to name. If vendor: mark ui/ as untouched upstream in docs/DESIGN.md and stop importing from it on coach-density surfaces.
note: The select.tsx fork is real and I confirmed both halves are live: `selectTriggerClassName` at :32 (min-h-9, `rounded-[var(--r-control)]` = 4px, text-xs) drives OptionsSelect, reached by 5 files via `<Select options=…>`; `SelectTrigger` at :359 (data-[size=default]:h-8, `rounded-lg`, and globals.css:43 maps `--radius-lg: var(--r-card)` = 14px) is exported and used by 10 files. Same role, 4px vs 14px corners, no comment explaining the split. That one finding stands. Everything else around it is refuted. The 32px control scale is not unreconciled — tokens.css:1029-1039 documents it in so many words: '44px because a tap target belongs to the input device … `console.css` re-authors this to its 32px, the exception a mouse-driven audience earns', and console.css:60-68 performs that re-authoring; playbook §11 tables coach 44px against console 30-34px as two deliberate densities. So input.tsx:12's h-8 and button.tsx:30's h-8 are the console face, correctly, and profile-step.tsx:203 overriding with STEP_FIELD_CLASS is the documented shared-consumer situation (playbook Part 2: 'Shared components have three consumers … check every consumer before rewriting anything shared'). The radius sub-claim is flatly wrong: `border-radius: 9px` appears 132 times and `10px` 97 times across design/coach/*.dc.html, including Vocabulary.dc.html and all six Onboarding artboards — `rounded-[9px]`/`rounded-[10px]` are canvas pixel authority, not untokenized accidents.

source: typography
tell: self-inconsistency — a weight asked for that next/font never downloads, so the browser synthesizes the face
title: One mono readout asks for weight 600 that IBM Plex Mono is not loaded at, producing a synthetic bold
why: layout.tsx:22-27 loads IBM_Plex_Mono with `weight: ["400", "500"]` — two static weights, no variable axis — and tokens.css:114-116 states the constraint explicitly: "IBM Plex Mono ships 400 and 500 only, which is why --w-mono has two steps and not four". Every other mono site in the product respects it: the four stylesheet mono rules all set 500 (consumer.css:241, console.css:275/426, coach.css:457), the twenty design/coach/*.dc.html mono spans use only 400 and 500 (52 at 500, 6 at 400, zero above), and every Tailwind mono site uses `font-medium` or `font-[500]`. day-counter.tsx:127 is the single exception: `className="mono text-row font-semibold"`, i.e. IBM Plex Mono at 600, which the browser can only fake by smearing the 500 master. It sits, per its own comment at :124-126, "in the same well as mono timestamps and mono counts on five surfaces" — all of which render a real 500 — so the one number in the well that was moved onto the mono face to line up is the one drawn with a synthesized weight.
fix: Change `font-semibold` to `font-medium` on day-counter.tsx:127, matching every other mono figure in the product, or add "600" to the IBM_Plex_Mono weight array in layout.tsx:22-27 if a mono semibold is genuinely wanted (it would then need a line in DESIGN.md §3, which currently says "IBM Plex Mono 400/500"). A lint rule refusing `font-semibold`/`font-bold` in the same class string as `mono`/`font-mono` would keep it from recurring.

source: shadcn
title: The one test guarding the shadcn kit pins the shadcn vocabulary and a foreign brand color
why: kit.test.tsx is the only test covering ui/, and it validates nothing about this design system. Line 19 hardcodes const primaryBackground = 'rgb(9, 105, 218)', which is #0969DA, GitHub's brand blue. It appears nowhere in tokens.css, which declares every color in OKLCH. Line 24 then injects its own <style> defining .bg-primary { background: rgb(9,105,218) }, and line 34 sets --color-primary on the host to the same literal, so the assertion at :61 that the button's background equals the token is circular: it compares a value the test itself wrote to a value the test itself wrote, and would pass identically if tokens.css were deleted. Line 57's expect(button).toHaveClass('bg-primary') actively pins the shadcn vocabulary as correct, so any attempt to port Button to --accent-fill breaks this test. The describe block is even named 'shadcn UI kit' (:18). Everything else is a smoke test that six components mount. Nothing asserts a radius, a spacing rung, a type role, or a real token.
fix: Rewrite against real tokens: drop the injected stylesheet and the rgb(9,105,218) literal, mount under the actual tokens.css cascade, and assert what matters, i.e. resolved border-radius equals --r-control for a button and --r-input for an input, and the computed background traces to --accent-fill. Remove the toHaveClass('bg-primary') assertion so it stops blocking the port.
note: Every citation is exact and the circularity is real, but the finding is out of the audit's declared scope and has zero visual consequence. VERIFIED line by line: :18 `describe("shadcn UI kit"`, :19 `const primaryBackground = "rgb(9, 105, 218)"` (= #0969DA; absent from tokens.css and globals.css, both of which are OKLCH), :24 injects `.bg-primary { background: rgb(9,105,218) }`, :34 sets `--color-primary` on the host to the same literal, :57 `toHaveClass("bg-primary")`, :61 compares the computed background to the host's --color-primary. Both sides of :61 are values the test itself wrote, so it would pass with tokens.css deleted -- the circularity claim is correct. FACTUAL ERROR: 'kit.test.tsx is the only test covering ui/' is false. src/components/ui/select.test.ts (64+ lines of class-string assertions on real repo tokens) and src/components/ui/select.test.tsx (behavioural, composed API) both cover ui/, and src/lib/workspace-round4.test.ts:244-254 asserts --shadow-raised/--card/--line/--r-card/--r-control on the select class names. SCOPE: the audit brief excludes test files as findings, and a test renders nothing -- no designer looking at the shipped UI could see this. It is corroborating evidence for pattern 1, not an independent design-system finding.

source: consumer+agent
title: Horizontal inset takes six spellings in one 344-line sheet and five values down one phone column
why: Within meet-your-agent.css alone the left/right inset is written as var(--s-5) (:129 topbar), 14px (:148 chrome controls), 22px (:190 panel band), 16px (:277 chip), 16px again (:290 composer input), 17px (:233 bubble) - six spellings, one of them the token, for the same visual job of holding content off an edge. In rehaul/meet-agent.tsx the phone is a single 390px column and its stacked children inset by 20px (head, :513), 18px (message list, :542), 15px (bubble, :554), 18px (composer, :581) and 16px (input, :593), so nothing down the phone's left edge aligns with anything above it. The ledger beside it insets at 24px (:318, :643) while the panel band above the ledger insets at 20px (:617), so the header text and the first row it heads start at different x. This is the tell in its purest form: no two values are far enough apart to read as a deliberate step, and none is a rung on the scale the repo says it uses.
fix: Pick one inset per container class from the --s-* rungs (20px = --s-5 for panel chrome, 16px = --s-4 for interior content reads correctly against the canvas) and apply it down the whole column, so the phone head, message list, bubble and composer share one left edge.
note: Both halves are miscounted. In meet-your-agent.css, :277 and :290 are both 16px - that is one spelling used twice, so the sheet has five distinct values, not six. Those five sit on six different objects at six nesting levels: a topbar gutter (:129), a chrome button's own padding (:148), a panel header band (:190), a 44px pill chip's padding (:277), an input's padding (:290) and a bubble's padding (:233). Giving a pill 16px of side padding and a panel band 20px of gutter is not one visual job done five ways. The phone column is worse: px-[15px] at :554 is the bubble's OWN padding inside a list that already insets, and px-[16px] at :593 is the input's own padding inside a form that already insets at 18. The actual edge insets down the 390px column are three - header 20 (:513), message list 18 (:542), composer 18 (:581) - so it is one 2px step, not 'nothing aligns with anything above it'. The ledger claim inverts the system: the band at :617 is px-[20px] and the rows at :318 are px-[24px], but the documented anatomy PRESCRIBES that offset - band 19px 20px, table rows 19px 26px (COACH-REDESIGN-PLAYBOOK.md:134-140, REDESIGN-CANVAS.md:28-31). 20/24 is closer to alignment than the spec's own 20/26. Residue: the 2px header-vs-list step inside the phone.

source: consumer+agent
title: --coach-target is declared, used five times, then hardcoded around at 46/48/56 in the same file
why: coach.css:67 declares --coach-target: 44px and COACH-REDESIGN-PLAYBOOK.md §11 calls it '44px, no exceptions'. meet-your-agent.css reads that token in five rules (:147, :168, :276, :304, :341) and then, in the same file, hardcodes height: 48px (:264 booking action), height: 46px (:288 composer input), height: 46px; min-width: 46px (:295 composer button) and min-height: 48px (:308 embedded action). rehaul/meet-agent.tsx adds h-[46px] (:281), h-[56px] twice (:288, :294) and h-[44px] (:593). The floor is never breached, so this is not an accessibility defect - it is that one screen's pressable controls come in four heights (44, 46, 48, 56) with no rule distinguishing them, in a file that proves it knows the token by using it five times. A composer input at 46px sitting next to a chip at var(--coach-target) 44px is a 2px misalignment nobody chose.
fix: Replace 46px and 48px with var(--coach-target) unless a rule states why the composer and the booking action are taller than every other control; keep 56px only for the primary commit control and name it (--coach-target-primary, mirroring consumer.css:67's --consumer-target-primary, which already solves exactly this).
note: Every citation resolves and the 44px floor is never breached, which the finding concedes. But the claim that distinguishes it from noise - 'no rule distinguishing them' - is false on all three tiers. 48px is argued in writing immediately above the rule the finding cites: meet-your-agent.css:246-250 says the booking confirm 'is the one thing on this panel a coach presses to commit, so it clears the floor by a wide margin rather than by a pixel', and :308's embedded action is the same class of control. 46px is a matched pair, not a stray: globals.css:912-916 makes .composer a flex row of input plus button, and :288/:295 raise both from the console's 42px to 46px together. In the tsx the heights are named constants - QUIET_BUTTON_CLASS h-[46px] (:281), PRIMARY_BUTTON_CLASS and SECONDARY_BUTTON_CLASS h-[56px] (:288, :294), composer input h-[44px] (:593). The '2px misalignment nobody chose' does not exist: chips live in .suggestion-chips (globals.css:853), a separate wrapped row above the composer, so a 44px chip row over a 46px input row is two stacked rows, not two things failing to line up. h-[48px] is also the house control size - 34 uses across the rehaul folder against 11 of h-[44px]. Genuine residue, unnoticed by the audit: --coach-target-primary (60px, coach.css:68) is used exactly once repo-wide (affiliate-money.tsx:324, on a mono readout's min-height) and on no primary button anywhere, while the consumer sheet uses its equivalent correctly twice.
